job_title: Hiring Senior ECommerce Video Editor ( Extra Performance Bonuses!!)
description: About Us We are a DTC eCommerce brand. We run paid social at a serious scale, and our creative is what separates us from everyone else in our space. We are looking for a creative operator who understands *why* ads work, cares about performance, and takes real pride in the quality of their craft. If you are the kind of editor who obsesses over the first three seconds, rewatches your own work to find what is not landing, this position is for you. What This Role Looks Like This is a **full-time, long-term position**. We do not hire editors to cycle through. We hire people we want to grow with, and we protect our best people. **Hours:** 8 hours per day, Monday through Friday **Output expectation:** - 1 video per day if the project is a long-form VSL (up to 5 minutes) - 3 videos per day for short-form ads You will produce Facebook ad creative across multiple formats. You will have a clear brief, organized assets, and a team behind you. What we need from you is execution at the highest level. What You Will Create - Direct-response video ads built to drive purchases - UGC-style ads that feel authentic, not produced - AI spokesperson and presenter videos that look and sound human - AI-generated B-roll that supports the script without looking artificial - Motion-graphics ads with clean visual hierarchy - Hook variations and creative iterations - Testimonial, review-style, and listicle ads - Product demonstrations and comparison ads What We Need From You Direct-Response Editing You understand what makes someone stop scrolling and what makes them buy. You can turn a script and a brief into a complete, conversion-focused ad. You know how to build a hook, carry tension through the video, and close with a call to action that actually converts. UGC Editing You can take raw creator footage and make it feel effortless. You know when to cut, when to leave imperfections in, and how to improve weak delivery without making the creator sound edited. AI Video Production You can use AI tools to generate or enhance spokesperson footage, voice-overs, and B-roll. You know how to catch the glitches, correct unnatural pacing, and produce an end result that does not feel artificial. Motion Graphics and Sound Design You can animate text, benefits, reviews, and offers in ways that aid clarity. You understand audio balancing, music selection, and how sound design affects retention. Organization and Communication You manage your own workload. You know what is due and when. You communicate blockers before they become problems. You submit clean, organized project files every time. Required Experience - Professional video editing experience (senior level) - Direct experience creating Facebook ad creative for ---------- ---------- brands - Experience editing UGC advertisements - Experience producing or enhancing AI video content - Strong motion-graphics skills (not just templates) - Proficiency in at least one professional editing suite: - Adobe Premiere Pro - Adobe After Effects - DaVinci Resolve - Final Cut Pro - Capcut **Preferred tools and platforms:** ( ALL TOOLS PROVIDED ) Kling, HeyGen, ElevenLabs, Gemini, ChatGPT, Google Drive, Slack, Meta Ad Library Compensation Base: $1,500–$2,000 USD per month depending on experience, speed, quality, and communication Performance Bonus: 0.5% of ad spend on your top 5 performing ads each month, paid after the month closes Our top editors earn **$5,000–$7,000 per month** when base and performance bonuses are combined. That ceiling is real. We have editors hitting it. How to Apply **Applications are accepted by email only.** Send your complete application to: **[jessicahiringmanager1@email.com]** Use the subject line: **Senior Video Editor Application – Your Full Name** Everything must be in one email. Applications missing any component below will not be reviewed. Generic, copy-paste, or fully AI-written applications that do not address your specific experience will not be considered. --- ## Application Questions Answer every question directly in the body of your email. **1. Experience** How many years of professional video editing experience do you have? How much of that has been direct-response or DTC eCommerce work specifically? **2. Output and Workload** How many video ads did you edit in the last 90 days? How many brands or clients were you managing at the same time? **3. Tools** List every editing, motion-graphics, AI-video, voice-generation, and image-generation tool you actively use. Which one are you strongest in and why? **4. AI Video** Walk us through your process for producing an AI spokesperson video. How do you make the voice, face, and B-roll look and sound natural? What do you check before you submit? **5. Performance and Judgment** Tell us about a specific ad you edited that performed well or failed. What happened? What do you think caused the result? What did you take away from it? **6. Handling a Weak Brief** What do you do when the brief you receive is incomplete or the assets provided are not strong enough to build a good ad? Walk us through exactly what you do. **7. Communication** Rate your written and spoken English from 1–10 and explain your rating honestly. Are you comfortable communicating via Slack, video calls, and Loom? **8. Availability** What country and time zone are you in? Can you work 9-5 EST? When can you start, and do you have any current commitments we should know about? **9. Compensation and Long-Term Fit** What base monthly rate are you seeking? What would you need to see from us to stay for two or more years? Why do you want to work here specifically? 10- Commitment Do you have any other commitments that you would need to address first? Be honest --- ## Required Work Examples Do not send your full portfolio. Do not link a general Drive folder. Do not send work that is unrelated to this role. Send only the following: - **Two UGC advertisements** - **Two direct-response advertisements** - **One motion-graphics example** - **One AI-assisted video** For each example, clearly explain: - What you personally edited, animated, or created - What AI tools were used and where - What stock footage, templates, or assets came from elsewhere - What, if anything, was completed by another person Applications that send a general portfolio instead of these specific examples will not be reviewed. --- ## Required Loom Video Record a Loom video under five minutes, specifically for this application. Do not send a generic introduction you have recorded for other jobs. In your Loom: - Introduce yourself - Explain why you are applying to this specific brand and role - Walk through the strongest examples you submitted - Explain exactly what you built in each one - Tell us why you believe you are the right person for this position Include the Loom link in the body of your application email. --- Qualified applicants will be contacted by email with next steps.

title: REMOTE SALES CALLER / APPOINTMENT SETTER   Part-Time to Full-Time | Long-Term Position | Night Shift (US Hours)
job_title: REMOTE SALES CALLER / APPOINTMENT SETTER   Part-Time to Full-Time | Long-Term Position | Night Shift (US Hours)
description: Part-Time → Full-Time | Long-Term Position We're StayBooked, a US web design agency that builds websites for local businesses like med spas, dentists, plumbers, tattoo shops, HVAC companies, and more. This is still cold calling. What is different is the list. We put a lot of work into every lead before it ever gets to you. For most businesses we have already built a finished demo website — their name, services, reviews, and booking. You will not get a spreadsheet with a name and a phone number and a “figure it out.” Inside GoHighLevel you get the brief: website, services, reviews, location, contact info, demo status, and the other data we collect so you know who you are calling and why they might be a fit. The better you understand the prospect, the better the conversation. Our job is the information and the tools. Your job is to turn that into conversations, appointments, and sales. Our system also flags when an owner opens their demo. First hour is for those people. You will often be calling someone who looked at the site we built them 20 minutes ago. The rest of the shift is still the job: voicemail, follow-up, and getting the next link opened. We're looking for one person we intend to keep long-term. WHAT YOU'LL DO 1. Call demo viewers first Most days you start with a same-day viewer list. Some days that is a handful of owners. Some days it is closer to 20. Call them within the hour, walk them through the site, handle objections, and either close the deal or book them onto our calendar. 2. Call businesses that haven't opened their demo We have 15,000+ completed demos waiting to be opened. Your goal is simple: get them to open the site while you're on the phone. 3. Call businesses with no website Confirm they don't have a website, get their best contact information, and we'll build their free demo. 4. Follow up Most deals don't close on the first call. A text within 60 seconds of every hang-up, then a cadence in GoHighLevel. Most deals that close do it on touch 3–8. 5. Keep the CRM updated Everything gets logged in GoHighLevel. If it's not in the CRM, it didn't happen. EXPECTATIONS 4 hours/day, Monday–Friday. Approximately 100 dials/day. Initial targets: • 1–2 booked appointments/day • 3–5 appointments/week that actually show • Close qualified prospects yourself whenever possible Shows are more important than dials. WHO WE WANT • 1+ year cold calling US businesses • Appointment setting or closing experience • Excellent spoken English • Hands-on GoHighLevel experience • Comfortable talking to business owners • Comfortable asking for the sale • Reliable internet, quiet workspace, and good headset Hours: 9 AM–1 PM US Pacific Time Approximately 12 AM–4 AM Philippines time (1 AM–5 AM). This is a night shift, so only apply if you're comfortable doing it long-term. PAY 30-Day Paid Trial $450/month base + $50 per closed deal After Trial $800/month base + $50 per closed deal + 5% recurring commission You earn 5% of the monthly payments from clients you personally close, for as long as they remain active. A 299/month client is about **15/month** to you, every month they stay. A book of 50 clients on that plan is about $750/month on top of base and the $50 closes. Long-term performers get raises and more responsibility. HOW TO APPLY Applications missing any of the four items below will not be reviewed. 1. Start your application with: SUNSET 2. Record a 1–2 minute voice memo. Pretend you're calling Maria, who owns a med spa in San Diego. We built her a free demo website and she opened it 20 minutes ago. Call her. Explain why you're calling. She will say she did not ask you to build this. Handle that, sell her on what she's looking at, and ask for the booking. Don't just read a script. We want to hear how you actually sound on the phone. Loom, Vocaroo, Google Drive, etc. are all fine. 3. Tell us in 2–3 sentences what you've done inside GoHighLevel or another CRM. Name the screens. Do not write “I am a fast learner.” 4. Your best week of numbers: dials, connects, appointments set, and closes (or say “no closes, only sets”). One week. Real numbers. We're not looking for 100 people. We're looking for one great salesperson.

title: Sr. Platform Engineer-PH
description: About the Role Pandoblox delivers enterprise-quality data platforms to mid-market companies in weeks, not months — a lean team amplified by AI. We're hiring a Senior Platform Engineer to own the infrastructure the entire client-delivery pipeline runs on, and to evolve it so a small team can stand up and operate many concurrent, fully-isolated client environments without scaling headcount. This is a senior IC role: ~70% hands-on platform/infra/DevOps, 20% architecture & security, 10% reliability. You live in Terraform, GCP IAM, CI/CD, and Cloud Run. The mandate isn't infrastructure for its own sake — it's infrastructure that gets client outcomes shipped faster, safer, and more repeatably. This role goes deep on infrastructure, not up into the app layer. If you'd rather be shipping product features and UI, this is the wrong seat. Responsibilities: In this role you'll get to... - execute and own the following: - IaC (signal-iac)— the Terraform/OpenTofu estate; provision a new client with a one-line flag flip. Every change is a PR with a plan diff; prod applies only through a gated workflow. Build the paved road so the delivery team onboards a client through a safe, gated path, not a ticket to you. - GCP multi-tenancy— a two-tier project model with one isolated project per client; physical, per-project isolation enforced by IAM. - Runtime isolation at scale— the shared services (signal-agents,signal-mcp, Supabase) serve every client at once, so one client's load can never degrade another: per-tenant quotas, fairness, noisy-neighbor protection. - Identity & secrets— the keyless model (Workload Identity Federation, impersonated service accounts). No long-lived keys, no secrets in Git, no path from laptop to prod. - CI/CD— GitHub Actions: build-once-promote, OIDC/keyless auth, trunk-based with environment promotion. - Observability & cost— SLOs, freshness/failure alerting, evidence-first i ---------- response, and per-client cost attribution so margin stays visible as clients stack up. - collaborate with the project team - perform other duties or responsibilities needed by the role Requirements: On day one, we'll expect you to... - have 8+ years of platform / infra / DevOps / SRE, owning cloud architecture end-to-end - have 3-4 years of experience in Terraform / OpenTofu — production modules, multi-env, gated apply - have 3-4 years of GCP experience — IAM & SA design, WIF, Cloud Run, networking, Secret Manager, BigQuery admin - have 3-4 yars of CI/CD experience — GitHub Actions (or equivalent), OIDC/keyless, build-once-promote, trunk-based - have 3-4 years of experience in security & identity judgment — keyless, least-privilege, gated-prod posture you own - These are preferred experiences: Multi-client/consulting delivery pipelines - Supabase/Vercel ops - Cloud Run cold-start & scaling tuning - AI-agent / LLM runtime infra (MCP, model APIs) - AI-augmented engineering workflows This is a remote, work from home job. title: Senior Xero Accountant / Hands-On Bookkeeper – Australian SME
job_title: Senior Xero Accountant / Hands-On Bookkeeper – Australian SME
description: Senior Xero Accountant / Hands-On Operational Bookkeeper Australian Construction and Maintenance Business | Part-Time | Long-Term Build Technics is an established Melbourne commercial building-maintenance and repair business. We are seeking an experienced Philippine-based Xero accountant who will personally own the accuracy and reliability of our Xero file. This is not a tax-specialist role, a supervisory role or a detached management-accountant position. It combines hands-on bookkeeping and reconciliation with practical operational insight. We need someone who can: * keep Xero clean and fully reconciled; * investigate discrepancies and unexplained balances; * notice financial and operational patterns; * connect accounting information with jobs and their actual stage; * identify possible root causes; * explain what matters in clear language; * recommend practical next steps. We do not want elaborate reports filled with financial ratios. We want concise, reliable information that helps us understand what is happening across jobs, cash flow and profitability. ## The role You will initially help clean up and improve our Xero file and then take ongoing responsibility for weekly processing, reconciliations, month-end accounts and operational-finance reporting. You will personally complete the work. This role must not be subcontracted, delegated or passed to another member of a bookkeeping team. ## Hands-on Xero responsibilities You will be responsible for work including: * reviewing and coding transactions; * bank and credit-card reconciliations; * accounts receivable and accounts payable review; * payment and clearing-account reconciliations; * reviewing GST coding and identifying exceptions; * reconciling payroll and superannuation liabilities; * reviewing loans, prepayments, accruals, fixed assets and suspense accounts; * correcting miscodings and investigating unexplained balances; * checking that receipts, invoices and supporting documents are present; * month-end journals and balance-sheet reconciliation; * maintaining clear reconciliation workpapers; * preparing a concise month-end exception list; * working with our current Xero and OFX/payment processes. Our Australian BAS/payroll agent retains responsibility for payroll, superannuation, BAS and specialist GST review. You will provide clean, reconciled information and raise issues requiring their attention. ## Operational and commercial insight Completing the reconciliation is not the end of the job. We expect you to look at what the accounting records are telling us about the business. You should notice: * unusual balances and changing trends; * recurring coding or documentation errors; * completed work that has not been invoiced; * invoices delayed by client approval or portal requirements; * supplier costs paid before corresponding client receipts; * customer deposits received for work not yet completed; * supplier deposits and prepayments relating to unfinished jobs; * jobs accumulating costs without sufficient revenue; * deteriorating margins; * recurring client, supplier or process issues; * clearing or suspense balances that repeatedly return; * financial information that reconciles mathematically but does not make commercial sense. When raising an issue, we would like you to explain: 1. What you noticed. 2. Why it appears unusual or important. 3. The likely cause or possible explanations. 4. The financial or operational effect. 5. What you recommend checking or changing. 6. Who needs to take the next action. You are not expected to have every answer or make decisions outside your authority. However, you should bring considered observations and possible solutions—not simply pass unexplained problems to someone else. ## WIP, larger jobs and cash exposure Most of our work involves relatively straightforward maintenance jobs. We do not require complicated WIP calculations for every small job. For material unfinished jobs—generally jobs above approximately AUD $15,000—we want a simple operational-finance overview showing information such as: * expected job or contract value; * customer deposits invoiced and received; * supplier deposits and costs paid; * approximate stage of completion; * revenue and costs currently appearing in Xero; * remaining supplier commitments; * work completed but not yet invoiced; * estimated amount remaining to invoice; * expected or forecast margin; * current cash exposure. We want someone capable of identifying when revenue, costs, cash and the actual stage of a job are telling different stories. ## Working with the local team You will work with: * the Directors, who make commercial and financial decisions; * our Australian BAS/payroll agent, who handles BAS, payroll, super and specialist treatments; * our local Business Support & Operations Lead, who obtains job-stage information and follows up operational actions; * administrative support staff who can locate receipts, invoices and other documents. Your role is to validate and explain the financial position. The local Business Support & Operations Lead will then investigate operational circumstances, make calls, allocate actions and follow through with clients, suppliers, trades and coordinators. For example, you might report: > “Five jobs have a combined AUD $43,000 pre-funded cash exposure, and three appear substantially complete but have not yet been invoiced.” The local lead then establishes what is preventing invoicing, who owns each action and when it will be resolved. ## Analytical ownership and continuous improvement We value someone who: * investigates rather than merely clears discrepancies; * distinguishes isolated errors from recurring problems; * looks for the process creating the accounting issue; * identifies trends across jobs, clients and reporting periods; * raises issues early; * explains information in plain English; * suggests simple improvements; * follows material issues through until resolved or formally handed over; * is honest about errors, uncertainty and missing information; * takes personal ownership of the quality of the file. A useful observation with a practical recommendation is more valuable to us than a large, polished report. ## Job-management-system experience Experience with job-management or field-service systems is highly regarded—particularly Simpro or AroFlo, as well as ServiceM8, Tradify, Fergus, Ascora, Buildertrend, Procore or similar platforms. We are especially interested in candidates who have used these systems alongside Xero to understand: * job costing; * work in progress; * purchase orders; * supplier costs; * deposits and progress claims; * unbilled work; * invoicing stages; * job profitability. We currently use ServiceM8 and expect our job-management and reporting capability to become more sophisticated over time. Simpro or AroFlo experience would be particularly valuable but is not essential. ## Required experience and qualities We are looking for someone with: * substantial hands-on Xero bookkeeping and accounting experience; * experience working with Australian businesses; * experience inside an Australian accounting/bookkeeping firm or directly within an Australian operating business; * strong month-end and whole-balance-sheet reconciliation capability; * understanding of Australian GST, BAS, payroll and superannuation accounts; * experience with customer deposits, supplier prepayments, accruals and clearing accounts; * confidence investigating unusual balances and coding; * clear written and spoken English; * strong judgement, curiosity and attention to detail; * the ability to work independently and communicate proactively; * a reliable and secure home-office setup; * a genuine interest in a stable, long-term relationship. An accounting degree, CPA qualification and Xero certification are highly regarded. Practical ability, ownership and operational thinking are more important than tax-specialist credentials alone. Experience with construction, trades, maintenance, field services or another job-based business will be highly regarded. ## Hours and rate * Initial clean-up and establishment period: approximately 10–12 hours per week, potentially slightly higher for short periods if agreed. * Likely ongoing requirement: approximately 8–10 hours per week. * Preferred working pattern: blocks on Monday and Tuesday so information is available for our Wednesday team meeting, with a shorter Thursday block if required. * Some regular overlap with Melbourne business hours is required. * Rate: approximately AUD $10–$17 per hour, depending on demonstrated capability and experience. * This is intended to be a stable, ongoing part-time engagement. Please apply only if these hours are genuinely worthwhile for you over the longer term. ## How to apply Start your application with: **BT XERO** Do not send only a generic cover letter. Please answer every question below in numbered order. Specific, factual answers are more useful than polished general statements. 1. How many years have you personally worked with Australian businesses in Xero? 2. Have you worked directly inside an Australian accounting or bookkeeping firm, or inside an Australian operating business? Name the type of organisation and explain the work you personally completed. 3. Describe the balance-sheet accounts you normally reconcile at month end. 4. Briefly explain how you would treat: * a customer commencement deposit for unfinished work; and * a 50% supplier deposit for an unfinished job. Include the broad GST and management-reporting considerations. 5. Give one specific example where you noticed an accounting discrepancy or financial trend that led you to identify a recurring operational or process problem. Explain: * what you noticed; * how you investigated it; * the root cause; * what you recommended; * the result. 6. For a construction and maintenance business, what would you include in a simple monthly operational-finance overview covering larger unfinished jobs, WIP, deposits, unbilled work, cash exposure and likely margin? 7. Have you used Simpro, AroFlo, ServiceM8 or another job-management or field-service platform? State: * the system; * how long you used it; * the business or industry; * exactly what you personally did; * whether you used it for job costing, WIP, purchase orders, supplier costs, deposits, progress claims, invoicing or job-profitability reporting; * how you compared or reconciled its information with Xero. If you have not used one, please simply say so. 8. State your current employment, normal working hours and number of other private clients. Confirm whether outside client work is permitted and whether you are continuing to seek full-time employment. 9. Confirm that you will personally perform and review all Build Technics work and will not subcontract, delegate or share access with another person. 10. Confirm whether you can provide: * 10–12 hours per week initially; * approximately 8–10 hours per week ongoing; * Monday and Tuesday working blocks; * some overlap with Melbourne business hours. 11. State your expected sustainable hourly rate in AUD. 12. Attach your résumé, Xero certification and details of your accounting qualification. Please also confirm whether an Australian manager or client can provide a reference covering your technical work and reliability. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete a standard paid practical assessment using synthetic accounting and job information. We are looking for a hands-on Xero accountant with operational and commercial curiosity—not simply a tax specialist and not a detached management accountant.

description: ON-SITE, EVERY WORKING DAY — Operations / Production Manager, Small Video Editing Team (City Open — Philippines) We are a US-based media company that produces long-form YouTube content at scale. We are opening a small, dedicated editing office in the Philippines and looking for ONE strong manager to run it. City is open. This is primarily a people-and-operations role, with hands-on editing as a backup skill — not a full-time editing job. That covers choosing the building, getting equipment set up, recruiting editors, and onboarding them — not 3 weeks until you personally walk through the door. That said, quality matters more than hitting the number exactly. We would rather have week 4 with three good editors than week 3 with two good ones and one warm body rushed in to hit a deadline. The last two hires especially are judged on fit and quality, not just speed. This is exactly why an existing network of editors in your city is a real advantage — recruiting from a cold start while also setting up an office in 3 weeks is genuinely difficult. WHAT WE NEED - ON-SITE, EVERY WORKING DAY. This is not remote and not hybrid — if you cannot commit to being physically present every working day, please do not apply - An existing network of video editors in your city you can bring in quickly — tell us who, how many, and where - A building in your city that can meet our office spec (see below) — tell us if you already have somewhere in mind - Experience as a team lead, lead editor, or someone who has supervised editors, managed workflow, or done QA/review on a team's output — tell us what that looked like - Basic-to-solid hands-on video editing ability — enough to judge quality and step in when needed. You do NOT need to be a world-class editor or edit every day. Adobe Premiere Pro / After Effects preferred. Tell us what software you use and share a portfolio/reel - Excellent English, written and spoken - Comfortable with project management tools (ClickUp, Trello, Asana or similar) - NBI clearance and at least 2 references we can actually call THE OFFICE SPEC Wherever the office ends up, the building must have: - Security with controlled access - Backup power - Fast, redundant internet - A private, lockable room for the team - 24/7 access - Daily cleaning NICE TO HAVE - Recruiting or hiring experience - Experience with YouTube content - Experience working inside a seat-lease / BPO facility WHAT WE OFFER - PHP 55,000 - 70,000 per month depending on experience - Full-time, long-term, on-site - You build your own team and grow with the office as it expands - Every editor on the team is hired individually and paid individually and directly by us - We are in the process of setting up formal business registration in the Philippines HOW TO APPLY Put the word TEAM at the top of your reply so we know you read this ad. Then send: 1. Your city, and a short note about a team or workflow you led, supervised, or did QA on, and how many people were involved 2. Your CV and a portfolio or reel showing your own long-form YouTube editing work 3. Your answer to this question: how would you recruit 4 good video editors in your city within 3 weeks? 4. Tell us about any editors you already know in your city and could bring in quickly, and whether you have a building in mind that fits our spec Shortlisted candidates will be asked to complete a small paid test/trial task before a final decision. Applications without the word TEAM at the top will not be reviewed.

title: Real Estate Research & Lead Generation
description: # Real Estate Research & Lead Generation Virtual Assistant ## Position Overview We are looking for a sharp, resourceful, and highly motivated **Real Estate Research & Lead Generation Virtual Assistant** to help identify, research, qualify, and organize potential real estate and short-term rental leads. This is **NOT a simple data-entry VA position**. We are looking for someone who can investigate information, connect the dots between multiple sources, think critically, and take ownership of getting to the end result. The ideal candidate is technically comfortable, analytical, fast-moving, organized, and willing to learn new tools and processes. ## Core Responsibilities You will assist with research and lead-generation activities involving real estate properties, Airbnb/VRBO listings, property owners, and potential clients. Responsibilities may include: * Research Airbnb and VRBO listings based on specific criteria. * Analyze listings, reviews, ratings, amenities, booking activity, and other property information. * Identify potentially underperforming short-term rental properties. * Perform **skip tracing** to identify property owners and available contact information. * Research ownership information using public records and real estate databases. * Use Zillow, Redfin, ---------- , county property records, and other listing or property-information services. * Compare property photos, listing information, maps, parcel information, and other available data to help identify properties. * Use **Google Reverse Image Search** and similar tools when appropriate. * Organize research findings in Google Sheets. * Verify information across multiple sources before entering results. * Identify relationships between Airbnb/VRBO listings, property addresses, owners, LLCs, social media profiles, and other available information. * Maintain accurate notes explaining how conclusions were reached. * Assist with building and maintaining prospecting databases. * Perform additional real estate research and lead-generation tasks as the business grows. ## Required Skills ### Research & Analytical Skills You must have: * Strong analytical and investigative skills. * Ability to research information across multiple websites and databases. * Ability to recognize patterns and connect information from different sources. * Strong attention to detail. * Ability to verify information instead of simply accepting the first search result. * Ability to work through incomplete information and determine the next logical research step. We are specifically looking for someone who can **connect the dots and accomplish the goal**, rather than getting stuck whenever the answer is not immediately obvious. ### Technical Skills You should be comfortable working with: * Google Sheets * Google Search * Google Maps * Google Reverse Image Search * Airbnb * VRBO * Zillow * Redfin * ---------- or similar real estate platforms * Public property records * Skip-tracing tools * ChatGPT and other AI tools Advanced Google Sheets knowledge is a plus, including: * Filters * Sorting * Conditional formatting * Data validation * Basic formulas * Removing duplicates * Organizing large datasets Experience with automation tools, scraping tools, CRM systems, AirDNA, PropStream, BatchLeads, Privy, REISift, or similar platforms is a major plus - but NOT required. ## Real Estate Knowledge Previous experience in real estate is strongly preferred. Helpful backgrounds include: * Real estate virtual assistant * Real estate lead generation * Property research * Skip tracing * Short-term rentals * Airbnb/VRBO research * Property management * Real estate investing * Wholesaling * Acquisition research * MLS or property-listing research You do NOT need to know everything on day one. We WILL TRAIN the right candidate. We are willing to train the right person who demonstrates strong intelligence, curiosity, work ethic, and the ability to learn quickly. ## Use of ChatGPT & AI You should already be comfortable using ChatGPT. We expect you to use AI as a productivity and research assistant when appropriate. However, **copying an AI answer without verifying it is NOT acceptable**. The goal is to combine AI, research tools, common sense, and human judgment to produce accurate results efficiently. ## What We Value Most ### Resourcefulness When one method does not work, try another. Do not immediately stop and say: “I couldn't find it.” Instead, think: “What other information do I have, and where else can I look?” ### Speed With Accuracy We do not expect reckless work. We do expect someone who thinks quickly, understands the objective, and keeps moving toward the answer. The ideal person does not need every small step explained before taking action. ### High Sense of Ownership Ownership is extremely important in this role. If you make a mistake: **Own it. Fix it. Learn from it. Don't repeat it. Move on.** We do not expect perfection. We do expect honesty, accountability, and continuous improvement. Do not hide mistakes or blame tools, websites, coworkers, or incomplete instructions. Bring the issue forward and help solve it. ### Leadership Although this position may begin as an individual contributor, we strongly value leadership ability. A strong candidate should eventually be capable of: * Improving processes * Suggesting better research methods * Creating SOPs * Training other VAs * Reviewing another researcher's work * Identifying inefficiencies * Helping build and manage a small research or lead-generation team We are looking for someone who wants to become increasingly valuable to the organization rather than simply complete assigned tasks. ## Ideal Personality You will probably succeed in this position if you are: * Curious * Analytical * Technically comfortable * Highly organized * Persistent * Fast learner * Resourceful * Self-directed * Accountable * Detail-oriented * Comfortable solving problems * Comfortable being challenged * Willing to learn from mistakes * Interested in real estate and technology You should enjoy situations where someone gives you a goal and you figure out **how to get there**. ## This Position Is NOT a Good Fit If You: * Need extremely detailed instructions for every task. * Give up quickly when information is difficult to find. * Primarily want repetitive data-entry work. * Frequently submit incomplete work without explaining what is missing. * Copy information without verifying it. * Are uncomfortable learning new technology. * Avoid responsibility when mistakes occur. * Need constant supervision to remain productive. ## Example Assignment You may be given an assignment such as: “Find Airbnb properties meeting these criteria, identify their likely physical addresses, research the property owners, locate publicly available contact information, and organize everything in a Google Sheet.” You may need to use several different sources to complete the assignment. We care about both the **final answer and the quality of the reasoning used to reach it.** ## Growth Opportunity For the right person, this can grow well beyond a traditional VA position. As our processes and lead-generation operation expand, there may be opportunities to become a: * Senior Research VA * Lead Generation Specialist * Research Team Lead * Operations Coordinator * Real Estate Acquisition Research Manager We want someone who is interested in learning the business and growing with the organization.

job_title: AI Sales System Build (Revenue Command) — n8n + Retell AI + Twilio + CRM Integrations (Multi-Client SaaS)
description: We run a sales and AI systems consultancy in Australia. We've already built and proven an AI sales stack for our own business — conversational SMS agents, AI voice agents, automated pipeline management and a live revenue dashboard. It works. It's producing real bookings and real revenue right now. We're now productising it so we can deploy the same system to other sales-driven businesses: recruitment agencies, real estate agents, business brokers and similar. We need one developer to build the productised, multi-client version. You are not inventing this from scratch — the logic, the sequences, the prompts and the workflows already exist and are running. Your job is to rebuild them properly as a repeatable, multi-tenant system that we can deploy to a new client in under a week instead of three. What you'd be building A four-layer system, deployed per client, managed from one place: 1. Daily briefing engine Automated morning brief and end-of-day close-out delivered to the client (email + SMS + dashboard). Pulls from their CRM and calendar: what's booked today, who went quiet, who's due for follow-up, what moved yesterday, what needs a human. Not a data dump — a prioritised, written brief. 2. Conversational SMS agent Two-way AI SMS that qualifies inbound enquiries, books appointments, chases no-shows, nurtures cold leads and escalates to the human when the conversation needs it. Must handle real replies (not just broadcast), write back to the CRM, respect opt-outs, and know when to stop. 3. AI voice agent Outbound calling of new leads and enquiries using Retell AI over Twilio, with an Australian SIP trunk. Batch campaigns plus real-time speed-to-lead calling. Call outcomes, transcripts and dispositions sync back to the CRM. Books directly into the client's calendar. 4. Client dashboard A web dashboard where the client sees their pipeline, lead flow, agent activity, conversion rates by stage, and ROI (what the system cost vs what it produced). Login per client. This is the thing they open every morning — it needs to be genuinely good, not a wall of numbers. Plus: a provisioning layer so onboarding a new client is configuration, not development. Integrations required CRM: HubSpot and GoHighLevel at minimum. Pipedrive and Salesforce as fast-follows. Must be built behind an abstraction layer — we will add CRMs and we do not want to rewrite the agents each time. Calendar: Google Calendar, cal.com, Calendly Email: Gmail / Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 Telephony: Twilio (Australian AU1 region), Retell AI LLM: your recommendation — we care about cost per conversation, not brand names Tech stack Our current production stack is Make.com + Retell AI + Twilio + HubSpot. For this build we expect to move the automation layer to self-hosted n8n for cost and multi-tenancy reasons — but if you can make a strong case for a different approach, we want to hear it in your proposal. Tell us what you'd actually do and why. For the dashboard, we're open on the stack. Something you can maintain, that we can hire for later. Milestones # Milestone Deliverable Est. hours 1 Foundation Multi-tenant automation infrastructure, client config layer, credential/secrets handling, logging and error alerting. One test client provisioned end to end. ~140 2 Integrations CRM, calendar and email connectors behind a common abstraction. Two-way sync verified against a live sandbox. ~110 3 SMS agent Conversational agent live: inbound reply handling, qualification, booking, escalation, opt-out compliance, full CRM write-back. ~100 4 Voice agent Retell + Twilio AU trunk live. Batch dialler + speed-to-lead trigger. Outcomes, transcripts and recordings synced. Calendar booking from call. ~100 5 Briefing engine Morning brief + daily close-out generating and delivering reliably for the test client. ~55 6 Dashboard Client-facing dashboard, authenticated, live data, ROI reporting. ~150 7 Provisioning + handover New-client setup tooling, templates, documentation, video walkthrough, 30 days of bug support. ~60 ~715 hours core + ~15% QA/revision allowance. Milestones are paid on acceptance. We'd like to start with Milestone 1 as a standalone engagement — if it goes well, the rest follows without re-negotiation. What we need from you Demonstrated production work with AI voice agents — Retell, Vapi, Bland or similar. Not a tutorial project. Something real, with real call volume. Demonstrated n8n or Make.com work at a level beyond simple linear automations — error handling, retries, queues, sub-workflows, multi-tenancy. Twilio experience including SIP trunking and non-US number provisioning. Real CRM API work — HubSpot or GoHighLevel specifically is a big plus. Front-end capability for the dashboard, or a named partner you work with (tell us who, up front). Written English good enough to work asynchronously across a 5–12 hour timezone gap. You test your own work. We are not your QA team. What we don't want Anyone who has only ever built demos Agencies who bid, win, then hand it to a junior — we want to talk to and work with the person doing the build Anyone who needs a spec for every decision. We'll give you the logic and the outcomes; you own the technical calls. Terms All code, workflows and IP assigned to us on payment. NDA before we share our existing prompts, sequences and workflow logic. Weekly 30-minute call at a time that works for both of us, plus async updates. We supply all accounts, API keys and test data. Ongoing retainer available after handover for maintenance and new client onboarding — this is the outcome we're hoping for. Screening questions (put these in the Upwork job form) Link us to an AI voice agent you have built that has handled real calls at volume. What was the call volume, and what was the connect-to-booking rate? We're planning to move from Make.com to self-hosted n8n for multi-tenancy and cost. Do you agree with that call? If not, what would you do instead and why? How would you architect this so that onboarding client #40 takes a few hours of configuration rather than a few days of development? Be specific. What's your realistic all-in cost per connected AI call minute for a call to an Australian mobile, and how would you bring it down? What hours do you work, in UTC? Paid test task (do this before you award the full project)

description: This is a part-time role designed to grow We are looking for someone to take ownership of our content, video and social presence, and to support the marketing systems sitting behind it. It starts at two days a week. For the right person the opportunity is considerably bigger than that — our intention is to grow the role alongside the person: more days, more scope, and in time the paid advertising we currently send outside. That progression is d ---------- by what you produce, not by how long you have been here. What the role actually is The larger part is content — video editing, graphic design and social media management. Turning raw footage shot on a phone on a building site, with no script and no shot list, into short-form video people stop scrolling for. Building the graphics and client-facing material around it, and running the calendar across Instagram, Facebook and ---------- . There is also the chance to work with professionally shot photography and video, and to put your own flair and style through our socials and website. The rest is the machinery behind it — our CRM, our website, our search presence, and the numbers that tell us whether any of it is working. We want both halves in one person. It is a genuinely hard combination to find, which is why we are being specific rather than hoping. The content side - Turning raw site footage into finished Reels — walkthroughs, before-and-afters, progress, behind the scenes, the trades at work - Cutting talking-head video with our director into something watchable - Editing and colour-correcting project photography - Carousels, branded graphics, marketing one-pagers, and the client-facing PDFs and information packs we send through pre-construction - Repurposing long-form material — blogs, videos, site notes — into social-ready pieces - Running and improving our content calendar across Instagram, Facebook and ---------- - Working with our site team to pull out the moments worth filming, and telling them what you need from them - Watching what performs and telling us what you would change - Bringing us ideas we did not ask for The systems side - Working in our CRM — pipelines, opportunities, forms, custom fields - Supporting workflows and automations, email and SMS campaigns - Making sure enquiries are captured properly and followed through - Blog uploads and page updates on our website, with half an eye on how they are structured for search - Tracking what actually produces enquiries, not just impressions We use GoHighLevel. Hands-on GHL experience is a real advantage and we want to hear about it in detail. Comparable CRM experience — HubSpot, ActiveCampaign, Keap, Zoho — plus a genuine ability to learn systems works too. Over time we want to bring more of our paid advertising in-house, so if you understand how ads, search and analytics fit together, that is where this role has the most room to grow How we think about AI We use AI here every day and we expect you to. Being good with it is a skill we value. What we are hiring is your judgement — the pacing of a cut, the hook in the first two seconds, the reason one shot follows another, the voice in a caption. Our homes are custom and our content should feel the same way: recognisably ours. If you can point at a real piece of your own work and tell us exactly where the model helped and where you took over, you are the sort of person we want to talk to. Who this suits You will not be expected to work it all out alone. You will have plenty of support while you learn our business, our brand and the way we work, and we expect questions during onboarding — we collaborate closely as a team. As you settle in we will expect you to take increasing ownership of your work. The people who do well with us bring solutions rather than questions, flag issues early rather than on the deadline, take feedback well and go around again to hit the standard, and genuinely care about what they put their name to. Every so often they send us something nobody asked for that turns out to be exactly what we needed. If you want to be told exactly what to do each morning, this will frustrate you. If you have been looking for somewhere that gives you real ownership and rewards it, this is that. What you need - Around three years of hands-on content creation experience — where video, design and social content have been a meaningful part of your actual role. If you have less but a portfolio that speaks for itself, apply anyway - Strong short-form vertical video editing — building an edit from raw, unsorted footage rather than working from a template - Confidence in CapCut, Premiere Pro, After Effects or DaVinci Resolve — whichever is genuinely yours, and tell us which - Strong Canva skills and the discipline to hold an existing brand kit - Real hands-on confidence inside a CRM, ideally GoHighLevel - Fluency with AI tools, and the judgement to keep the creative decisions your own - Excellent written and spoken English - The ability to work two days a week without being chased, and to say early when something will not be ready Helpful, not essential: construction, architecture or property experience · Google Ads or Meta Ads · SEO fundamentals and Google Analytics · WordPress · Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator or InDesign · LinkedIn content How to apply One honest note first. We know some people will paste this ad into an AI tool and send back whatever comes out. We are not against you using AI to help you write — we use it every day ourselves. But we can tell the difference between an application written with help and one where nobody was really there, and we only want to hear from people who actually want this particular job at this particular company. Two of the things below cannot be produced by a tool. They are the two we read first. 1. Your resume 2. A link to your portfolio. We want to see short-form video you have edited yourself, not only static work 3. One or two sentences on our Instagram — ---------- — go and look at it, then tell us one thing you would change and one thing you would keep. Key Responsibilities: Plan & Specification Review * Review architectural, structural, and applicable civil plans. * Review project specifications and identify requirements affecting the rough carpentry scope. * Interpret plans, details, sections, schedules, and general notes. * Identify discrepancies between architectural and structural drawings. * Identify missing information and items requiring clarification or RFI. * Review addenda, bulletins, RFIs, and revised drawings and determine their impact on the estimate. Quantity Takeoffs * Prepare detailed quantity takeoffs for rough carpentry materials and labor, including: * Dimensional lumber, wall framing, wood stud walls, and interior/exterior framing * Floor and roof framing, roof/floor/wall sheathing, plywood, and OSB * Blocking and backing, miscellaneous wood framing, pressure-treated lumber, sill plates, and ledgers * Posts and beams, glulam beams, LVL, and engineered wood products * Hardware and connectors, including hold-downs, straps, clips, hangers, anchor bolts, and fastening requirements * Trusses, roof/floor truss-related scope, and miscellaneous rough carpentry materials * Clearly identify quantities by building, floor, area, and material type whenever applicable. Labor Estimating * Assist with developing labor quantities based on takeoff information. * Understand the relationship between material quantities and field installation. * Identify conditions that may increase labor requirements. * Consider difficult access, height, phasing, sequencing, and other project conditions that may affect productivity. * Identify prevailing wage or other labor requirements shown in the bid documents. Scope Review * Develop a thorough understanding of the complete rough carpentry scope and identify items that may be missed during a standard material takeoff. * Review scope responsibilities and general contractor requirements. * Account for temporary construction, equipment, hoisting, material handling, cleanup, protection, and layout. * Identify blocking and backing, fire-treated, and pressure-treated lumber requirements. * Review special inspection, engineering, and deferred submittal requirements. * Coordinate rough carpentry scope with structural steel, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and other trades. Estimate Preparation * Organize takeoffs in accordance with company estimating standards. * Enter quantities accurately into company estimating software and templates. * Maintain clear supporting documentation for all quantities. * Clearly document assumptions, exclusions, and clarifications. * Identify potential cost risks before the estimate is finalized. * Compare estimates against historical information when available. * Assist the lead estimator in preparing the final proposal. Quality Control * Perform a complete self-review of the takeoff and verify quantities against plans. * Confirm all buildings and areas have been included. * Review architectural quantities against structural requirements. * Confirm plan revisions and addenda have been incorporated. * Verify that major material quantities are reasonable. * Check for duplicated or missing scope. * Clearly identify questionable conditions rather than making unsupported assumptions. * Maintain organized takeoff files so they can be easily reviewed by another estimator. Required Skills & Qualifications: * Previous experience estimating rough carpentry, wood framing, or wood-frame construction * Strong ability to read and interpret architectural and structural construction documents * Experience performing detailed construction quantity takeoffs * Strong understanding of wood framing systems and construction sequencing * Familiarity with lumber, plywood, OSB, engineered wood products, trusses, hardware, and connectors * Strong mathematical, analytical, organizational, and attention-to-detail skills * Ability to manage multiple estimates and meet assigned deadlines * Strong ability to identify scope gaps, discrepancies, and unusual project conditions * Ability to clearly communicate questions, assumptions, and potential problems * Comfortable working independently while collaborating with a U.S.-based estimating team * Strong written and verbal English communication skills * Bluebeam Revu experience preferred * Experience with On-Screen Takeoff or similar takeoff software preferred * Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and Teams * Experience with construction estimating software and PDF plan/specification management systems is a plus * Willingness to ask questions and seek clarification rather than make unsupported assumptions * Able to work during agreed-upon overlapping hours with the U.S.-based team Note: An NBI or police clearance will be required upon acceptance of the job offer.

title: Bilingual Admin VA (English/Spanish) — Vehicle Rental Company
job_title: Bilingual Admin VA (English/Spanish) — Vehicle Rental Company
description: About us FastLane Hustle Rentals is a vehicle rental company in South Florida. We rent cars on 28-day renewable terms to gig-economy drivers — Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Amazon Flex, Instacart — across three counties. Our customers are working drivers. The car is how they feed their family, so this work is fast, personal, and it matters. We are a small, tight team. There is no call center behind you. Everything runs through one system (GoHighLevel), and everything gets logged. The role in one sentence Every Spanish-speaking lead that comes into FastLane is yours — from the first phone call, through the rental, through every renewal after that. This is not a script-reading appointment-setter job and it is not a back-office data-entry job. You are the entire customer relationship for a whole segment of our business. If you are good at this, you will have your own book of accounts that you personally built. Why Spanish is required A large share of South Florida gig drivers speak Spanish as their first language, and right now those leads do not get the same attention as our English leads. That is the gap you are filling. Our sales script is maintained in Spanish as well as English. You need to sell, calm someone down, and chase a late payment — all in Spanish, on the phone, with a real person. This is not "some Spanish would be nice." Textbook Spanish will not survive the first call. Part 1 — You own the lead Take the inbound call. Leads come in through our system. You call them back fast. Speed is most of the job. Qualify. Is the driver 25 or older, living in our service area, already approved and active on at least one gig app, and looking for a month or more? If they are not yet approved on a platform, they cannot finish — you tag the lead and set a callback instead of running the pitch. Discovery. Which apps they run, how long they have been driving, what they are trying to solve. Present the program. One flat weekly price that includes the car, the coverage, the taxes, unlimited miles, and maintenance. No deposit, no credit check. Quote the car. Off our live availability sheet, built up in a specific order that we will train you on. There is a right way and a wrong way to say the number, and the wrong way loses the deal. Send the exact car. Photos of that specific vehicle on our lot, by text. Everything after this happens in that thread. Collect two things. A photo of their driver's license through our secure link, and proof of their active gig platform. Nothing else on the call. Hand off for screening, then call the customer back the same day with the approval and a pickup time. That callback is the close. If it slips, the lead is gone. Get the paperwork signed and the pickup booked. Part 2 — You keep the customer Once your customer has the keys, they stay yours: Renewals. Every rental renews on a 28-day cycle. Seven days out you call and confirm: extending or returning? Log it the same day. Payments. Verify the weekly payment landed. When one is missed, you contact the customer daily. Unresolved at 72 hours, you escalate to management — you document, you do not decide enforcement. Weekly tolls. Every Monday, pull the prior week's tolls, match each one to the right customer, and invoice it. Problems with the car. Gather the details and dispatch to our Fleet Coordinator. You do not diagnose vehicles. Returns. Coordinate the return and get the car back on the availability board fast. An idle car earns nothing. Notes. Every call, every commitment, every next step goes into the system. Our rule: if it is not logged, it did not happen. Hard rules you will be trained on These are legal and safety boundaries, not preferences. We check them. No money on the phone. Ever. No deposit, no reservation fee, no card number. The first payment happens at pickup, in person. South Florida drivers are primed against rental scams — asking for money on a call kills the deal and reads as fraud. You never give coverage advice. We are not an insurance agency and you are never the agent. If someone asks whether a specific situation is covered, the answer is always "let me confirm that and follow up," then you escalate. Saying the wrong thing here is a legal problem, not a sales problem. You never promise income. Not to a driver, not to a vehicle owner. You never change the price or the terms. Rates come off the sheet. Exceptions require written approval. You never skip a screening step. Every step exists because something went wrong once. When in doubt, escalate. "Let me confirm that for you" is always an acceptable answer here. Requirements Fluent, natural Spanish and English, spoken and written. You will be selling and collecting in both, by phone, every day. Real phone confidence. You will make outbound calls to strangers, present a price, and ask for a commitment. You will also call people about money they owe. If that drains you, this is not your role. Available Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM US Eastern Time. Non-negotiable — it is when our customers and our office are awake. Check what that is in your local time before applying. Reliable phone and internet. Minimum 10 Mbps down / 5 Mbps up, a backup connection, a quiet room, and a quality headset. Background noise on a sales call costs us deals. Organized under load. You will carry dozens of open files at once, each on its own clock, with callbacks that cannot slip. Follows a process exactly. We need someone who works the system, not someone who improvises. Long-term. This is a permanent seat, not a short project. Nice to have (not required) Phone sales, inside sales, retention, collections, or account management experience Experience with GoHighLevel, or any CRM (HubSpot, Zoho, Salesforce) Experience with a US-based company — especially automotive, rental, logistics, or fleet Google Sheets What we offer: $7.00 USD/hour, paid twice monthly on the 1st and 15th Full-time, stable, long-term work with a company that is growing its fleet Paid training, a written script, and SOPs for every step Direct access to the owner — no layers, no bureaucracy Real ownership of a segment of the business, with room to grow into a senior seat as we scale Do not apply if: Your spoken Spanish or English is not genuinely conversational You are uncomfortable selling or asking for a commitment on the phone You cannot commit to US Eastern business hours You are looking for part-time or short-term work, or juggling several other clients FIELD: HOW TO APPLY / APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS I read every application that follows these steps. I delete every one that does not. 1. Put this exact phrase in your subject line: FASTLANE-ES 2. Answer these three questions in your message: What time is 9:00 AM US Eastern in your local time, and can you work through 6:00 PM Eastern every weekday? Tell me about a time you sold something over the phone, or convinced a hesitant customer to commit. What did you say? Where did you learn Spanish, and how often do you currently speak it? 3. Record a voice sample and share the link (Google Drive, Dropbox, or Vocaroo). About two minutes total, unscripted: First 30 seconds, in English: introduce yourself and describe your work setup and internet connection. Next 45 seconds, in Spanish: you are calling a driver named Carlos who asked about renting a car for Uber. Introduce yourself and the company, find out which apps he drives for and how long he has been driving, and ask for the appointment. Last 45 seconds, in Spanish: same Carlos, three weeks later. His weekly payment was due two days ago and has not come through. Be polite, be clear, and get a commitment on when he will pay. The Spanish recordings are the most important part of this application. Please do not use AI voice generation, a word-for-word script read, or a translation tool. I will be able to tell, and it is an automatic no. 4. Attach a screenshot of your internet speed test (speedtest.net). Shortlisted applicants get a short video interview with me directly.

job_title: Full-Time Paid Media Buyer for DTC Ecommerce Brand
description: Full-Time Paid Media Buyer for DTC Ecommerce Brand Summary We are a fast-growing DTC ecommerce brand selling consumer products in the US market, and we are looking for an experienced Paid Media Buyer to join our team full-time. This is not a freelance, part-time, agency, or short-term position. Meta Ads will be your primary responsibility, but we also want someone who is comfortable expanding and testing across TikTok Ads, Pinterest Ads, and AppLovin. You should have hands-on experience managing approximately $1,000 to $5,000+ per day in paid ad spend, preferably for DTC ecommerce brands. We already have an internal team handling video editing, design, landing pages, and operations. Your role is to manage performance, identify winning angles, develop testing strategies, guide the creative team, and scale what works. What You’ll Be Responsible For You will manage our paid advertising campaigns daily, with Meta as the primary channel. You’ll monitor performance and make decisions around budgets, campaign structures, audiences, bidding, placements, creative allocation, and scaling. You’ll also help us launch, test, and scale campaigns across TikTok, Pinterest, and AppLovin, identifying which products, creatives, and angles are best suited to each platform. A major part of this position is creative strategy. You’ll work closely with our internal team to develop new hooks, angles, UGC concepts, ad copy, static ads, video concepts, and creative briefs based on actual performance data. We expect continuous testing. You should be able to look at campaign performance and determine what we should test next rather than simply turning campaigns on and off. You’ll also analyze the customer journey, including advertorials, landing pages, product pages, offers, bundles, upsells, and checkout performance, and recommend improvements that can increase conversion rate and profitability. Who We’re Looking For You should have proven experience personally managing approximately $1,000 to $5,000+ per day in paid advertising spend for DTC or ecommerce brands. Strong hands-on experience with Meta Ads Manager is required. Experience with TikTok Ads, Pinterest Ads, and AppLovin is highly preferred. You do not need to be equally strong across every platform, but you should understand how creative strategy and campaign structure differ between channels. You should understand Pixel, CAPI, attribution, campaign structures, creative testing, retargeting, audience testing, and performance analysis. You should also understand direct-response creative, including hooks, angles, offers, UGC, advertorials, VSLs, landing pages, and conversion funnels. Most importantly, we want someone who can think independently. If CPA suddenly increases, CTR falls, CPM rises, or a winning creative begins to fatigue, we expect you to investigate why and propose what we should test next. What We Offer This is a full-time, long-term position with a growing ecommerce company investing heavily in paid acquisition. You’ll work with an established internal team and have access to significant advertising budgets, existing campaign data, creatives, funnels, and products to test. There is substantial room to grow with the company for someone who consistently produces results. Compensation is negotiable based on experience and track record. Important We are only looking for a full-time individual media buyer. Please do not apply if you are an agency, looking for freelance projects, managing a large portfolio of outside clients, or only available part-time. We want someone who can make this position their primary focus. To Apply Please include: 1. Examples of DTC/ecommerce campaigns you personally managed, including approximate daily spend. 2. Screenshots or case studies showing spend, revenue, ROAS, CPA, or other relevant performance metrics. 3. Your experience with Meta, TikTok, Pinterest, and AppLovin, including approximately how much spend you have personally managed on each. 4. Examples of winning ads, hooks, creative briefs, or testing concepts you developed. 5. Explain how you would approach scaling a Meta campaign from $1,000/day to $5,000+/day while maintaining profitability. 6. Explain how you identify creative fatigue and d ---------- what concepts or angles to test next. 7. Tell us which paid advertising platform you consider your strongest and why. 8. Confirm that you are available for a full-time, long-term position. Please start your application with the words “FULL TIME MEDIA BUYER” so we know you read the entire job description.

description: JOB TITLE: B2B Appointment Setter (Cold Calling) - US Market Company: Pulse Marketing Collective Type: Part-time, 2 to 2.5 hours per day, Monday to Friday Hours: Must work during 9am to 5pm US Eastern. You will be calling business owners to book short introductory meetings with our team. You are NOT selling anything on the phone. Your job is done the moment the meeting is on the calendar. WHAT YOU WILL DO You will be given a clean list of business names and phone numbers, a proven script, and access to every tool you need. From there: - Work the list, get past gatekeepers, and reach the owner or decision maker - Book qualified introductory meetings directly into our calendar - Log every call outcome accurately in the CRM, including who you spoke to and what they said - Send a short confirmation to every booked prospect and follow up to reduce no-shows - Flag bad numbers, wrong contacts, and closed businesses so the list improves over time - Report your numbers at the end of each day (dials, connects, meetings booked) HOW YOU WILL BE MEASURED The daily target is 100 dials, which is 500 per week. But we judge you on MEETINGS BOOKED, not dials. To be direct: if you make 70 dials a day and book 15 meetings a week, that is a better result than 120 dials a day and 5 meetings. We would rather you slow down, get through to the right person, and have a real conversation than rush through a list to hit a number. The dial target is a floor for effort, not the thing you are graded on. What does not work is low dials AND low meetings. If both are down, the role is not working. REQUIREMENTS - Near-native spoken English with a neutral accent and no hesitation. You need to sound like a natural conversation to a US business owner, not like someone reading. This is the single most important requirement for this role. - Ability to go off script. Gatekeepers ask unexpected questions and you must respond naturally in the moment. - Proven track record of B2B cold calling into the US market and booking meetings. Be ready to discuss what industry you called, your connect and booking rates, and what worked. - Comfortable with gatekeepers. Not aggressive, not apologetic. Calm and hard to brush off. - Reliable fiber internet with a backup connection, a quiet home office, and a noise-cancelling headset. No background noise, no call center floor, no family in the room. - Consistent availability during US Eastern business hours. - Coachable. We record and review calls, give direct feedback, and expect you to apply it. NICE TO HAVE - Experience calling owner-operated small businesses rather than enterprise - Familiarity with a CRM and a power dialer - Experience in med spa, aesthetics, healthcare, or professional services HOW TO APPLY 1. Send a short note about your US B2B cold calling background with real numbers. Start your message with the word "MIAMI" so we know you read this post. 2. Attach TWO voice recordings: - Recording 1: You reading a short cold call script, about 60 seconds. We will send the script if you ask, or use one of your own. - Recording 2 (more important): Answer this unscripted in your own words, about 2 minutes. "Tell me about the hardest gatekeeper you ever got past and exactly what you said." No script. No preparation. Just talk. Applications without BOTH recordings will not be reviewed. 3. Shortlisted candidates do a live video call with us. Part interview, part live role play where we play a difficult gatekeeper. 4. Successful candidates start a PAID two-week trial on real dials before anything becomes ongoing. WHAT YOU GET FROM US - A clean, pre-built lead list. You never source your own numbers. - A script that already works, plus objection handling. - All software and phone systems paid for. - Direct feedback on recorded calls so you actually improve. - More hours and higher pay as your booking volume grows.

title: Virtual Cold Caller
description: # EXPERIENCED U.S. REAL ESTATE COLD CALLER / VIRTUAL ASSISTANT — $4.50/HOUR — FULL TIME **PAY:** $4.50 USD/hour **SCHEDULE:** 40 hours/week **POSITION:** Full-time, long-term **LOCATION:** Remote — Philippines **MARKET:** Tampa, Florida / U.S. Eastern Time **INDUSTRY:** U.S. Real Estate Investing / Off-Market Property Acquisition ## ⚠️ PLEASE READ THE ENTIRE POST BEFORE APPLYING I am looking for an **experienced U.S. real estate cold caller** to join my growing real estate investment business. This is NOT a general virtual assistant position. This is NOT a beginner telemarketing position. This is NOT a data-entry job. I am specifically looking for someone who has **previously cold called U.S. homeowners for real estate investors, wholesalers, or real estate companies** and understands how to have a natural conversation with a homeowner, identify motivation, qualify the opportunity, and properly document the lead. If you have NEVER cold called U.S. homeowners before, please do not apply. --- # ABOUT THE BUSINESS We are a U.S.-based real estate investment business focused on finding **off-market properties and motivated property owners**. We contact homeowners directly to determine whether they may be interested in selling their property. When we identify a genuinely motivated seller, the lead is transferred to the acquisitions side of the business for further qualification, negotiation, and potential purchase. Our focus is on: **Finding motivated sellers → qualifying them → following up → creating legitimate acquisition opportunities.** We are NOT interested in misleading homeowners or pressuring people who don't want to sell. --- # YOUR PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY Your #1 job is: ## FIND MOTIVATED SELLERS. You will make outbound calls to property owners in the Tampa, Florida market. You will have conversations with homeowners and determine: * Why they might sell * Whether they actually want to sell * How soon they want to sell * Condition of the property * Whether the property is occupied * Whether it is rented * What repairs may be needed * Their price expectations * Their circumstances * Whether there is a legitimate opportunity for our acquisitions team You are NOT expected to close the purchase yourself. Your job is to identify and qualify the opportunity and get the lead to me quickly. --- # REQUIRED EXPERIENCE ## YOU MUST HAVE: ### 1. Previous U.S. real estate cold-calling experience You MUST have experience calling **U.S. homeowners/property owners**. I strongly prefer candidates who have worked directly with: * Real estate wholesalers * Real estate investors * House flippers * Real estate investment companies * Motivated seller campaigns * Off-market property acquisition * Distressed property campaigns Please explain exactly what you did in your previous position. --- ### 2. Previous high-volume cold-calling experience You should be comfortable making a large number of outbound calls every day. You should NOT be someone who gets discouraged after 20–30 rejections. You will hear: "No." "Not interested." "Take me off your list." "How did you get my number?" "Who are you?" "I already have a realtor." "I don't want to sell." This is normal. You need to remain professional, calm, respectful, and persistent. --- ### 3. Excellent spoken English You must have: * Clear English * Strong pronunciation * Good listening comprehension * Natural conversational ability * Ability to understand American accents * Ability to communicate with older homeowners * Ability to ask follow-up questions naturally I am NOT looking for someone who sounds like they are simply reading a script. --- # REAL ESTATE KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED You should understand the basic concepts of: * Wholesaling * Motivated sellers * Off-market properties * Absentee owners * Vacant properties * Distressed properties * Tired landlords * Probate * Code violations * High-equity properties * ARV * Comps * Repairs * Cash buyers * Assignment contracts * Acquisitions * Dispositions You do NOT need to be an expert at underwriting. However, you need enough real estate knowledge to understand what the acquisitions team is looking for. --- # TYPES OF SELLER LISTS You may be calling property owners from targeted lists such as: * Absentee owners * Vacant properties * High-equity owners * Long-time owners * Tired landlords * Probate-related property owners * Code violation properties * Distressed properties * Tax-delinquent properties * Other motivated-seller lists The goal is NOT to blindly call everyone. The goal is to identify the people who have a legitimate reason to consider selling. --- # WHAT A GOOD CALLER DOES A good caller does NOT sound like this: "Hello sir, are you interested in selling your property? We buy houses cash. Can I make you an offer?" Instead, you should be able to have a natural conversation. For example: "Hi, my name is [FIRST AND LAST NAME], and I'm calling on behalf of [COMPANY NAME]. We're reaching out to property owners in the Tampa area to see if they might be interested in selling their property. I wanted to see if that's something you'd ever consider." If they show interest, you should be able to continue naturally: "What has you thinking about selling?" "How long have you owned the property?" "How is the property currently?" "Is anyone living there?" "What kind of repairs does it need?" "When would you ideally like to sell?" "Have you thought about what you'd like to get for it?" The most important skill is: ## LISTEN. Do not interrogate the homeowner. Do not rush through the script. Do not talk over people. Do not pressure people. --- # HOT LEAD QUALIFICATION A lead becomes important when the seller demonstrates real motivation. Examples: * Wants to sell soon * Inherited property * Moving * Tired landlord * Property is vacant * Major repairs * Financial pressure * Difficult tenants * Doesn't want to deal with the property anymore * Wants to avoid repairs * Wants a simple sale * Other legitimate reason for selling When you find a HOT lead: ## CONTACT ME IMMEDIATELY. Do not let a highly motivated seller sit in the CRM for several hours. --- # FOLLOW-UP IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT Many sellers will NOT be ready to sell during the first conversation. You will be responsible for following up with leads according to the instructions in the CRM. Examples: * "Call me next week." * "Call me next month." * "I'm thinking about selling." * "I need to talk to my family." * "I'm waiting until after the holidays." * "I'm getting the house cleaned out first." These are NOT automatically dead leads. You need to document the conversation and follow up at the appropriate time. --- # CRM RESPONSIBILITIES After every meaningful conversation, you must accurately document: * Seller name * Property address * Phone number * Motivation * Timeline * Property condition * Occupancy * Estimated repairs * Price expectations * Seller comments * Lead temperature * Follow-up date * Call outcome * Any important information Bad notes = bad leads. Good notes = better acquisitions. --- # DAILY PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS This is a full-time position. You will work: ## 40 HOURS PER WEEK Your initial target will be approximately: ## 4,000–5,000 outbound call attempts per week However: **QUALITY > PURE VOLUME.** I do NOT want you rushing through conversations simply to increase your dial count. We will monitor: * Calls made * Conversations * Qualified leads * Hot leads * Follow-ups completed * Appointments/callbacks * Lead quality * CRM accuracy * Attendance * Punctuality --- # WORK SCHEDULE You must be available to work U.S. Eastern Time hours as scheduled. Because you will be calling U.S. homeowners, your calling schedule must follow the approved calling windows for the homeowner's local time. Your schedule will be established before you begin. You must be able to work your scheduled hours consistently. --- # COMPLIANCE IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT We take compliance seriously. Florida also restricts certain automated dialing and recorded-message calls without prior express written consent. Federal telemarketing rules also address Do-Not-Call compliance, calling hours, caller ID, abandoned calls, and robocalls. ### IMPORTANT: If a homeowner says: **"Do not call me again."** You must immediately: 1.
