title: Appointment Setter for Medical Clinics (GHL / Calls)
job_title: Appointment Setter for Medical Clinics (GHL / Calls)
description: We are Novaris Global. We run the marketing for medical clinics. Our ads bring in patient inquiries. Your job is to call those people, talk to them like a human, and get them booked into a consultation with the doctor. This is not cold calling. Every person you call already raised their hand and asked about a treatment. Your job is to reach them fast, answer their questions, handle the hesitation, and lock in the appointment. We are hiring one person, full time, long term. Our current setter is leaving the country and we want her replacement to be better. What you will do every day - Call new leads within 5 minutes of them coming in. Speed is the whole game here. - Follow up by call, SMS, and WhatsApp with anyone who did not pick up, until they answer or clearly say no. - Qualify the patient: what treatment they want, their budget, how soon they want it, whether they are a real fit for the clinic. - Book the consultation into the doctor's calendar and confirm it. - Call the day before every appointment so people actually show up. - Log every call, note, and outcome in GoHighLevel. If it is not in the CRM it did not happen. - Report your numbers daily: leads called, contact rate, appointments booked, shows. Who we are looking for - Female. Our patients are women discussing body, face, and post-surgery concerns. They open up more on the phone with a woman, and our booking rate depends on that. - Excellent spoken English. Clear, warm, neutral accent. You will be speaking with Singaporean patients who expect a professional on the line. - Real appointment setting experience. Not chat support, not general virtual assistant work. You have called leads on the phone and booked them. - Experience in the medical, clinic, aesthetic, dental, or healthcare space. You should already know how to talk about treatments without being pushy, and know why patient privacy matters. - You know how to use GoHighLevel properly. Pipelines, opportunities, SMS, calendars, tags, workflows. Do not apply if you have only watched a tutorial. - Reliable internet, a quiet place to work, and a good headset. No barking dogs, no roosters, no cafe noise. - You take rejection well. Most people will not pick up. You call the next one. Nice to have: - Experience with high ticket appointment setting ($3,000+ treatments or services) - Familiar with Singapore or other Asian markets - Can also handle WhatsApp and Instagram DM conversations - Basic understanding of aesthetic treatments (liposuction, breast surgery, skin, injectables) What you get - Stable full time salary, paid on time, every time - Bonus for every consultation that actually shows up. The better you are, the more you make. - Real training. You get scripts, objection handling, and recorded calls to learn from. - Direct access to me. No middle manager, no agency layers. - Long term. We want someone here for years, not months. HOW TO APPLY (read this carefully, we ignore applications that skip it) Send your application with the subject line: Setter - [Your Name] In the message, answer these four things: How many months or years have you spent calling leads and booking appointments? What industry? Which clinics or medical companies have you worked with, and what were you booking? On your best month, how many appointments did you book and what percentage showed up? What is your internet speed and what is your setup (headset, dialer, location)? Then attach a 2 to 3 minute video of yourself on camera, in English, covering both parts: Part 1 (30 seconds). Introduce yourself. Name, where you are based, and the single best result you have gotten as an appointment setter. Part 2 (90 seconds). Role play a call with me. I am a woman who filled out a form about liposuction three days ago and never answered your calls. I finally pick up. Open the call, handle me, and try to book me into a consultation. Speak the whole thing out loud like it is a real call. Record it on your phone or laptop, face visible, no script being read off screen. Upload to Google Drive, Loom, or YouTube unlisted, and paste the link. Applications without the video will not be read.

title: Retail Program Operations Coordinator
description: About CoTa Global CoTa Global is a U.S.-based consumer products company that develops, sources, distributes, and sells products across major retailers, wholesale customers, e-commerce marketplaces, and specialty retail. We operate a large portfolio of products and believe strongly in process, ownership, accuracy, continuous improvement, and execution. We are looking for an exceptionally organized Retail Program Operations Coordinator to take ownership of recurring retail programs, beginning with one of our major Walmart programs. This is not a traditional administrative-assistant position. We are looking for someone who becomes the owner of the process. The Role Major retail programs operate in recurring rounds. Each new round can involve changes to products, quantities, pricing, store counts, images, descriptions, order information, presentations, internal systems, and supporting documentation. Your responsibility is to ensure that every relevant part of the program remains synchronized. When a new round arrives, you will compare it with the previous round, identify every change, determine what other files or systems are affected, make or coordinate those changes, verify the results, maintain excellent file organization, and close every outstanding issue. Your job is not simply to complete assigned tasks. Your job is to make sure the entire process is complete and correct. Responsibilities You will: Own recurring retail-program rounds from beginning through final archive. Maintain customer-facing product flyers and presentations. Compare new rounds against previous rounds and identify changes. Maintain accurate product, SKU, UPC, pricing, quantity, case-pack, store-count and related information. Update and reconcile order sheets. Update required information in QuickBooks. Maintain program tasks and status in LeanKit/Kanban systems. Maintain product images and supporting files. Maintain clean and consistent folder structures. Maintain clear version control. Archive completed rounds correctly. Ensure the final approved round becomes the correct starting point for the next round. Identify every downstream location affected when information changes. Reconcile information across systems rather than assuming one source is correct. Identify discrepancies and investigate them. Follow up with other team members for missing information. Maintain an exception list until every open issue is resolved. Escalate genuine business decisions without escalating routine problems. Improve the visual quality and organization of flyers and presentations. Use Excel/Google Sheets efficiently. Use AI tools to compare files, identify discrepancies, organize information, improve processes and reduce repetitive work. Create and improve SOPs and checklists. Identify opportunities to automate recurring work. Maintain historical records so previous rounds can be reconstructed when needed. Confirm completion only after all relevant systems and documents have been checked. What Success Looks Like Eventually, management should be able to tell you: “The new Walmart round has arrived.” You should know what happens next. You should be able to return later and say: “Round 24 is complete. All systems and files reconcile. There are two exceptions requiring management decisions.” We should not need to remind you which systems need updating. We should not need to ask whether something was archived. We should not discover discrepancies after you tell us a round is complete. The Person We Want You are unusually detail-oriented. You notice when: Two prices don't match. A SKU is formatted differently. A UPC has the wrong digit. A product image is outdated. A quantity changed unexpectedly. A store count looks unusual. A file is saved in the wrong location. Someone is using an outdated version. A task was updated in one system but not another. You naturally ask: “If this changed, what else does it affect?” You enjoy turning messy recurring processes into clean, reliable systems. You follow open issues until they are actually closed. You are comfortable reminding people when you are waiting for information. You do not consider something finished because “your part” is finished. You care about how information looks as well as whether it is correct. Required Skills Excellent written English Exceptional attention to detail Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills Strong file and document organization Comfortable working with PDFs and product images Ability to compare large amounts of information accurately Strong follow-up and project-tracking habits Ability to work independently Ability to learn new software quickly Comfortable using modern AI tools such as ChatGPT Strong numerical accuracy Strong written communication Experience with QuickBooks, LeanKit/Kanban tools, retail operations, merchandising, sales operations, order management, consumer products, Walmart or other major retailers is valuable but not required. What We Do NOT Want This position is not appropriate for someone who: Waits to be told every next step. Marks tasks complete without checking downstream effects. Assumes information is correct because it appears in a spreadsheet. Is uncomfortable following up repeatedly on missing information. Has weak file-management habits. Frequently makes small data-entry errors. Values speed more than accuracy. Needs constant supervision. Hides mistakes. Treats AI output as automatically correct. HOW TO APPLY: Email me your 1 page max-resume, screenshot of your internet speed test and a short paragraph why you are perfect candidate.

job_title: Part-Time Outbound Caller - B2B Construction (Experienced, Remote)
description: ABOUT HT BLINDS HT Blinds is Vancouver's factory-direct window coverings manufacturer. Our commercial pipeline is built by phone. That is what this role exists to do. THE ROLE You will call construction companies from our list and find the right person. That means navigating past reception, identifying who holds the role we need - project manager, estimator, or whoever handles subtrade procurement - and confirming their name, title, direct line, and email. You will note what you learn about the company's current activity, and you will follow up on the schedule the system gives you. Every call is logged in our CRM the same day, in the structured fields provided. The record is the deliverable. A call that is not logged properly did not happen. WHAT THIS ROLE DOES NOT DO Read this carefully. It is as important as the list above. - You do not quote, price, or discuss cost. Ever. - You do not negotiate, sell, or try to close anything. - If a conversation turns into a live opportunity, you hand it to our sales lead the same morning. You do not carry it forward yourself. Your job is to find the right person and record what you learn. Our team takes it from there. HOURS 8:00 AM - 12:00 PM Pacific Time, Monday to Friday. This window is not flexible. It is when construction project managers are at their desks and before they leave for site. In the Philippines that is 11:00 PM - 3:00 AM your local time. Apply only if you can hold this window consistently, five days a week, without exception. The trial is three weeks at 20 hours per week. Hours increase after that for callers who meet the bar. WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU - Clear, easily understood English on the phone. This is the single biggest requirement. - Gatekeeper navigation. Building quick rapport with a receptionist and getting to the right person is a distinct skill, and it is most of this job. - Confidence with brief, direct conversations. Construction people are busy and blunt. That is normal, not rejection. - Disciplined data entry. Detail-oriented, with real follow-up discipline. - Willingness to learn construction vocabulary - tender, scope letter, bid close. We train this. You have to want to learn it. - Reliable internet, backup power, a quiet room, and a proper headset. - Proven outbound calling, appointment setting, or B2B research experience. This is not an entry-level role. We are hiring experienced callers only. Helpful, not required: any exposure to construction, trades, building supply, or architecture. WHAT WE PROVIDE - A Canadian phone line through our own system, so your calls show a local Vancouver number - CRM access, with everything you need for each call prepared in advance - Scripts for every call type, plus recorded examples - Direct coaching from our sales lead in the first weeks HOW WE MEASURE THE TRIAL Not raw dial counts. We measure: - Contacts confirmed - name, title, direct line, and email verified - Records completed accurately, every field, same day - Follow-ups kept on schedule COMPENSATION $7 to $8 USD per hour depending on experience, paid weekly, plus a per-outcome bonus for each confirmed contact record. HOW TO APPLY Applications missing any of these four items will not be reviewed. 1. Put the word SPECLINE in the first line of your application. 2. Record a voice sample, 60 to 90 seconds. Use this scenario: You are calling a mid-sized general contractor for the first time. A receptionist answers. Your goal is to find out who handles subtrade procurement there and get that person's direct line. Record the opening of that call as you would actually make it. Audio only. Any recorder is fine. Attach the audio file to your application or include a link to it. 3. In two or three sentences, tell us what you would do if the receptionist says: "We don't give out that information." 4. State your local time zone and the exact local hours that 8:00 AM - 12:00 PM Pacific corresponds to for you, and confirm you can work them five days a week. title: Supply Chain Coordinator – Part-Time
description: Supply Chain Coordinator – Part-Time Remote | About 20 hours per week Compensation: $7–$10/hour, depending on experience About Us We’re a small, family-run company that makes wooden maker kits, real tool sets, tool belts, and other hands-on products for kids. We love creating products that get kids away from screens, working with their hands, building something real, and proudly saying, “Look what I made!” Our products are sold on Amazon, Shopify, Etsy, Walmart, and in independent toy, gift, and hardware stores across the country. We’re not a huge company with layers of departments and endless meetings. We have about a dozen products, a small team, and four manufacturing partners in China. Everyone on our team plays an important role, and we’re looking for someone who would genuinely enjoy taking ownership of the supply chain side of our business. About the Role We’re looking for a dependable, organized Supply Chain Coordinator to help manage everything that happens between placing an order with one of our factories and getting that inventory safely into our warehouses. That includes purchase orders, factory communication, production schedules, inspections, freight, customs, product compliance, landed costs, inventory planning, and making sure what we ordered is actually what showed up. In a larger company, several different people might handle these responsibilities. In our company, you’ll have the opportunity to understand the whole process and become the person we rely on to keep it running smoothly. You’ll work directly with the owners, our factories, freight forwarders, testing labs, and warehouses. We’re looking for someone who enjoys being organized, solving problems before they become big problems, and knowing exactly where things stand. What You’ll Be Responsible For Purchasing & Factory Communication Create and issue purchase orders across our four factories Track deposits, balance payments, and payment due dates Communicate regularly with our suppliers through WeChat Keep production moving toward agreed completion dates Follow up when something is falling behind instead of waiting for someone else to notice Coordinate pre-shipment inspections and required product testing Help us track supplier performance, including on-time production, quality issues, and responsiveness Freight, Customs & Compliance Coordinate ocean and air freight with our freight forwarders Track shipments from the factory through arrival at our warehouses Organize shipping and customs documentation Help manage duties, HTS classifications, and import-related records Maintain compliance documentation for our children’s products, including CPCs, CPSC documentation, testing records, and tracking labels Keep an eye on tariff and duty changes and help us understand how they affect our product costs Inventory, Cost & Planning This is an especially important part of the position. We don’t just need someone who can track shipments. We want someone who can help us understand what inventory we need, when we need it, and what it is really costing us. You’ll help: Reconcile incoming shipments against purchase orders, packing lists, and warehouse receipts Investigate and resolve inventory discrepancies Maintain accurate landed costs by product, including factory cost, freight, duties, and other import expenses Track sales velocity, inventory levels, seasonality, and days of stock remaining Build and maintain a rolling inventory forecast Prepare quarterly reorder recommendations for the owners You won’t be making major purchasing decisions alone, but the information you provide will play a big part in the decisions we make. Why This Role Is a Little Different You’ll get to see the whole picture. You won’t spend all day doing one small piece of supply chain work. You’ll be involved from the moment we place a purchase order until the inventory arrives and is reconciled in our warehouse. Your work will actually matter. If you spot a production delay early, catch a receiving discrepancy, improve our landed-cost calculations, or help us order the right amount of inventory for Q4, we’ll see the impact immediately. You’ll help us build better systems. We’ve grown a lot of this process organically over the years, and not everything is documented as well as it should be. Part of your role will be helping us turn what we do into simple, repeatable processes that make the company better. You’ll work directly with the owners. There aren’t five layers of management between you and the person who can make a decision. If you find a problem, have an idea, or need an answer, you can talk directly with us. You’ll have room to make the role your own. We want someone who eventually knows this part of the business better than we do. If you see a better way to track something, organize something, forecast something, or communicate with a supplier, we want to hear it. We Think You’ll Be a Great Fit If You… Have experience coordinating international freight, customs, freight forwarders, brokers, shipping documents, or HTS classifications Have worked directly with overseas manufacturers, ideally factories in China Are comfortable communicating with suppliers through WeChat Can overlap at least part of your working schedule with China business hours Are very comfortable with spreadsheets Enjoy organizing information and keeping detailed records Naturally follow up when something is late, missing, or doesn’t look right Like solving problems and figuring out why the numbers don’t match Are comfortable taking responsibility for an area of the business instead of waiting for someone to tell you every next step You do not need a degree in supply chain or logistics. We care much more about what you’ve actually done, how you think, and whether we can rely on you. Even Better If You Have Experience With… Children’s product compliance, CPSIA, CPC certificates, testing, or tracking labels 3PL warehouse systems and receiving reconciliation Amazon Seller Central, especially inbound inventory and shipment reconciliation Inventory forecasting or reorder-point models Creating SOPs and documenting processes None of these are absolute requirements. If the core of this role sounds very familiar to you, we’d still love to hear from you. What Success Looks Like Within your first year, we’d love to be able to say: Our purchase orders are organized and issued on time We always know the status of every production run and inbound shipment Deposits and supplier payments are tracked correctly Every warehouse receipt is reconciled against what the factory shipped Our landed costs are accurate and current We have a reliable inventory forecast and quarterly ordering process Our compliance documents are organized and easy to find Our supply chain process is clearly documented instead of living in someone’s head Most importantly, we want to reach the point where we can ask, “What’s happening with inventory?” and know that you have the answer — or know exactly where to find it. title: Composer for Original Sonic Identity, YouTube Travel Channel (One Time Buyout)
job_title: Composer for Original Sonic Identity, YouTube Travel Channel (One Time Buyout)
description: Remote | One Time Buyout I am commissioning the sonic identity for my YouTube travel channel. One time project, full buyout, no ongoing commitment on either side. ABOUT THE CHANNEL Travel with Schu is a long form travel documentary channel. Real adventures in places most people never go, the food, the people, the corners off the tourist trail. Recent films shot in Lebanon, China and the United States. WHAT I AM ACTUALLY BUYING Not a song. A sting. Two to four seconds, one memorable phrase, plus longer bed versions cut from the same motif. A jingle between cutscenes works because it is identical every single time, not because the underlying music is good. Repetition is the entire mechanism. This is a brand asset in the same category as a logo, and it will be treated as one. THE REFERENCE The benchmark is Simon Wilson's channel and his "Honey" sting, composed by David Cutter Music. His audience recognises it within about two seconds, and that recognition comes from playing the identical phrase in every single video, not from the music being complicated. That is exactly the effect I want. The difference is that his is a free to use library track anyone can license. Mine needs to be original and owned outright, so it belongs to this channel and no other. Please listen to it before you apply. Match the effect, not the sound. Anything that resembles it directly will be rejected. THE ONE HARD CONSTRAINT It has to work over Mississippi and Bali. Anything locked to one region or one genre breaks the moment the channel leaves that place. This is the first filter I will apply and it eliminates most obvious ideas. DELIVERABLES 2 second stab. Hard transition sting. The workhorse, used between scenes 4 second version. Chapter card and cutscene title. Same motif, resolved ending 15 second bed. Sits under the cold open. Loopable, no hard ending 30 second bed. Optional. Seamless loop for longer setup sections Stems. Drums, melody and bass delivered as separate files so my editor can strip elements down under dialogue Format. WAV, 48kHz, 24 bit, plus MP3 reference copies Motif. Every version derived from one four to six note phrase. Non negotiable THE FIVE DIRECTIONS I AM SEARCHING AGAINST Pitch against one of these, or propose your own if you can justify it against the Mississippi and Bali test. Retro travelogue brass. Muted trumpet, vibraphone, walking bass. Sixties spy lounge, 110 to 130 BPM. Reads instantly as passport and adventure. Risk is tipping into pastiche if the arrangement is busy Whistle and stomp. Handclaps, tambourine, foot stomp, whistled four note hook, 100 to 120 BPM. Whistling is the stickiest thing a human brain retains and it survives phone speakers at low volume. Risk is that it is heavily used in advertising, so it needs a distinctive interval Brass fanfare stab. Single horn hit, one deep drum, short tail, two seconds maximum. The bold option, excellent as a Shorts hook. Risk is reading as sports broadcast or news bumper Warm analog arp. Tape saturated synth arpeggio, four notes, soft attack. Neutral and global, cuts cleanly under a text card without fighting a voiceover. Risk is being genuinely generic I have already ruled out delta blues and resonator slide as the primary. It sounds excellent but it fails the Mississippi and Bali test. CONTRACT TERMS These are not negotiable. Please only apply if you accept all four. Full buyout. Worldwide, perpetual, all media, all platforms, including monetised YouTube and TikTok, sponsored content and paid advertising Written confirmation of no third party samples. Every element original or from a cleared royalty free sample library You must not register the work with Content ID. This is the one that catches people out. Composers routinely register their own catalogue, which then automatically claims videos using music I paid to own. I need this in writing Exclusivity. You cannot resell or relicense the finished sting to anyone else You will be credited by name in the description of every video on the channel and on the channel about page. TIMELINE AND REVISIONS One to two weeks turnaround. One revision round included. Please price accordingly. HOW TO APPLY Do not reply to this post directly. Applications sent any other way will not be reviewed. Fill out the application form here: ---------- For anything else, or if the form does not work for you, email ---------- Please link your portfolio in the form. Original work only, no AI generated tracks.

title: Senior Graphic Designer
description: Senior Graphic Designer Childcare Marketing Group | Remote-First | Full-Time Position Overview We are looking for a Senior Graphic Designer who can turn strategy into visual impact. At Childcare Marketing Group, we help childcare centers and early education businesses attract more families, strengthen their brands, and grow. Our creative work is not decoration — it is a critical part of how our clients communicate, compete, and generate results. As our Senior Graphic Designer, you will take ownership of visual execution across a diverse portfolio of clients. You will work from concept through completion, translating marketing strategies and campaign objectives into creative that is compelling, commercially-minded, and built to perform. This is not a role for someone who simply waits for a brief and follows instructions. We want a designer who can think, challenge, create, refine, and raise the creative standard. Someone who understands that great design combines creativity with strategy, knows how to work at speed without sacrificing quality, and has the confidence to own projects from beginning to end. You will work across multiple projects, brands, and formats while maintaining exceptional attention to detail and consistently delivering work that clients are proud to put their name behind. Compensation Competitive Compensation: Based on experience and level of expertise. Performance Bonuses: Additional earning potential may be available based on performance and company programs. Why You Should Work Here ? Work That Matters: You help transform lives by supporting the marketing of businesses that care for and educate children. Your creative work helps childcare providers connect with more families who need their services. ? Recession-Proof Growth: Childcare is an essential industry, and our clients need effective marketing to continue attracting families, filling places, and growing their businesses. ? Leadership That Has Your Back: You’ll work with a supportive, attentive, and motivated leadership team that wants you to succeed and gives you the support to keep developing. ? An Owner Who Shows Up: Our owner is actively involved in the business and invested in building a high-performing company and team. ? Small-Team Feel: You’ll be part of a collaborative environment where your ideas are visible, your work matters, and you’re treated as a person rather than a headcount. ? Remote-First Flexibility: Work from anywhere with a reliable internet connection while staying closely connected to a collaborative international team. ? Top-of-Market Opportunity: We want exceptional people and believe strong talent should have the opportunity to grow with the company. ? Train to Be the Best: Extensive initial and ongoing training, courses, and professional development designed to help you become exceptionally strong at what you do. ? A Workspace That Feels ---------- Our remote environment is designed to keep the team connected, collaborative, and engaged even when we're working from different parts of the world. ? Quarterly Town Halls: Regular company-wide updates so you understand what is happening across the business and where we are heading. ? The Dream-On Program: Our CEO grants multiple wishes each year pulled directly from team members' dream boards. ? 25 Days Off: A full 25 paid days off per year, because great work requires time to recharge and have a life outside work. ? Paid Days to Give Back: 4 paid days each year to volunteer with a charity of your choice. What Success Looks Like Within your first 90 days, you will understand our creative standards, clients, workflows, and brand requirements and begin taking full ownership of your design projects. Ongoing, you will be measured on: ? Creative Quality: Consistently producing polished, original, high-quality creative that meets or exceeds professional agency standards. ? Creative Ownership: Taking projects from initial concept through final delivery with minimal supervision and strong judgment at every stage. ? Brand Consistency: Ensuring every asset reflects the client's brand, audience, positioning, and campaign objectives. ? Strategic Design: Creating visuals that do more than look good — they communicate clearly, support marketing objectives, and contribute to measurable campaign outcomes. ? Speed & Reliability: Managing multiple projects and deadlines without sacrificing quality or allowing important details to slip through the cracks. ? Attention to Detail: Catching inconsistencies, errors, spacing issues, formatting problems, and other details before work reaches the client. ? Collaboration: Working effectively with marketers, strategists, copywriters, account managers, and other creative team members to produce stronger work. ? Client Impact: Creating work that clients value, approve confidently, and can use effectively across their marketing. A Typical Week Might Include ? Reviewing creative briefs and marketing objectives before translating them into visual concepts. ? Developing concepts, layouts, graphics, advertisements, social media creative, presentations, and other marketing assets. ? Taking a project from rough concept through design, revision, approval, and final delivery. ? Collaborating with Account Managers, Marketing Strategists, copywriters, and other internal specialists. ? Reviewing existing client creative and identifying opportunities to improve visual consistency and effectiveness. ? Managing multiple projects simultaneously while prioritizing deadlines and maintaining quality. ? Presenting creative concepts and explaining the strategic thinking behind your design decisions. ? Responding to feedback, refining creative, and knowing when to push an idea further versus when to move forward. ? Staying current with design trends, creative technology, AI tools, and evolving visual communication practices. Key Competencies ? Creative Thinker: You generate original ideas rather than simply replicating what already exists. ? Exceptional Attention to Detail: You notice the small things that separate good design from outstanding design. ? Strategic Designer: You understand that design needs to serve an audience, communicate a message, and support a business objective. ? High Standards: You hold your own work to a professional standard and are not satisfied with "good enough." ? Excellent Communicator: You can explain creative decisions clearly and confidently to both internal teammates and professional clients. ? Problem Solver: You can work through unclear briefs, creative challenges, competing priorities, and tight deadlines without becoming stuck. ? Adaptable: You can move between different brands, industries, audiences, and creative requirements without losing quality. ? Time Management Master: You know how to manage your workload, prioritize competing deadlines, and deliver consistently. ? Collaborative: You know when to lead creatively, when to listen, and how to make the people around you better. ? Resilient & Self-Confident: You are comfortable receiving feedback, defending a strong creative idea when appropriate, and continually improving your work. This Role Is Not for You If ? You need someone to give you exact instructions for every design decision. ? You are primarily interested in making things look attractive without considering the marketing objective behind them. ? You struggle to manage multiple projects or deadlines simultaneously. ? You take creative feedback personally or resist revisions. ? You regularly miss small details that affect the quality of finished work. ? You are uncomfortable working in a fast-moving agency environment where priorities can change. ? You need constant supervision to stay productive. ? You are not interested in continuing to develop your creative skills and staying current with new design tools and trends. Skills and Experience Required ? 5+ years of professional graphic design experience, with a strong track record of producing commercial, marketing-focused creative in an agency, in-house marketing, advertising, or similarly fast-paced environment. ? A strong portfolio demonstrating high-level commercial and marketing design work across multiple formats and industries. ? Thorough understanding of graphic design principles, including typography, layout, composition, hierarchy, colour, visual storytelling, and brand consistency. ? Demonstrated ability to take a project from concept through final execution. ? Advanced proficiency with Adobe Creative Cloud, particularly Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign. ? Strong understanding of designing for digital marketing, including social media, paid advertising, web, email, and other digital channels. ? Ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously. ? Excellent written and verbal communication skills. ? Strong attention to detail and quality control. ? A reliable remote work setup and ability to work independently. Preferred Skills and Experience ? Previous experience working in a digital marketing or creative agency. ? Experience designing creative specifically for paid advertising and conversion-focused campaigns. ? Experience working across multiple client brands simultaneously. ? Experience with motion graphics, video editing, animation, or other multimedia design. ? Experience with Figma, Canva, or similar collaborative design platforms. ? Familiarity with AI-assisted creative and design tools. ? Experience designing for childcare, education, franchise, healthcare, or other multi-location businesses. ? Experience presenting creative concepts to clients or senior stakeholders. ? Understanding of marketing performance and how creativity can influence engagement, conversion, and acquisition. Work Environment This is a full-time, remote-first position. About Childcare Marketing Group Childcare Marketing Group helps child care centers, day nurseries, and early education businesses attract more families, retain enrollment, and grow with smarter marketing. We are a fast-growing, remote-first marketing company serving clients across the U.S., U.K., and beyond.

topics, visuals, hooks, and creative concepts across multiple marketing channels ### Organization & Brand Quality * Maintain an organized library of brand assets, templates, graphics, videos, and source files * Follow established brand standards while continuously helping improve the quality of our creative * Review your work carefully for spelling, formatting, design issues, accuracy, broken links, and other quality problems before publishing * Keep source files organized so creative can easily be updated and reused ### Collaboration * Work closely with our Paid Growth Specialist to support advertising campaigns with new creative * Work with our future SEO/CRO specialist on content briefs, website improvements, and new content opportunities * Work with our marketing supervisor as description: We run international luxury fashion e-commerce stores (Shopify, selling to Europe, US, and Australia). We need a careful, detail-obsessed VA for a LONG-TERM role. Accuracy matters more than speed — every price you report must be real and verifiable. 2) Shopify product work (occasional): adding/editing products — photos (light background, clean), descriptions, tags, SEO fields, metafields, CSV uploads. We encourage using AI tools (ChatGPT etc.) to work faster — but every fact and price must be verified by you on the actual retailer page. REQUIREMENTS: - Experience with e-commerce product research or competitive pricing (or provable ability to learn it fast) - Shopify admin experience - Meticulous: you keep change logs, double-check your work, and tell us early if something will be late - VPN (or willingness to set one up) to check European/US market prices - Good written English; some working-hours overlap with Hong Kong time - Long-term intent — we are not looking for a 3-month gig PAY: $7–10/hour USD depending on experience (≈ $600–850/month at 20 hrs/week), paid reliably. Hours can grow toward full-time as we add stores. HOW TO APPLY (read carefully — applications that skip this are rejected without being read): Start your application with the single word CROISSANT, then answer these 4 questions. Short, specific answers beat long generic ones. Q1. Name at least 3 websites you would NOT trust when researching competitor prices for new luxury goods, and why. Q2. Mini-task (10–15 min): Find the lowest legitimate price for the "Canada Goose Women's Expedition Parka" — new condition, from the brand or an authorized retailer. Paste: the URL, the price, and one sentence on why you trust that retailer. Q3. Your longest client engagement: how long, what you did, why it ended. Plus: how many hours/week you can commit now, and what times of day you work. Q4. How do you use AI in your work today? And would you trust an AI chatbot's answer about a competitor's current price — why or why not? We reply to shortlisted applicants within 2 weeks. This is a stable, long-term seat for someone who takes pride in being exact.

title: TikTok Shop Short-Form Video Editor – Beauty & Skincare
job_title: TikTok Shop Short-Form Video Editor – Beauty & Skincare
description: I am looking for a creative and reliable short-form video editor to help me produce TikTok Shop affiliate videos in the beauty and skincare niche. I will film and provide all the raw FACELESS product footage. You will NOT be required to film content, appear on camera or create UGC yourself. Your job is to take my raw footage and turn it into engaging, natural-looking short-form product videos that I can finish and post to TikTok Shop in the UK. The videos should feel like natural TikTok creator content — not polished corporate advertisements. What I Will Provide For each product, I will provide a folder of raw vertical footage which may include: Product close-ups Hands holding the product Opening/closing products Pumps and droppers Skincare texture shots Product application POV demonstrations Bathroom/bedroom lifestyle shots Product hero shots Different camera angles B-roll Problem/solution footage where appropriate The content will primarily be faceless. I will also provide basic product information and guidance on the type of videos required. Your Main Responsibility Your most important job is to take a folder of raw footage and turn it into multiple DIFFERENT short-form videos. For example, footage from one skincare product might become: Problem → solution video Product demonstration Curiosity-led video Benefits-focused video Product-focused/conversion video I do NOT want five nearly identical videos with minor changes. You should be able to look at raw footage and identify different ways to tell the product story. What You Will Do You will be responsible for: Reviewing the raw footage Selecting the strongest clips Creating strong opening visual sequences Structuring each video to hold attention Creating natural, fast-moving pacing Cutting unnecessary footage Creating smooth cuts Using zooms/transitions only where appropriate Creating product demonstrations Creating problem → solution sequences Creating different versions from the same raw footage Basic colour/exposure correction where necessary Exporting clean vertical 9:16 videos Making reasonable revisions following feedback Videos will generally be approximately 12–30 seconds, although length may vary depending on the product and concept. You will also normally NOT need to add the final on-screen text unless requested. You are welcome to suggest hooks, text or creative ideas, but I will control the final wording and TikTok sound used. This means your main focus should be: Clip selection + storytelling + pacing + retention + creative editing. Editing Style The videos should feel: Natural Authentic Creator-style Product-focused Fast-moving Scroll-stopping Suitable for TikTok Like genuine iPhone/UGC content I DO NOT want: Corporate-looking advertisements Excessive transitions Heavy effects Over-editing Generic templates used repeatedly AI-looking videos Highly polished commercial-style edits Simple, natural and effective is better. Experience I'm Looking For Experience with the following is preferred: CapCut TikTok TikTok Shop UGC-style editing Short-form product videos Instagram Reels YouTube Shorts Beauty/skincare content Direct-response or performance creative You should understand that the first 1–2 seconds of a short-form video are extremely important. Previous TikTok Shop experience is helpful but is NOT essential if your short-form editing skills are strong. Working Relationship I am looking for someone reliable who I can potentially work with long term. Initially, this will be freelance/part-time work. If we work well together and the content performs, there is potential for regular ongoing work and increased volume. Communication, reliability and willingness to learn are very important to me. Paid Trial Shortlisted applicants will be invited to complete a PAID editing trial. Everyone completing the trial will receive the same raw footage. You will be asked to create: TWO different short-form product videos from the SAME raw footage. The videos should have noticeably different: Opening sequences Clip selection Structure Storytelling approach Pacing where appropriate The purpose is to see how creatively you can use the same footage. The trial videos should be delivered as clean edits without music or final on-screen sales text. Full instructions will be provided. How to Apply Please send: A short introduction about yourself. Your experience editing TikTok, TikTok Shop, UGC, Reels or other short-form videos. Three examples of short-form videos that YOU personally edited. At least one beauty, skincare or product-demo example if available. Your usual turnaround time. Your preferred hourly rate and/or per-video rate. Tell me briefly: What makes the first 2 seconds of a TikTok product video effective? Please start your application with: GLOW EDITOR This confirms that you have read the full job description. I am looking for someone who wants to develop a reliable, long-term working relationship rather than simply complete a one-off editing job.

title: YouTube Virtual Assistant / YouTube Growth Specialist
job_title: YouTube Virtual Assistant / YouTube Growth Specialist
description: # YouTube Virtual Assistant / YouTube Growth Specialist ## About the Channel I'm looking for a reliable, proactive and ambitious **YouTube Virtual Assistant / YouTube Growth Specialist** to help manage and grow my YouTube channel, **Rexy Breaks It Down**. The channel focuses on fascinating topics surrounding wealth, luxury, billionaires, powerful families, secret societies, ultra-rich lifestyles and other high-interest subjects. Our content primarily follows a **"7 Levels" format**, breaking down a topic from the lowest level to the most extreme. I'm looking for someone who doesn't just want to complete tasks, but wants to actively contribute to the growth and success of the channel. --- # The Role This is more than a simple video uploading position. I am looking for someone who can help manage the channel, monitor performance, identify opportunities and actively suggest improvements. You should think like a **YouTube Growth Specialist**. The goal is to find someone who can eventually become an important part of the channel and grow together with the business. --- # Main Responsibilities ## 1. Uploading & Publishing Videos You will be responsible for making sure videos are consistently uploaded and published correctly and on time. The channel currently aims to publish approximately: ### **3 videos per week** Your responsibilities include: * Uploading videos to YouTube * Scheduling videos correctly * Making sure videos are published on time * Uploading the correct thumbnail * Adding titles and descriptions * Optimizing metadata and relevant keywords * Selecting the correct playlists * Adding end screens and cards where appropriate * Checking subtitles or captions when available * Checking monetization and video settings * Performing a final quality check before publishing Reliability is extremely important. Videos should always be uploaded and scheduled correctly. --- # 2. Video Optimization Every video should be properly optimized to give it the best possible chance of performing well. This includes: * Reviewing and optimizing video titles * Reviewing titles for clickability and audience appeal * Optimizing descriptions and metadata * Reviewing thumbnails before publishing * Making sure the title and thumbnail work well together * Identifying opportunities to improve video packaging * Suggesting alternative titles when necessary * Suggesting thumbnail improvements * Optimizing videos after publishing when opportunities are identified I don't want someone who simply uploads the files and moves on. I want someone who actively thinks about: **"How can we give this video the best possible chance to perform?"** --- # 3. Channel Monitoring & Analytics You will regularly monitor the performance of the channel and individual videos. Important metrics include: * CTR (Click-Through Rate) * Impressions * Views * Average view duration * Audience retention * Watch time * Subscriber growth * Traffic sources * Overall video performance You should actively look for patterns and opportunities. For example: * Why is one video performing better than another? * Which titles are generating the highest CTR? * Which thumbnails are working? * Which topics are performing best? * Which videos are underperforming? * Where are viewers dropping off? * What can we improve? You don't need to simply report the numbers. I want you to analyze what is happening and make recommendations. --- # 4. Improving Underperforming Videos Part of your role will be identifying videos that are not performing as well as expected. When appropriate, you should suggest improvements such as: * Better titles * Alternative titles * Thumbnail changes * Improved packaging * Metadata improvements * Other optimization opportunities The goal is to continuously improve the channel rather than simply uploading a video and forgetting about it. --- # 5. Topic Research Topic research will be an important part of your role. You will help research and identify: * New video topics with strong potential * Topics with proven audience demand * Trending topics within our niche * Successful competitor videos * Topics that are currently gaining momentum * Opportunities that fit the Rexy Breaks It Down format I prefer research based on **actual YouTube performance and evidence**, rather than simply brainstorming random ideas. For example: * What similar videos are currently getting views? * What topics have recently performed well? * Which competitors are growing? * Which subjects have proven audience demand? * What titles are working? * Are there successful ideas that can be adapted to our format? You should regularly bring researched topic ideas and opportunities to me. --- # 6. Competitor & Trend Research You will also monitor relevant competitors and trends. This includes: * Following relevant YouTube channels * Monitoring what competitors are uploading * Identifying successful videos and topics * Analyzing titles and thumbnails * Looking for emerging trends * Identifying opportunities before they become oversaturated * Finding successful formats that could inspire new content The goal is not to copy other channels. The goal is to understand what audiences are currently interested in and identify opportunities that make sense for Rexy Breaks It Down. --- # 7. Proactive Channel Growth This is one of the most important parts of the position. I am **not looking for someone who simply waits for instructions**. I want someone who takes initiative. If you notice an opportunity, problem or potential improvement, I want you to bring it to my attention. Ideally, your communication should look something like this: **"I noticed this video is underperforming compared to similar videos. I believe the main reason could be the title and thumbnail. Here are three improvements I recommend."** I want someone who actively: * Looks for opportunities * Analyzes performance * Identifies problems * Suggests solutions * Brings new ideas * Monitors competitors * Researches new opportunities * Helps improve the overall channel strategy Think like a **YouTube Growth Specialist**, not simply an uploader. --- # Working Hours The position will initially start at approximately: ### **5 hours per week** The workload will initially focus on: * Approximately 3 video uploads per week * Upload optimization * Channel monitoring * Basic performance analysis * Improvement suggestions * Topic and competitor research However, the channel is growing and we are planning to expand the content production significantly. Therefore, there is strong potential for the number of hours and responsibilities to increase quickly. The ideal candidate should be interested in a **long-term collaboration** and preferably have the availability to take on additional hours as the channel grows. --- # What I'm Looking For The ideal candidate: * Has experience working with YouTube channels * Understands YouTube Studio and Analytics * Understands CTR and audience retention * Understands what makes titles clickable * Understands thumbnails and video packaging * Has experience with YouTube optimization * Can conduct topic and competitor research * Is proactive and independent * Pays close attention to detail * Is reliable and organized * Can consistently meet deadlines * Communicates clearly in English * Is interested in YouTube growth and content strategy Experience with tools such as the following is a plus: * vidIQ * TubeBuddy * Nexlev * YouTube Analytics * Other YouTube research or optimization tools --- # Long-Term Opportunity This position is intended to become a **long-term collaboration** for the right person. We are currently starting with approximately **5 hours per week**, but the channel is expanding quickly and the workload is expected to increase. The right candidate will have the opportunity to take on more responsibility and potentially become a larger part of the channel's operations. As the channel grows, the role may expand into: * More channel management * More uploads * Advanced analytics * Growth strategy * Topic research * Competitor analysis * Content strategy * Channel optimization I want to find someone who can **grow together with the channel**. --- # When Applying, Please Include Please answer the following: 1. Tell me about your experience managing YouTube channels. 2. Have you worked with channels similar to this before? 3. Please share examples of channels you have worked on, if possible. 4. What experience do you have with YouTube Analytics? 5. How do you analyze CTR and audience retention? 6. What experience do you have with optimizing titles and thumbnails? 7. How do you normally research new YouTube video topics? 8. Which tools do you use for YouTube research and optimization? 9. How would you identify opportunities to grow a YouTube channel? 10. Are you available to take on more hours as the channel grows? 11. What is your hourly rate? ### Important Question: **If you were hired today, what would be the first three things you would analyze or improve on a YouTube channel?** I'm looking forward to finding someone proactive, reliable and ambitious who wants to help grow **Rexy Breaks It Down** into a much larger channel. :::

title: Operations & Bookkeeping Assistant — Long-Term, Part-Time to Full-Time, Growth to Team Lead (US Company)
job_title: Operations & Bookkeeping Assistant — Long-Term, Part-Time to Full-Time, Growth to Team Lead (US Company)
description: Job description (paste below this line) Operations & Bookkeeping Assistant — we're building a team, and you'd be the first hire We run a computer and phone repair company with two retail locations in Michigan, USA, plus a growing managed IT services side of the business. Small team, real customers, real numbers to keep straight. We're hiring our first virtual assistant. Not a temporary one. We're looking for the person who becomes the operational backbone of this business, and who — if it goes the way we intend — is managing a small team of assistants under them within a year or two. If you want a job where you do the same three tasks forever, this isn't it. If you want to be handed more responsibility every quarter and grow into leading people, keep reading. Let's get the AI question out of the way We use AI heavily. Every day. We're going to keep using it, and we'll expect you to use it too — we'll teach you if you're new to it. We are not hiring you to replace you later. That's not the plan and it's not the math. Every process we automate frees you up for higher-value work, and the more we automate, the more work we can take on together. AI makes our small team capable of doing what a much bigger team does. It doesn't make the people unnecessary — it makes them worth more. If you're excited about working alongside AI tools rather than worried about them, you'll fit here. What you'll own, starting out The core of this role is making sure the numbers are right and the money comes in. Monthly true-ups — reconciling what we billed against what we delivered, across both locations, and flagging discrepancies Invoice tracking — making sure every invoice we've issued gets paid, and every invoice we owe gets paid on time Accounts receivable follow-up — professional, persistent follow-up on unpaid balances until they close Inventory report verification — double-checking inventory counts and reports against what the system says, and chasing down the differences General admin — data cleanup, list maintenance, keeping our service catalog and documentation accurate Research projects — supplier sourcing, vendor comparisons, and other work where you go find answers and bring back a recommendation What you'll grow into (in this order) Customer communication — email and SMS follow-up, making sure nothing from a customer goes unanswered, quote follow-ups, review requests. You'll start by drafting for our approval and move to sending on your own as trust builds. Full bookkeeping — categorization, reconciliation, month-end close prep, working directly with our accountant Process ownership — you write the SOPs for everything you learn, and those SOPs become how we train the next person Team lead — hiring, onboarding, and managing additional assistants, with a pay increase to match Step 4 is the actual goal. We're telling you that up front because we want someone who's aiming at it. Who we're looking for Required: Strong with numbers. You should be genuinely comfortable in spreadsheets, reconciling two sources that don't match, and finding out why. Excellent written English. You'll eventually be writing directly to US customers and chasing US businesses for payment. Your writing needs to be clean and professional. 2+ years working with a US-based or Western company Detail-obsessed. This role is fundamentally about catching things other people missed. The instinct to flag a problem rather than quietly work around it Reliable computer, backup internet, backup power, quiet workspace Willing to complete an NBI clearance and reference check before starting Willing to be on camera for video calls Strongly preferred: Bookkeeping, AR/collections, or accounting experience (QuickBooks especially) Experience with inventory or POS systems Experience using AI tools in your actual work — tell us specifically how Retail, repair shop, IT services, or MSP background Not required: a specific degree, or prior "VA" job titles. We care what you can do. The arrangement Start: 20 hours/week, $600/month Schedule: Monday–Friday, 9:00pm–1:00am Manila time (that's 9am–1pm US Eastern, so we overlap for our morning). Flexible on the exact window if you have a strong reason — tell us what works. After 60 days, assuming it's going well: full-time at $1,200–$1,400/month 13th month pay included Annual increases, plus a significant raise when you step into team lead Paid on time, every time, via Wise. We are not going to make you chase us for your own money — that would be a strange way to run a company that's asking you to chase other people for ours. You'll work directly with the owner. No layers, no middle manager, no agency taking a cut of your pay. HOW TO APPLY Applications missing any of these steps get deleted without being read. This is the first test. 1. Start your application with the words "orange slices". 2. Answer these in writing, in your own words. Do not use AI to write your answers — we'll ask you about them live, and it's obvious when the two don't match. Which US or Western company have you worked for, in what role, and for how long? Our system says we sold 42 screen replacements last month. Our inventory report says we used 47 screens. Our purchase records show we bought 40. Walk me through how you'd figure out what's going on. What questions would you ask first? A business customer owes us $1,840, it's 45 days overdue, they've ignored two emails, and they're a repeat customer we want to keep. Write the exact message you'd send next. What's the most useful thing you've ever automated or improved at a job? What was it like before, what did you change, and how did you know it worked? What AI tools have you used, and for what? Be specific. "ChatGPT sometimes" is not an answer. 3. Record a 60–90 second video (phone camera is fine) telling us: why this role interests you, and which part of it you think would be hardest for you. 4. Send a screenshot of your internet speed test, and tell us your backup power situation. We read every complete application and reply to everyone we shortlist.

title: Full-Time Content Operations & Executive Assistant for MacSparky
job_title: Full-Time Content Operations & Executive Assistant for MacSparky

I’m looking for an organized, enthusiastic person who can help keep this work moving and gradually take ownership of the operations surrounding it. I need someone who can handle the many details around the content, publish the rest of the social package, and close the open loops so I can focus on creating useful work. As you learn my preferences and demonstrate good judgment, the role can expand into more scheduling, research, project coordination, and executive-assistant work. Perhaps, most importantly, I’m looking for someone who wants to be a legitimate part of what I’m making here and help me make it better. No Dementors! Responsibilities Content operations: Keep recurring projects organized and moving, with accurate status, complete assets, clear deadlines, and sensible next steps. Social media: Adapt approved videos, blog posts, newsletters, podcasts, and member material into platform-appropriate written posts and simple static graphics. Schedule or publish approved posts, verify the live copy, artwork, tags, and links, and maintain the social calendar. Coordinate finished video Shorts with the existing producer. Creating or editing those Shorts is outside this role. Content publishing: Review drafts for weekly and monthly member updates, correct the writing, verify that nothing is missing, check every link, stage or schedule the finished posts, and inspect the published result. Format and stage approved blog posts and pages when needed. No coding experience is required. Light media production: Perform simple, repeatable audio edits after training, including podcast ad reads and a weekly audio report. Simple video editing may become part of the job later if it proves to be a good fit. Prior editing experience is not required. Project coordination: Gather files, artwork, links, sponsor copy, and other required assets. Prepare complete handoffs for professional editors and follow up on missing pieces. Research and support: Help research content topics, products, services, meetings, and business questions. Bring back a concise recommendation rather than a pile of unfiltered links. Systems: Work from a shared task list, maintain the production calendar, and turn recorded walkthroughs into clear checklists and standard operating procedures. Sounding board: Provide honest feedback on my ideas and point out missing details or avoidable problems. Executive assistance: As trust develops, help with scheduling, travel research, routine correspondence, outside-party follow-up, and other administrative work. How We’ll Work I will teach unfamiliar workflows by recording myself doing the work and explaining my decisions. You will turn those walkthroughs into clear instructions, use them, and improve them as the process becomes familiar. We already use AI for transcription, research, and routine processing. You should be comfortable checking AI output carefully and carrying the work through to completion. The job is finished when the deliverable is correct, organized, published or staged, and verified. description: - Customer Success Manager (Wholesale and B2B) for US Headwear Brand) - About Lift Down Lift Down is a premium headwear brand based in New York City. We make unbranded, better-fitting caps in three real sizes and sell them direct to consumers and to businesses that want custom embroidered caps for their teams, events, and merch. More than 500 companies have ordered from us, including Google, Shopify, The Ritz-Carlton, and Stanford University. Our wholesale side is growing fast. We now handle around 125 wholesale and custom orders every month, and we need someone whose full-time job is making sure those customers feel looked after and come back. ## The role This is a customer relationship role with two halves. 1. Wholesale customer success - Reach out to every new wholesale customer after their order ships to make sure it arrived and they are happy with it - Check in with existing accounts on a regular schedule (30, 60, 90 days and beyond) to see how the caps are being used, whether they need a reorder, and whether anything went wrong that we should fix - Keep our CRM accurate and up to date for every wholesale account, including contact details, order history, notes from each conversation, and next follow-up dates - Spot reorder opportunities (events coming up, new hires, seasonal needs) and bring them to the team - Flag any issue, complaint, or at-risk account to the founders right away - Work closely with the Lift Down team to learn our communication style and upsell tactics, and build a deep understanding of who our clients are and what they need ### 2. Instagram B2B outreach: Many businesses follow our Instagram after seeing one of our B2B ads. They are interested but not ready to order yet, or they mean to come back to our custom cap configurator and forget. Your job is to catch them before they go cold. - Monitor new followers, likes, comments, saves, and DMs every day and identify which ones are business accounts, brands, agencies, or companies - Assess whether an account is a legitimate business worth pursuing (real website, real team, real activity) versus a fake, spam, or irrelevant account - Reach out to qualified accounts by DM or email, introduce Lift Down, and offer a blank sample cap so they can feel the quality - Point them to our self-serve custom cap configurator and help them get started - Log every lead in the CRM with a status and a follow-up date, and follow up on schedule until they order or clearly decline - Report weekly on how many accounts you reached out to, how many replied, how many requested samples, and how many placed an order ## What we are looking for - At least 2 to 3 years of experience in customer success, account management, or B2B sales, ideally for an ecommerce or product brand - Sales experience is important. A big part of this role is turning interested followers into customers and existing customers into repeat customers, so you need to be comfortable asking for the order - Excellent written English. You will be writing to US business owners, marketing managers, and procurement teams every day, and your messages need to read as clear, warm, and professional - Able to write without relying on AI. Our customers should never feel like they are talking to a bot, so you need to be able to write messages in your own voice and style, without running everything through ChatGPT first. AI tools are welcome for working through complex problems or tightening up a sentence now and then, but your English has to be strong enough to stand on its own - Hands-on experience keeping a CRM organized (any CRM is fine as long as you are disciplined about it) - Comfortable doing outreach on Instagram and by email, and comfortable with polite persistence - Good judgment about people. You can tell the difference between a real company and a time-waster, and you know when to push and when to back off - Organized and self-directed. You will own your own follow-up calendar and nobody will chase you on it - A real understanding of how different kinds of businesses work and buy. A 10-person startup, a marketing agency ordering for a client, a hotel, a university, and a Fortune 500 procurement team all have different needs, timelines, and decision makers, and you should be able to adjust how you talk to each one - Comfortable dealing with large companies. Some of our customers are S&P 500 companies, and you need to be able to hold a professional conversation with them without being intimidated or overly casual - Familiarity with Shopify is a plus - Full alignment with the US Eastern schedule. You need to be online and available from at least 8am to 4pm Eastern Time, Monday through Friday ## Who you are - Communication is the most important trait for this role. You write clearly, you listen well, and people enjoy hearing from you - You understand how business relationships actually work. Trust is built over time, not in one message, and a customer who feels remembered is a customer who reorders - Adaptable and a quick learner. We are a fast-growing company and things change often. You pick up new tools and processes quickly and you are not thrown off when priorities shift - Comfortable with ambiguity. You will not always have a script, and you are fine figuring things out and asking good questions ## What you get - A long-term, full-time role with a small team where your work is visible and directly affects the business - Direct access to the founders. No layers of management - A clear playbook for the customer journey, plus the freedom to improve it ## How to apply We would rather read a few strong applications than a hundred generic ones, so please do the following. (1) Put the words CLASSIC CAP at the start of your application subject line so we know you read this far. Then, in your application, answer this question in a few sentences. Do not send a template or a copied cover letter. (1) Tell us about a time you re-engaged a customer or client who had gone quiet. What did you say and what happened? Applications that skip these steps will not be reviewed.
