title: PRACTICE ADMINISTRATION & WORKFLOW COORDINATOR
description: ABOUT US We are a chartered accounting firm in New Zealand. We are a small team looking after several hundred business clients, nearly all of them owner-operated. We run on Xero for accounting, Xero Practice Manager (XPM) for practice management, and FYI Docs for document management. That experience is the first filter for this role. We are looking for someone who has worked inside an accounting firm and used Xero and a practice management system as part of their normal working day, rather than someone who has simply seen them in passing. If that is your background, you should find your feet here quickly. We are not short of systems. We already have workflow templates, checklists, naming conventions and reporting packs. They are written, they work, and the bones of the system are already there. What we do not have is one person who owns the admin engine and makes sure everything actually gets finished. Almost everything here gets prepared and then waits for a human to close the loop: The job with nobody assigned to it. The annual return that is one signature away from being filed. The invoice that never went out after the work was marked complete. The client email that was drafted three days ago but never sent. That is the role. You are the person at the end of those pipes. You keep things moving, follow them through, and make sure the last 10 percent actually gets done. We would rather hire one capable person properly than spread this work across four people who each do a little bit of it. We are a small and friendly team. People help each other here, the work is varied, and you will be trusted with real responsibility early on. WHO YOU WORK WITH You will work closely with our administrator in New Zealand, who handles everything that needs to happen physically at this end. Together, you will build and run the administrative systems the firm needs. They know how the work runs today. You bring the discipline to turn that knowledge into something written down, repeatable and difficult to drop. Expect plenty of back and forth during your first few months while you work out how each process should run, document it properly, and then hand the routine parts to the right person. You will also work directly with our director and our accountants. You can ask any of us anything. THE WORK There are six main areas. You will not be expected to pick them all up at once. In your first month, expect to focus mainly on client take-on, filing and follow-up. The remaining areas will come across as you are ready for them. 1. NEW CLIENT AND ENTITY TAKE-ON Set up new clients and entities in XPM and FYI correctly the first time, including group structures, entity relationships, balance dates, IRD numbers, contact records and job templates. Run the onboarding checklist from beginning to end and hold responsibility for it until every box is closed. Collect and follow up identity and verification documents. You gather and record the information. A New Zealand accountant assesses it. Prepare engagement paperwork from our templates and send it for signature. Request records from the client's previous accountant and follow up until they arrive. 2. COMPANIES OFFICE AND ENTITY ADMINISTRATION New Zealand has a public companies register that every client company needs to keep current. The work is deadline-driven, administrative and important. It is also exactly the sort of work that gets forgotten until something becomes late if nobody owns it. You will handle: Annual returns, run as a monthly cycle so nothing falls past its filing month. Company incorporations, name reservations and the associated paperwork. Trustee company set-ups. Director, shareholder and share allocation changes. Registered office, address for service and address for communication updates. Company name changes and wind-ups. You prepare them, track them, and make sure nothing sits half-finished. Following up directors for the consents and confirmations required for filings. Reconciling our internal entity register against the public register and fixing any gaps. You do not need to have used the New Zealand Companies Office register before. You do need to be the sort of person who can read the rules once, turn them into a process, and then make sure a due date is never missed. 3. JOB AND WORKFLOW ADMINISTRATION XPM is our practice management system. It controls our jobs, due dates, workflows and timesheets. You will: Run a standing weekly exception sweep covering jobs with nobody assigned, jobs sitting in the same state for more than 14 days, anything past its due date, and recurring templates that have stopped assigning correctly. Produce one short action list from that sweep, not a long report. Keep recurring job templates, due dates and job states accurate. Manage annual accounts intake as client documents arrive, renaming and filing them according to our conventions by group, entity, financial year and category. Update production sheets from XPM at the beginning of each week. Maintain client and system data hygiene across XPM, FYI and our other systems. Systems drift over time. Somebody needs to be the person who notices and cares. 4. DOCUMENTS, SIGNING AND CORRESPONDENCE You will: Build and send signature bundles, then follow them up until they come back. Send final accounts and reports with the appropriate covering correspondence and file the completed documents. Draft routine client correspondence in our voice, using templates, for approval before it is sent. Run batch emails where the same communication needs to go to a group of clients. We already have a working process for this. You populate it and run it. Keep the document management system tidy and consistently named. If something is filed properly the first time, nobody should need to go looking for it twice. 5. CHASING AND FOLLOW-UP This is the part that makes everything else work. If something has been asked for and has not been delivered, you own the follow-up until it is resolved or escalated. You will: Maintain one follow-up register covering what we owe clients, what clients owe us, and what members of the team owe each other. Put a date against every item. Follow everything up politely, repeatedly and without needing to be reminded. Follow up our own team for reviews, billing decisions and completed drafts that have not yet been sent. Follow up clients for documents, signatures and consents. Follow up timesheet completion and send a short weekly summary. This is a polite nudge about getting the work done, not a management conversation. 6. BILLING SUPPORT You will: Assemble the monthly work in progress workbook from XPM and follow up managers for their billing decisions. Identify and follow up completed jobs that have not turned into an invoice. Run the first three stages of debtor follow-up from a written script, with a clear escalation point where responsibility passes to somebody else. Keep the monthly billing archive tidy and complete. AND THROUGHOUT: WRITE IT DOWN We are saying this openly because we have been burned by it before. Too much of this work currently lives in people's heads. As you learn each task, you and our New Zealand administrator will document the process together in plain English so the next person does not have to start from nothing. That is part of the role, not an extra task. Building a reliable administrative system around the firm will be one of the things we judge the success of this role on. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR These are genuine requirements rather than a wish list, so it is worth checking them before you apply. You need: At least three years' experience working inside an accounting or bookkeeping firm in practice administration, corporate administration or client onboarding. This is different from a general office administration role. Please tell us the firm, the country, and roughly how many clients it looked after. Hands-on Xero experience at a day-to-day working level. We are not looking for someone who has simply completed a certificate. You should be comfortable opening a messy client file and knowing where to start. Daily experience using Xero Practice Manager (XPM). XPM runs every job, due date, workflow and timesheet in our firm, so genuine XPM experience puts you well ahead of the field. If you have instead used Karbon, WorkflowMax or a close equivalent properly, tell us what you used and for how long. We are not in a position to teach practice management from scratch. Daily experience using a document management system. We use FYI Docs, but a comparable system counts if you genuinely used it as part of your normal working day. Experience running deadline-driven work, in any country, where being late has a consequence. Confidence working with spreadsheets. You do not need to build financial models, but you should be able to build and maintain a useful working register. Excellent written English. You will be drafting emails that clients read and that go out under our names. Discretion. You will handle client identity documents and financial information every day. This is a condition of the role, not a preference. Reliable internet and a quiet home office. NICE TO HAVE, BUT NOT REQUIRED Experience working for an Australian or New Zealand accounting firm. Exposure to New Zealand GST or payroll. Experience with a public companies register, trusts, client take-on or verification requirements. Bookkeeping or billing administration experience. Experience documenting a procedure for work that was originally handed to you informally. WHAT ACTUALLY MATTERS TO US You do not miss a fixed date. Several parts of this role have deadlines set by law and they do not move. You raise your hand when something looks wrong instead of processing it anyway. You are comfortable chasing people politely and repeatedly, including people more senior than you. You can hold a long list without dropping the quiet items on it. You finish things. The reason this role exists is that too much work currently gets to 90 percent and stops. You enjoy building a system, not just working inside one. If you can see a better way to run something, we want to hear it. You are happy owning careful, unglamorous work and being the person trusted with it. HOURS The role requires availability from 5:00am to 2:00pm Manila time, Monday to Friday, with a one-hour break. These hours provide strong overlap with the New Zealand working day throughout the year. We know that is an early start. We are stating it up front because the point of this role is to work alongside our New Zealand team during our normal working day. If those hours do not fit around your life, we completely understand, and we would rather you knew before you applied. PAY You will be paid an agreed hourly rate for hours worked. Payment will be made in New Zealand dollars, twice monthly. This is intended to be a long-term position. YOUR FIRST MONTH By the end of your first month, we would expect you to be: Running new client set-ups on your own. Holding the follow-up register. Writing up your first few procedures in your own words. The Companies Office cycle and billing work will come across to you when you are ready for them, rather than according to an arbitrary schedule. HOW TO APPLY We read every application properly, so a few specific sentences will do far more for you than a long generic cover letter. Start your message with the word REGISTER so we know you read to the end. Then answer these four questions. Short answers are fine. Which accounting firms have you worked for? For each one, tell us the country, roughly how many clients it had, and exactly which accounting, practice management and document systems you personally used. You are given a list of 40 overdue things across six different people. What do you do first, and what do you send us at the end of the day? You have asked a client for the same document three times and heard nothing. What do you do next? What is your current work schedule, and are you genuinely able to start at 5:00am Manila time? Attach your CV. If you have Xero certification, tell us which certification you hold and when you completed it.

title: Client Relations and Separations - EWS Supervisor
job_title: Client Relations and Separations - EWS Supervisor
description: EWS SUPERVISOR Early Warning System, Risk Management, Coaching & Retention JOB SUMMARY The EWS Supervisor oversees the Early Warning System (EWS) and is responsible for reviewing, mitigating, and resolving identified VA risks that may lead to performance issues, client dissatisfaction, termination, or separation. CSMs are responsible for identifying and risk-tagging Yellow and Red cases, conducting the initial check-in, and implementing the first-level intervention. The EWS Supervisor provides the next level of support by reviewing flagged cases and intervening when risks are unresolved, escalating, recurring, or require additional management support. The EWS Supervisor assesses the situation, meets with the CSM and/or VA as needed, provides coaching, conducts Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and develops an appropriate mitigation plan. Based on the findings and progress, the EWS Supervisor may recommend resolution, continued monitoring, a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP), or VA replacement. The primary objective of the role is to reduce avoidable VA terminations and separations by addressing risks early, identifying root causes, and driving effective corrective action. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES EWS & Risk Management ● Review Yellow and Red VA risk flags identified by CSMs. ● Prioritize unresolved, escalating, or high-risk cases. ● Assess whether additional EWS intervention is required. ● Monitor cases through resolution, escalation, or replacement. Risk Intervention ● Meet with CSMs and/or VAs when additional intervention is required. ● Identify the underlying cause of the issue through assessment and RCA. ● Determine whether the issue is related to performance, capability, training, behavior, client expectations, CSM execution, role alignment, or process. ● Develop and monitor the virtual assistant progress. ● Recommend the appropriate outcome based on documented findings: resolve, PIP, or replace. Coaching & Performance Management ● Coach CSMs on risk management, difficult conversations, corrective action, and retention strategies. ● Provide direct VA coaching when appropriate. ● Develop or support PIPs for documented performance concerns. ● Monitor improvement and escalate cases when corrective action is unsuccessful. Incubation & Preventive Risk Management ● Provide heightened oversight of qualifying VA risks during the 0–30 day Incubation period. ● Support the 1st Week EWS intervention process for qualifying cases. ● Support preventive coaching and risk reviews for VAs within the 31–180 day period. Reporting & Process Improvement ● Track EWS outcomes, intervention effectiveness, and separation trends and Analysis. ● Identify recurring risk drivers and recommend improvements to Client Success and Manager of Client Relations and Separations KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS ● Reduction in preventable VA terminations and separations of at least 15% monthly. ● Reduction in unresolved Yellow and Red cases. ● EWS intervention and resolution rate. ● 1st week resolution of high risk drivers for VAs on 0-30 days tenure ● Timely completion of required EWS interventions. ● Improvement in CSM risk-management and intervention effectiveness. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS ● Experience in coaching, performance management, and people development. ● Experience conducting Root Cause Analysis (RCA). ● Experience developing or managing Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs). ● Strong analytical, organizational, and case-management skills. ● Excellent written and verbal communication. ● Strong judgment and ability to make objective, evidence-based recommendations. ● Ability to manage sensitive performance and client matters professionally. ● Experience in legal services, legal staffing, law firm environments. ● Experience with escalation, retention, or separation-prevention programs. OVERALL OBJECTIVE The EWS Supervisor's primary objective is to mitigate identified VA risks before they become terminations or separations by providing timely intervention, effective coaching, root cause analysis, and measurable corrective action. The CSM identifies the risk. The EWS Supervisor provides support to resolve it. *** PS: Payrate Range is not negotiable so if you are expecting a higher Hourly rate please do not apply *** *** We use Hubstaff as productivity and screen monitoring systems, please do not apply if you are not comfortable with this***

title: Full-Time AI Static Ad Creator / Performance Creative Strategist
job_title: Full-Time AI Static Ad Creator / Performance Creative Strategist
description: We’re looking for a full-time AI Static Ad Creator / Performance Creative Strategist who understands that high-performing creative starts with research, positioning, and strategy — not random design ideas. This is not a traditional graphic design role, and it is not a position for someone who simply knows how to use Canva or AI image generators. You will be responsible for researching markets, identifying opportunities, developing structured advertising concepts, producing static ads, analyzing performance, and iterating based on actual data. Every Ad Batch Must Have a Strategy We do not create random batches of ads and hope something works. Every batch should be developed around a specific hypothesis and clearly defined variables, including: Target customer avatar Market awareness level Market sophistication level Specific problem or issue Core customer desire Advertising angle Hook Unique mechanism or differentiator Customer objections Previous solutions they may have tried Emotional drivers Proof architecture Competitive positioning The specific variable being tested You should be able to clearly explain why an ad exists before you create it. For example, instead of thinking: "Let's make 10 new ads for this product." We expect thinking closer to: "This batch targets a solution-aware customer who has already tried multiple alternatives without getting the result they want. The market is highly sophisticated, so simply promising the end benefit is unlikely to be enough. We need to differentiate through mechanism, create contrast against existing solutions, address skepticism with proof, and test whether a problem-led or outcome-led hook creates stronger engagement." That is the level of strategic thinking we expect. Your Responsibilities You will be responsible for: Conducting deep customer and competitor research Identifying specific customer avatars Determining market awareness levels Evaluating market sophistication Finding customer pain points, desires, objections, frustrations, and language Developing research-driven advertising angles Turning those angles into static ad concepts Creating high-performing Facebook and Instagram static ads Using AI tools to generate realistic people, environments, product scenes, UGC-style imagery, and other supporting assets Creating native-style ads that blend naturally into social feeds Producing testimonial, advertorial, comparison, problem/solution, authority, editorial, before/after, product-focused, and other direct-response formats Developing multiple executions of proven angles rather than constantly abandoning winning concepts Reviewing creative performance and determining what should be tested next Iterating winning advertisements through new hooks, visuals, avatars, headlines, proof devices, formats, and executions Clearly organizing creative tests so we know what variable each advertisement is testing PERFORMANCE EXPERIENCE IS REQUIRED Do not apply unless you can provide actual proof of advertising performance from previous accounts. We are looking for people who have personally created direct-response advertisements that have scaled profitably. At minimum, you must be able to show us an advertisement or creative concept you personally worked on that achieved: $10,000+ in ad spend at a 2.0+ ROAS. You must provide actual evidence from previous advertising accounts showing: The advertisement or creative Ad spend ROAS Revenue/purchase performance Relevant date range We may ask additional questions to verify your involvement in the creative. Any application submitted without proof of $10,000+ spend at 2.0+ ROAS will NOT be considered. A design portfolio alone is not enough. We are hiring based on the ability to create advertising that performs, not simply advertising that looks good. Research Is a Major Part of This Position Before developing creative, you should be comfortable researching through sources such as: Meta Ad Library Competitor websites Competitor landing pages Amazon and customer reviews Reddit Forums Social media comments Customer feedback Existing winning advertisements Advertorials Surveys Product reviews Internal creative-performance data You should be able to convert research into clear advertising hypotheses and testable creative concepts. AI & Creative Tools You should be highly comfortable using modern AI creative tools. Experience with tools such as: ChatGPT Midjourney Gemini / Nano Banana Higgsfield Sora Flux Photoshop Canva Other AI image-generation and editing platforms is highly valuable. We care less about the specific software you use and more about the quality of the finished advertisement. You should be capable of generating highly realistic images and then refining them so they do not immediately look AI-generated. AI is a tool used to execute the strategy. AI itself is not the strategy. What We're Looking For You should have: Proven direct-response advertising experience Proven Meta creative experience Strong understanding of customer avatars Strong understanding of market awareness Strong understanding of market sophistication Strong direct-response copy instincts Ability to develop compelling hooks and angles Excellent visual judgment Strong AI image-generation skills Ability to make AI imagery believable and realistic Strong research abilities Strong understanding of creative testing Ability to analyze advertising performance Ability to determine why an ad won or lost Ability to systematically iterate winners Strong attention to detail Fast turnaround times Reliable communication Ability to take feedback and implement it correctly Ability to work independently Experience working with DTC/e-commerce brands spending significant amounts on Meta advertising is strongly preferred. The Mindset We're Looking For Before creating an advertisement, you should naturally be asking: Who exactly are we targeting? What does this person already know about their problem? What solutions have they already seen or tried? What awareness level are they at? How sophisticated is this market? What specific issue are we addressing? What is the deeper desire behind solving it? What angle are we testing? What does the customer need to believe before purchasing? What proof will make the message credible? What variable are we testing against the previous batch? What did the last round of ads teach us? Not: "What cool AI image can I make today?" Position Full-Time / Long-Term We are looking for someone who can become a long-term member of our creative team. We continuously produce and test new advertisements, concepts, iterations, avatars, hooks, and angles. There is significant room to grow for someone who consistently contributes winning ideas and creatives. How To Apply Your application MUST include: Your portfolio Examples of static advertisements you personally created Screenshots proving at least one creative or concept you worked on generated $10,000+ in spend at a 2.0+ ROAS An explanation of exactly what YOU contributed to that winning advertisement A brief explanation of your research process before developing a new batch of creatives The AI and design tools you currently use Your availability Your expected monthly salary Any DTC/e-commerce industries you have previously worked in Applications without actual performance proof will not be reviewed. Shortlisted applicants may be invited to complete a paid trial where we provide the necessary product information, research, and performance data and ask you to develop a research-driven creative batch.

Develop distinct: Audiences Messages Offers Creative briefs Landing pages Retargeting Follow-up 3. CUSTOMER PERSONAS & BUYING INTENT Understand: Who buys Why they buy What problem they're solving How quickly they need it What prevents them from buying What competitors they're considering What matters most: price, speed, quality, convenience, service or customization How often they reorder What else they may purchase Turn customer knowledge into marketing strategy. 4. META ADVERTISING You must be highly experienced with: Meta Business Manager Meta Ads Manager Facebook Ads Instagram Ads Meta Pixel Events Manager Conversion API concepts Custom audiences Customer lists Website audiences Engagement audiences Video audiences Prospecting Retargeting Catalog ads where appropriate Advantage+ tools where appropriate Lookalike/similar audience strategies where available You should know how to build campaigns from scratch and improve them over time. 5. TIKTOK MARKETING & ADVERTISING Understand both organic TikTok behavior and TikTok Ads Manager. Know how to: Identify TikTok-native creative Select objectives Build campaigns Develop audiences Retarget Test creative Read performance Use Pixel/Events data Scale winners Kill poor performers Work closely with the Creative Lead to produce platform-native assets. 6. YOUTUBE Develop opportunities through: YouTube content YouTube Shorts Video advertising Retargeting Product demonstrations Educational content Customer-intent content Determine which videos are brand-building and which are direct-response assets. 7. PINTEREST Evaluate and utilize Pinterest when appropriate for visually driven products including: Apparel Signs Design inspiration Events Weddings Business branding Promotional materials Understand the difference between Pinterest content strategy and paid Pinterest acquisition. 8. LINKEDIN / B2B DIGITAL MARKETING Develop B2B opportunities where economically justified. Potential audiences include: Companies Marketing managers Restaurants Franchises Schools Organizations Event companies Contractors Procurement teams Determine when LinkedIn advertising makes financial sense and when organic outreach/content is more appropriate. 9. PAID SOCIAL MEDIA STRATEGY Own: Campaign architecture Audiences Objectives Budgets Placements Bidding/optimization strategy Prospecting Retargeting Testing Scaling Exclusions Frequency Creative rotation Campaign analysis The Creative Lead makes the creative. You make sure the right creative reaches the right person. 10. CREATIVE BRIEFING You must understand creative even though you are not our primary creative producer. Example: Instead of telling the Creative Lead: "Make me five Facebook ads." You should be capable of saying: "We're targeting youth baseball-team managers. Price is not their biggest problem—ordering 15 different names and numbers correctly is. I want three 15-second videos built around simplifying team ordering. Give me one testimonial angle, one problem/solution angle and one demonstration." THAT is marketing. You provide the business/customer insight. The Creative Lead turns it into excellent creative. 11. CREATIVE PERFORMANCE FEEDBACK You will provide the Creative Lead with data. Example: Creative A: High hook rate, low CTR. Creative B: Lower watch time but excellent purchase rate. Creative C: Strong CTR but terrible conversion rate. Creative D: Excellent ROAS but beginning to fatigue. Your job is to interpret those results and request the next round of creative intelligently. 12. RETARGETING SYSTEMS Build sophisticated retargeting journeys. Examples: Website visitor Viewed shirt page. > Shirt benefit advertisement. Repeat visit Still did not buy. > Testimonial/social-proof advertisement. Added to cart Didn't purchase. > Cart-recovery advertising + email/SMS. Purchased Remove from new-customer acquisition advertising. > Cross-sell. 60/90/180 days later > Reorder/win-back campaign where appropriate. Different behavior should trigger different marketing. 13. FIRST-PARTY CUSTOMER DATA Develop strategies around properly obtained customer data. Segment by: Product purchased Purchase date Frequency Order value Customer type Geographic area Lifetime value Engagement Lead vs. customer Lapsed customer Use appropriately on supported platforms for: Customer Match Custom audiences Exclusions Retention Reorders Cross-selling Prospecting/modelled audiences where supported Follow applicable privacy and platform requirements. 14. EMAIL MARKETING Own email strategy and deployment. Build automated flows such as: Welcome New subscriber> introduction > value > proof > offer. Abandoned Cart Cart > reminder > benefits > proof > incentive if justified. Browse Abandonment Visited repeatedly > relevant product reminder. Post Purchase Confirmation > education > review > cross-sell. Reorder Expected replenishment/reorder timeframe > reminder. Win Back Customer hasn't purchased recently > targeted return campaign. VIP High-value customer > special treatment/offers. 15. SMS MARKETING Build compliant SMS programs for: Abandoned carts Promotions Limited-time offers Reorders Product launches VIP customers Customer lifecycle campaigns Avoid destroying customer trust through excessive messaging. 16. CROSS-SELLING & UPSELLING Customers buying one product may need another. Examples: Business cards > flyers. Yard signs > banners. Custom shirts > signs. Event printing > apparel. Restaurant menus > uniforms/signage. Develop data-driven cross-sell and upsell campaigns. 17. CUSTOMER LIFETIME VALUE You must think beyond the first transaction. Understand: CAC First-order value Average order value Purchase frequency Repeat purchase rate Customer lifetime value Gross margin where provided Payback period Sometimes spending $100 to acquire a $75 first order can make sense. Sometimes spending $20 to acquire a $75 order is terrible. The answer depends on margin, repeat purchases and lifetime value. Think like a business owner. 18. FUNNEL DEVELOPMENT Create complete funnels. Examples: Social Ad > Landing Page > Purchase or: Video > Lead Form > Email/SMS > Quote ? Sale or: Educational Content > Retargeting > Product Page > Purchase or: Customer List > Reorder Offer > Purchase Every campaign should have an intentional next step. 19. LANDING-PAGE STRATEGY You do not need to code the pages. You DO need to understand what makes them convert. Recommend: Headlines Offers Layout Social proof Videos Reviews Calls to action Forms Product presentation FAQs Urgency Guarantees Mobile improvements Work with our SEO/web team on implementation. 20. OFFER STRATEGY A great advertisement cannot always overcome a bad offer. Develop and test: Percentage discounts Dollar discounts Quantity breaks Free shipping Bundles Free design assistance Limited-time offers First-order incentives Reorder incentives Referral offers Volume pricing Seasonal promotions Measure actual profitability. 21. A/B AND MULTIVARIATE TESTING Develop disciplined experiments around: Creative Hooks Audiences Offers Landing pages Headlines CTAs Email subject lines SMS Retargeting windows Campaign structures Do not change ten things and then claim you learned something. Test intelligently. 22. MARKETING AUTOMATION Design automated workflows using systems such as: Zapier CRM systems Email/SMS platforms Lead forms Webhooks/integrations where available ManyChat Other automation platforms Example: Facebook Lead > CRM > Immediate SMS > Immediate email > Sales notification > Follow-up > Retargeting audience > Conversion tracking. 23. CRM STRATEGY Help organize customers/leads by: Source Product interest Stage Customer type Purchase history Value Follow-up status Marketing should become smarter as our customer database grows. 24. INFLUENCER & CREATOR MARKETING Own the business side of influencer/creator campaigns. You determine: Which creators make sense Audience fit Expected economics Compensation structure Affiliate opportunities Tracking Offers/codes Content usage rights Performance Creative Lead owns/supports creative direction. 25. ORGANIC SOCIAL STRATEGY Our VAs can perform repetitive posting. You determine: Platform strategy Posting priorities Content mix Frequency Campaign themes Promotions Audience development Growth opportunities Do not spend your entire day manually posting. Your value is strategy and growth. 26. SOCIAL MEDIA VA MANAGEMENT Create documented systems our VAs can execute. Examples: Posting calendar Group-posting instructions Response templates Escalation rules Comment procedures Lead-capture procedures CRM entry procedures Use lower-cost execution resources intelligently so your own time remains focused on high-value marketing work. 27. ANALYTICS & ATTRIBUTION Understand: GA4 Meta attribution TikTok attribution Platform attribution differences UTMs Conversion events CRM source data Call tracking Post-purchase surveys where useful First-touch vs. last-touch Assisted conversions Do not blindly believe one dashboard. Understand how measurement works. 28. CORE PERFORMANCE METRICS You should be highly comfortable with: Revenue ROAS MER CPA CAC CPL Cost per purchase Conversion rate Average order value Customer lifetime value Repeat purchase rate CTR CPC CPM Frequency Email revenue SMS revenue You must be able to explain these numbers to management in plain English. 29. BUDGET ALLOCATION Recommend how marketing dollars should be distributed. Example: If Meta is producing 5X ROAS and TikTok is producing 1.2X, do not continue equal budgets because the original spreadsheet said so. Evaluate: Scalability Incremental performance Margins Acquisition cost Customer quality Lifetime value Seasonality Move money intelligently. 30. SCALING You must understand the difference between: "A campaign works at $50/day" and: "We can profitably scale this campaign to $5,000/day." Scaling requires monitoring: Audience saturation Frequency CPA Creative fatigue Conversion rate Inventory/capacity Customer economics 31. COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE Continuously study competitors. Analyze: Offers Advertisements Creative Landing pages Promotions Social channels Reviews Positioning Customer complaints Influencers Funnels Email capture Retargeting Find gaps we can exploit. 32. NEW GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES We expect you to continually ask: "What aren't we doing?" Examples could include: New customer segments New channels Affiliate programs Referral programs Partnership marketing Creator partnerships Lead magnets New funnels Reorder programs Loyalty B2B campaigns Geographic campaigns Seasonal opportunities We want proactive thinking. WHAT YOU OWN You OWN: Digital marketing strategy Social marketing strategy Paid social Audience strategy Customer segmentation Retargeting Customer-list marketing Campaign architecture Media buying Budget allocation Funnel strategy Offers Email strategy SMS strategy Lifecycle marketing Marketing automation CRM marketing strategy Influencer economics Conversion analysis Attribution Social marketing reporting ROAS/CPA optimization Growth experiments WHAT THE CREATIVE LEAD OWNS The Creative Strategy & Advertising Content Lead owns: Creative concepts Scripts Hooks development Photography direction Static advertisements Video advertisements Reels Shorts TikToks UGC creative direction Editing Creative variations You provide the marketing requirements. They turn those requirements into exceptional advertising. REQUIRED EXPERIENCE We prefer 5+ years of serious digital/performance marketing experience. You should have substantial experience with: Meta Ads Ecommerce Paid social Retargeting Customer audiences Conversion tracking Email marketing SMS marketing Funnels Analytics Marketing automation Campaign testing Scaling We strongly prefer candidates who have managed substantial real advertising budgets and can demonstrate revenue—not merely followers or traffic. TO APPLY Do NOT send a generic marketing cover letter. Send: 1. PDF Resume 2. Advertising Results Provide examples showing: Spend Revenue ROAS CPA CAC Leads Purchases Conversion rates Explain exactly what YOU controlled. 3. Biggest Account Tell us: What company/product Monthly spend Platforms Your responsibilities Initial problem What you changed Result 4. Strategy Challenge We want to sell custom dye-sublimated shirts nationwide. Target possibilities include: Schools Sports teams Restaurants Businesses Clubs Organizations Events If you had a $10,000 initial test budget. Tell us: Which audiences you test first. Which platforms you use. How you divide the budget. What creative you request from our Creative Lead. What landing pages/funnels you use. What conversion events you track. How you retarget non-buyers. How you market again to purchasers. What results determine whether you scale or stop. What you do after the first 30 days. 5. Diagnostic Challenge A Meta campaign has: Excellent video engagement Excellent CTR Cheap CPC Almost no purchases Tell us what you investigate and why. 6. Scaling Challenge One advertisement produces a 6X ROAS at $100/day. What do you do next? We are looking for someone who thinks like a growth marketer and business owner. Not someone who simply knows how to operate Ads Manager.

title: Senior Graphic Designer — Must Be Able to Design Almost Anything
job_title: Senior Graphic Designer — Must Be Able to Design Almost Anything
description: READ THIS ENTIRE POST BEFORE APPLYING. We are looking for an exceptional, highly experienced Graphic Designer who can handle almost any design project we put in front of them. This is NOT an entry-level position. We are not looking for someone who only makes social media posts, logos, or basic T-shirt graphics. We need a serious professional who can move from: Dye Sublimation Apparel ? Vehicle Wraps ? T-Shirts ? Business Cards ? Brochures ? Signs ? Banners ? Marketing Materials ? Print Production …and do all of it at a very high level. If you are the kind of designer who can look at almost any project and say: “Yes, I can design that.” then we want to hear from you. WHO WE ARE We are an established international commercial printing and apparel company with more than 23 years in business. Our capabilities include: Dye sublimation printing Cut-and-sew sublimated apparel Screen printing Custom T-shirts Vehicle wraps Signs Banners Large-format printing Business cards Flyers Brochures Marketing materials Branding Commercial printing Our company is growing rapidly, especially our Dye Sublimation Cut & Sew Division, and we are extremely busy. We need talented designers who can jump in and contribute immediately. THIS POSITION IS FOR A REAL DESIGNER You should be: Extremely creative Fast Accurate Detail-oriented Technically strong Production-minded Able to work independently Able to follow instructions Able to handle revisions quickly Comfortable with multiple deadlines Capable of solving design problems without constant supervision We need people who can think, create, execute, and deliver. SOFTWARE SKILLS You must be highly proficient with professional design software. Adobe Illustrator — EXPERT LEVEL REQUIRED - Illustrator is extremely important in our production environment. You should be able to work quickly using: Pen Tool Pathfinder Shape Builder Clipping masks Compound paths Layers Artboards Typography Vector illustration Patterns Gradients Image tracing Spot colors Pantone colors Bleeds Cut paths Production templates Print-ready files Keyboard shortcuts are expected. If you need to search through menus to perform basic Illustrator functions, this position is probably not for you. Adobe Photoshop You should be highly skilled with: Photo editing Retouching Masking Color correction Compositing Mockups Smart Objects Image manipulation Raster artwork Large-format graphics Production-ready artwork Adobe InDesign Strong experience with: Brochures Flyers Catalogs Multi-page documents Marketing materials Typography Print layouts Preflight Print-ready PDFs Additional Software Knowledge Is a Plus Experience with any of the following is valuable: Adobe Acrobat Pro CorelDRAW Figma Canva Procreate Adobe Lightroom After Effects Premiere Pro 3D or mockup software RIP software Large-format production software AI design tools Other professional graphics software You do not need to know every program listed above, but you must be technically strong and able to learn new software quickly. WHAT YOU MAY BE DESIGNING One day you may design a fully sublimated sports jersey. The next project could be a vehicle wrap. Then a brochure. Then a T-shirt. Then a banner. Then business cards. Then a complete branded marketing piece. You should be comfortable designing: Dye sublimation shirts Sports jerseys Team uniforms Fishing shirts Racing jerseys Custom apparel T-shirt graphics Vehicle wraps Vehicle lettering Signs Banners Window graphics Trade-show graphics Business cards Flyers Brochures Posters Sales sheets Marketing materials Logos Branding Digital graphics Promotional graphics Versatility is extremely important. SUBLIMATION EXPERIENCE Professional dye sublimation apparel experience is strongly preferred. You should understand: All-over-print apparel Sublimation templates Cut-and-sew layouts Front/back/sleeve design Sponsor and logo placement Names and numbers Pattern development Production layouts Apparel mockups Production-ready sublimation files YOU MUST UNDERSTAND PRODUCTION Being creative is not enough. Your files must actually work when they reach production. You should understand: CMYK vs. RGB Pantone and spot colors Bleeds Safe areas DPI and resolution Raster vs. vector Font outlining Embedded and linked artwork Transparency Print-ready PDFs Large-format production Sublimation production Screen-printing considerations Vehicle templates Cut paths File setup Preflight We do not want designers whose files constantly need to be repaired before production. SPEED MATTERS We are a high-volume production company. We are busy. Very busy. We need designers who can work fast without sacrificing quality. We are not looking for someone who takes all day to complete a basic project. We need the combination of: CREATIVITY + SPEED + ACCURACY + PRODUCTION KNOWLEDGE RESPONSIBILITIES You will: Create original graphic designs Design sublimated apparel Design T-shirts Create vehicle wraps Design signs and banners Design commercial print materials Create branded marketing materials Build customer proofs and mockups Prepare production-ready artwork Recreate or clean up customer artwork Make revisions quickly Follow templates and production specifications Collaborate with our creative and production teams Manage multiple projects simultaneously Maintain organized files Meet deadlines Maintain a high standard of design quality MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS DO NOT APPLY unless you meet these requirements: Minimum 5 years professional graphic design experience Expert Adobe Illustrator skills Strong Photoshop skills Strong InDesign skills Strong typography and layout skills Strong understanding of color and composition Professional print-production knowledge Ability to work quickly Ability to handle multiple projects Excellent attention to detail Strong English communication Reliable computer Reliable high-speed internet Dependable attendance Ability to work independently POSITION DETAILS Full-time 40 hours per week Monday through Friday Remote Permanent, long-term position High-volume workflow Growing international company Paid vacation during Christmas break We are looking for someone who wants to become a long-ter ---------- mber of our team, not someone looking for temporary freelance work. HOW TO APPLY Incomplete applications will not be considered. Your application must include: Resume Portfolio link At least 10 examples of your best work If you claim sublimation experience, include at least 10 sublimation apparel designs Examples showing multiple design categories are strongly preferred Short video introducing yourself and speaking English Briefly describe your experience with: Illustrator Photoshop InDesign Dye sublimation Commercial printing Vehicle wraps / large-format graphics IMPORTANT We are not looking for an average designer. We want someone who is exceptionally good at what they do. Someone who can be given a project with minimal direction and figure it out. Someone who can create from scratch. Someone who understands what looks good. Someone who understands how artwork gets produced. Someone who works fast. Someone who catches mistakes. Someone who takes pride in their work. And most importantly: WE WANT SOMEONE WHO CAN DESIGN ALMOST ANYTHING WE PUT IN FRONT OF THEM — AND DO IT VERY WELL. If that describes you, send us your portfolio. Show us what you can do.

title: Accounting & Marketing Assistant
description: You have successfully maintained the books and accounting for an Australian business turning over $5 million or more and are now looking for a broader role where you can take on greater responsibility and contribute beyond finance in a key position. Reporting to the Australian management team, you'll take ownership of the day-to-day bookkeeping and financial administration. You'll maintain accurate financial records, complete reconciliations, manage accounts payable and receivable, and prepare timely financial information and management reports. You'll also work alongside our external accountant, who manages the BAS and taxation requirements. Beyond the accounting responsibilities, you'll enjoy a varied role supporting the business in other key areas. This includes coordinating marketing activities with our Australian team to grow Yum Tasmanian’s online presence, assisting with grant applications, and contributing to a range of business initiatives. Yum Tasmanian is a proudly Australian, family-owned business that has been supplying premium potatoes throughout Australia for more than 30 years. Beginning as an organic potato producer in 1994, the business has grown into a nationally recognised supplier to major retailers including Coles, Woolworths, IGA, independent retailers and wholesale markets. Today, the group operates across several businesses within agriculture, fresh produce and related industries. As the business continues to grow, there is a strong focus on building the Yum brand, educating consumers and expanding its online presence through organic marketing. We want you to be a driver in helping us build Yum into Australia's most recognised online potato brand by growing our organic digital presence to over 1 million Instagram and Facebook followers through organic marketing. The role is Monday to Friday, working from an office. In return for your great performance, you’ll be supported with autonomy, rewards and more opportunity for growth over time. If this sounds like a role you’d enjoy and succeed in, apply now via the link below for more information. Application link: ----------

title: Trailer Repair Admin
description: GH Logistics and AJG Transport operate a high-performance freight brokerage and asset-based transportation network specializing in dry van and refrigerated freight. We move quickly, but we move with structure. Our operation is built on real-time visibility, disciplined execution, clear communication, and accountability. We take pride in keeping freight organized, assets accounted for, and operations running cleanly from pickup through delivery. If you have experience coordinating equipment repairs, working with drivers and repair vendors, and keeping trailer operations moving during overnight hours, this role provides an opportunity to take ownership of a critical part of our Trailer Management operation. Role Overview The Trailer Repair FMT is responsible for maintaining overnight control of trailer repair activity and supporting off-tour Trailer Management operations. Your primary responsibility is to coordinate trailer repairs during the night shift, including high-volume on-road repair activity, while ensuring trailer records, repair statuses, documentation, and operational updates remain accurate in real time. You will work closely with the night repair team, drivers, carriers, repair vendors, facility personnel, and the Trailer Management team to keep equipment issues moving toward resolution. The night team is also responsible for verifying and completing work handed off by the day team and delivering a fully reconciled and accurate board for the incoming day shift. This is an operations and repair coordination position. You will not physically repair trailers and you will not have authority to approve company spending. What You’ll Be Doing Overnight Trailer Repair Coordination • Serve as the primary Trailer Management point of coordination for overnight and on-road trailer repairs, working with drivers, carriers, facilities, roadside providers, mobile mechanics, and repair vendors. • Review reported trailer defects, gather photos, inspection details, diagnoses, estimates, parts information, and other documentation needed to determine the appropriate next step. • Coordinate roadside service, mobile repairs, terminal repairs, inspections, trailer swaps, or equipment repositioning and follow up on vendor status, parts availability, completion timelines, and return-to-service expectations. • Continue follow-up on repairs handed off by the day team until they are resolved or properly documented and returned to the day team. • Escalate repair costs, safety concerns, major equipment issues, and matters requiring financial approval to authorized leadership; this role has no authority to approve spending. Fleetio and Data Integrity • Maintain Fleetio records overnight in real time and enter all repair, trailer, and operational updates handled during the shift. • Ensure trailer repair statuses, locations, assignments, conditions, and related records remain accurate and current. • Conduct overnight data integrity checks and investigate missing, outdated, conflicting, or incomplete information. • Update and maintain records involving misused trailers, partner carrier trailers, repair activity, vendors, and supporting documentation. • Identify and resolve discrepancies between operational information and system records before the morning handoff whenever possible. Off-Tour Trailer Operations • Run the required overnight trailer classification sweep and identify trailers requiring correction, investigation, or follow-up. • Close operational gaps and unfinished trailer-related work handed off by the day team. • Assist carriers requiring trailers and coordinate trailer availability, loading, seating, assignments, and related movements. • Monitor and address trailer concerns that may affect drivers, facilities, customers, freight movement, or equipment availability. • Handle additional overnight trailer-related tasks and maintain communication with facility personnel and designated internal operational contacts. Documentation and Morning Handoff • Maintain complete and organized trailer repair paperwork and supporting documentation throughout the shift. • Clearly document completed work, pending repairs, vendor responses, equipment concerns, unresolved issues, and required follow-ups. • Verify items handed off by the day team and document what was completed, remains pending, or requires escalation. • Ensure every unresolved item has clear ownership, an accurate current status, documented next steps, and a proper handoff. • Deliver the 8 AM handoff complete and on time, including a reconciled board accurately reflecting trailer locations, statuses, repairs, outstanding issues, and required follow-ups. What Success Looks Like • Overnight and on-road trailer repairs are acknowledged quickly, coordinated effectively, and consistently followed through toward resolution. • Fleetio, trailer classifications, repair records, and other operational data remain accurate and updated in real time throughout the shift. • Drivers, carriers, vendors, facilities, and internal teams receive timely and clear communication regarding repair and trailer needs. • Repair documentation, escalations, and unresolved issues are complete, organized, and properly handed off without unauthorized spending decisions. • The day team receives a complete 8:00 AM handoff with a fully reconciled trailer board showing completed, pending, and escalated items. Who We’re Looking For • Experience in trailer management, fleet operations, dispatch, transportation, roadside assistance, or maintenance coordination. • Knowledge of common trailer repairs, components, equipment defects, and maintenance terminology; repair coordination experience preferred. • Able to review driver reports, photos, inspections, diagnoses, and estimates, ask the right follow-up questions, and determine appropriate next steps. • Strong communication, attention to detail, problem-solving, prioritization, and follow-through in a fast-paced overnight operation. • Comfortable working independently and using Fleetio or similar fleet systems; Samsara, LoadStop, Microsoft Office, and Google Workspace experience is a plus. • Minimum 50 WPM typing speed, strong written and verbal English, and a reliable remote setup with backup internet and power. Schedule and Work Setup • Long term and full time remote independent contractor role • Direct engagement with a US company, not an agency or BPO • Current shift availability: Tuesday - Saturday 8 PM - 6 AM CDT • Consistent availability during the assigned US shift is required • Zoom presence with camera on throughout the shift is required • Time tracking software, including Hubstaff or another platform, may be implemented as operationally required What You’ll Get • Independent contractor setup • $75 monthly insurance stipend, with eligibility beginning 30 days after hire • Reliable biweekly payments • A stable, long-term opportunity that is not seasonal or project-based • Direct exposure to a live US transportation and fleet operation • Meaningful responsibility over overnight trailer repair activity • Opportunities to develop deeper experience in Trailer Management, fleet maintenance, repair coordination, and transportation operations • Potential growth within Trailer Management, Fleet Operations, Maintenance Coordination, or broader logistics operations This role is built for someone who can keep control of trailer repairs after hours. You will not simply receive repair requests and pass them along. You will coordinate the response, maintain accurate Fleetio records, follow open repairs, support overnight trailer needs, clean up operational discrepancies, document what happened, and make sure the day team receives a reliable and reconciled picture of the operation every morning. title: OpenClaw Agent Engineer - Build AI Agents and Keep Them Running
job_title: OpenClaw Agent Engineer - Build AI Agents and Keep Them Running
description: READ THIS FIRST You must have used OpenClaw before. You must be able to prove it. If you have not used OpenClaw, please do not apply. We will not read your message. We are saying this clearly so we do not waste your time or ours. THE JOB IN ONE SENTENCE You build OpenClaw agents. You keep them running. You make them faster, cheaper and more reliable every week. That is the whole job. ABOUT US We are a health and wellness company. We sell products online. We have a small remote team in several countries. We are building a team of AI agents to run parts of our business. WHAT IS AN AGENT HERE An agent is a small program that does one job. It runs by itself on a timer. Nobody starts it by hand. It runs at 3am while everyone is asleep. We want 10 to 20 agents. Each one does one job. Three real examples: 1) STORE WATCHER. Every 3 hours it checks our online shop. Is checkout working? Is any product priced wrong? Are we selling stock we do not have? If yes, it reports. If no, it says nothing. 2) INBOX READER. Twice a day it reads email, Slack, Asana and meeting notes. It works out what is waiting on the owner. Then it writes the replies for him to approve. 3) COMPETITOR WATCHER. Once a week it checks what our competitors changed. It only reports the changes. Above all the agents sits one main agent. We call it the Chief of Staff. It manages the other agents. It is the only agent that talks to the owner. WHAT YOU WILL DO 1) BUILD THE PLATFORM. One AWS account. OpenClaw installed and running on a timer. A safe place to store passwords and API keys. A log of every run. A stop button. 2) BUILD THE AGENTS. One at a time. We give you a written brief for each one. You d ---------- how to build it. 3) KEEP THEM RUNNING. This is half the job. An agent that stops quietly is worse than no agent at all, because we will trust a silence that means nothing is being checked. 4) MAKE THEM BETTER EVERY WEEK. - Using too much money? Make them cheaper. - Too slow? Make them faster. - Sending too many messages? Reduce the noise. - Failing sometimes? Find out why and fix it. You will send a short report every week: how many runs, how many failures, how much it cost, and what you improved. 5) OWN IT. You will be the only person who understands this system. We need you to write things down so that stays safe. YOU MUST HAVE 1) OPENCLAW EXPERIENCE. This is not optional. You have installed OpenClaw yourself. You have run it. You have fixed it when it broke. We need proof. See the PROOF section below. 2) AWS. You have set up EC2 yourself. You know IAM. You have used Secrets Manager or something like it. 3) PYTHON. You write code that runs on a server. Not only in a notebook. 4) API EXPERIENCE. REST APIs. OAuth. Webhooks. You have handled rate limits and retries. You have worked with an API that gave you wrong data. 5) LLM API EXPERIENCE. OpenAI, Anthropic or similar. Inside real code. Not only in a chat window. 6) CLEAR WRITTEN ENGLISH. Most of our work is written. You must be able to explain a technical decision in writing. 7) TIME OVERLAP. At least 4 hours per day that overlap with Sydney, Australia business hours. PROOF OF OPENCLAW EXPERIENCE Your application must include at least one of these. Two is better. OPTION A - A SHORT SCREEN RECORDING. 2 to 3 minutes. Record your own screen. Show OpenClaw running on your machine or your server. Show the config. Show the logs. Show it doing something. OPTION B - A REPOSITORY. A GitHub link with your commit history, showing your OpenClaw setup or an agent you built for it. OPTION C - A LIVE SYSTEM. Something running now that we can look at, or that you can show us on a call. Screenshots alone are not enough. Anyone can send a screenshot. We need to see you working with it. AND ANSWER THESE FIVE QUESTIONS. These are simple if you have really used it. Please answer all five. 1) Did you install OpenClaw yourself, or did you use a one-click hosting service or a template? Both answers are fine. We just need to know which one. 2) What machine did it run on? Say the operating system and where it was hosted. 3) How did you keep it running after you closed your laptop or logged out? Name the exact method you used. 4) Where do you look when you want to see what OpenClaw did? Name the file or the command. 5) Tell us about one time it broke. What broke, and how did you fix it? PLEASE DO NOT APPLY IF - You have never used OpenClaw - You cannot show us proof - You have only used no-code tools and never written code that runs on a server - You want a job where every task is fully explained before you start - You are sending the same message to many jobs today ONE MORE THING, AND WE MEAN IT We need you to tell us the truth about what you can and cannot do. If something is too hard for you today, say so. We will pay for the course. We will give you the time. What we cannot work with is a date that was never real, or a yes that was really a maybe. Before you start each piece of work, we will ask you to rate it from 1 to 10. 1 is very easy. 10 is very hard. We want the real number. If it is an 8, say 8. This is a real part of the job. It is not a nice sentence in a job advert. HOW TO APPLY Send a message with all five things below. If anything is missing, we will not read it. 1) Start your message with the word HEARTBEAT. This shows us you read the post. 2) Your proof of OpenClaw experience. Recording, repository or live system. 3) Your answers to the five OpenClaw questions above. 4) Your answers to these three questions. Short answers are better than long ones. a) Tell us about one program you built that ran by itself for 30 days or more. Something broke while nobody was watching. How did you find out it had broken? b) Your program runs at 3am. Nobody is logged in. It needs an API key to do its job. Where do you keep that key, and why there? c) Twenty different agents all send messages to one busy person. After one month, that person stops reading them. What do you build so this does not happen? 5) Your rate. USD per month, for 40 hours per week. Please write your application yourself. We read a lot of AI writing every day. We are hiring for good thinking, not for good grammar. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT 1) We read your proof and your answers. 2) A 30 minute video call. 3) A paid test project. One week. One small agent. We pay your normal rate. You keep the money even if we do not continue. 4) If it goes well, full time and long term.
