This is not a role for someone who only wants to pass tasks on to developers or rely entirely on page-builder apps. We need someone who is comfortable getting into Shopify, working with themes, building properly, testing carefully and using good judgement. Okay, you’re mid way through this ad, congrats but to help ensure you’re not just using AI tools to skim the job post, make sure you include “Buy Better Coffee Online” in your application subject line. You’ll work closely with Operations, Marketing, Design and Customer Support to make sure the online store is accurate, on-brand, commercially useful and improving over time. A few things you’ll be across - Owning Shopify theme customisation, including hands-on use of Liquid, HTML and CSS - Building and maintaining sections, templates and custom landing pages - Keeping the Online Store 2.0 structure and theme configuration clean, current and easy for others to use - Applying practical UX and conversion judgement to page layout, hierarchy and mobile experience - Managing website content, including homepage, category pages, landing pages, promo flags, navigation and seasonal campaign content - Working closely with the Marketing team to execute the promotional calendar as it relates to e-com outputs. - Setting up and testing promotions in line with planned campaign activity - Coordinating assets for new product launches, sales, campaigns and e-commerce changes with Design, Marketing and the wider team - Supporting end-to-end online e-commerce projects, from stakeholder briefing through to testing - Providing real-time and monthly reporting on campaign, product and site performance - Translating reporting into clear, useful recommendations, not just sending raw numbers - Maintaining sources of truth for performance data that stakeholders can reference directly - Monitoring stock and maintaining accurate catalogue information - Auditing the site and assets to make sure all available products are live, current and accurate - Supporting and optimising subscription operations through Recharge - Building SOPs, templates and automation where possible to reduce manual catalogue and audit work over time What you’ll bring - Minimum two years’ experience in a similar Shopify-focused e-commerce role - Advanced Shopify experience, including hands-on theme customisation with Liquid, HTML and CSS - Confidence building custom landing pages and templates without relying only on third-party page-builder apps - Practical UX and conversion design sense, especially around layout, hierarchy and mobile experience - Strong attention to detail and a high standard for accuracy - Good written and verbal communication skills - Confidence working with stakeholders across Customer Support, Design, Marketing and Operations - Ability to turn data and reporting into clear, practical recommendations - Comfortable working independently across time zones, while still being part of a collaborative team - Confidence using Microsoft 365 systems, tools and a willingness to learn new apps, plugins and systems. Bonus points if you’ve got Microsoft Business Central experience. - A continuous improvement mindset, you notice repetitive work and look for better ways to get it done Highly regarded - Experience with Recharge or a comparable subscription app - Experience with Yotpo or a comparable rewards app - Experience with Shopify Plus, including Plus migration experience - Familiarity with Figma or a similar design/collaboration tool - Experience in online coffee, food and beverage, retail, subscription, or multi-channel e-commerce (including Amazon, TikTok Shop, Google Shopping) - Experience using AI or automation tools to improve workflows and reduce manual effort What success looks like - The online store is accurate, organised, current and easy to manage - Product catalogue data is clean, reliable and well maintained - Campaigns and assets are turned around within agreed timelines - Promotions are uploaded, tested and launched accurately - Reporting leads to clear recommendations and better decisions - Manual audit effort reduces over time through SOPs, templates or automation - Stakeholders have confidence in the store, the data and the way campaign work is coordinated - You help make the e-commerce function smarter, cleaner, more scalable over time and ultimately a more profitable channel What’s in it for you First up: we want this role to be one of the best jobs you’ve ever had. You’ll have the chance to grow your skills, improve systems, work on meaningful e-commerce projects, and help a purpose-led coffee brand keep building a better online experience. This role will be part of our growing e-com Team. We offer a generous package, Quarterly Performance bonus after probation, HMO Program after one year of tenure, Volunteer and Training Leave, Philippine Public Holidays converted to Annual Leave credits, access to ongoing learning and development, and an Employee Assistance Program. Sounds like your kind of role? Send us your resume and cover letter (Resume without cover letters won’t be considered), plus: A link to one live Shopify store you’ve personally built or theme-customised (yours, a client’s, or an employer’s), with a sentence or two on one specific section or page you built using Liquid, HTML or CSS, and why you built it that way. job_title: Direct Response Video Editor & AI Creative Producer for E-commerce
description: Hiring: Direct Response Video Editor (VSLs + Competitor Ad Recreation + AI Cartoon Videos + Other AI Style Ads + Short Form Videos) DTC / dropshipping brand doing ~$100k/month in revenue Role: Video Editor / AI Video Producer Read this part first We are not looking for someone to "make our videos look nice." We are looking for someone who understands that a video's job is to hold attention and make people buy — and who can build that video end to end, including sourcing or generating every frame of footage inside it. If you need a folder of assets handed to you before you can start editing, this role isn't for you. If you can take a script, a product, or a competitor reference and come back with a finished, conversion-ready asset, keep reading. Who we are We're a direct response DTC brand currently doing around $100k/month, almost entirely on the back of paid media and creative. Creative is our growth lever. Not the site, not the offer tweaks, not the email flows — the video. That means the editor seat is one of the highest-leverage roles in the company. When a video wins here, it wins loudly and you'll see it in the numbers within days. We're scaling, and we want to stop stitching together freelancers per project. We want one highly skilled person who becomes part of the team, learns our angles and our customer inside out, and gets sharper with every batch we ship. How this role starts (please read carefully) This does not begin as a full-time position, and that's deliberate. We start every editor on a lighter workload — a smaller number of videos per week — for the first stretch. Not because we're testing whether you can hold a job, but because we want to see how you fit: how you take feedback, how you handle a brief or reference ad we hand you, how you communicate when something's unclear, and whether the work holds up once the novelty wears off. It also gives you time to learn our customer, our angles, and what a "winning" video looks like in our account specifically. The first type of work you'll primarily be doing is competitor ad recreation and localization. We'll give you proven competitor ads and your job will be to rebuild them for our brand and our market. This lets us quickly see how well you can reverse-engineer winning creative, source footage independently, match pacing and structure, and execute without needing everything handed to you. From there it scales. As the fit proves out and your creatives start performing, the volume goes up, the pay goes up, and the arrangement moves toward a secure, permanent full-time seat — with a defined monthly retainer rather than per-project work. To be clear about what we're offering: Phase 1 — Fit: Lower volume, paid per project or at a smaller retainer. You'll primarily start with competitor ad recreations/localizations and short-form creatives. Heavy feedback from us. We're both figuring out if this works. Phase 2 — Ramp: Volume increases, you take on the VSLs, AI cartoon projects, original concepts, and competitor recreations with less hand-holding. Pay increases accordingly. Phase 3 — In-house: Full-time, secure retainer, you own the creative pipeline and have real input on direction. Room to grow into a creative lead as we bring on more editors. We're not looking for someone to fill a gap for three months. We're looking for the person who's still here in two years running our creative. The slow start is how we get there without either of us wasting the other's time. If you need immediate full-time income from day one, this probably isn't the right fit right now — and that's fine, just be upfront about it. What you'll actually be making 1. Competitor Ad Recreation & Localization This is where you'll start, and it will be a major part of your initial workload. We actively research winning ads from competitors and other markets. We'll give you proven creatives and references, and your job is to reverse-engineer what makes them work and recreate them for our brand in Swedish. We're looking for someone who can take a competitor ad and recreate the structure, hook, pacing, visual flow, editing style, captions, voiceover structure, and overall concept as closely as needed — while replacing the competitor's product, branding, language, footage, and other elements with assets appropriate for our brand. In many cases, this means rebuilding an ad almost shot-for-shot. You might receive nothing more than the competitor ad, our product information, and access to our tools. From there, you're expected to figure out how to rebuild it. You'll be responsible for: Breaking down exactly why the original ad works — hook, pacing, cuts, visual sequence, proof, mechanism, CTA, etc. Translating and localizing scripts, captions, hooks, and on-screen text rather than producing awkward word-for-word translations. Sourcing replacement footage yourself when we don't provide it. Using AI-generated footage when the necessary shot doesn't exist or can't be sourced. Replacing competitor products and branding with our own product wherever necessary. Recreating visual demonstrations, product shots, graphics, animations, screenshots, and other elements when needed. Matching the pacing and psychology of the original creative rather than simply making something that covers the same topic. The goal isn't to blindly copy an ad. The goal is to identify the elements making a proven creative work and rebuild those elements for our product and market. 2. Long-form VSLs (Video Sales Letters) The core of the long-form side of the role. 2–7+ minute sales videos built off scripts we provide. You'll be responsible for: Pacing the entire video so retention doesn't collapse — pattern interrupts, cuts, zooms, motion, sound design, text emphasis, visual proof Sourcing your own b-roll. Stock libraries, licensed footage, UGC-style clips, screen recordings, archival, whatever the script calls for. You find it. You don't ask us to send it. In some cases we will also provide clips and we have a bunch of softwares that you can use to make this process easier aswell. Generating AI video to fill the gaps stock can't cover — visualizing mechanisms, metaphors, before/after states, scenarios that don't exist as footage. Building the visual language for a section, not just laying clips over a voiceover. Kinetic text, callouts, subtitles, on-screen proof elements, testimonial treatments. Sound design and music that carries emotional beats without burying the VO. 3. AI cartoon / animated videos (short form AND long form) We're producing a growing volume of fully AI-generated animated content — story-driven ads, explainer content, character-led narratives. title: Growth Marketing / Customer Acquisition Manager
description: GROWTH MARKETING MANAGER Growth & Customer Acquisition Manager — HVAC & Electrical We are looking for an independent Growth Marketing Manager who will take ownership of the company's entire marketing function: strategy, paid and organic channels, content, and analytics. The primary result of this role is new customers, collected revenue, and profit. Not posts, not impressions, not reports. Compensation is a percentage of the revenue generated by the marketing system you build. There is no income cap. ============================================================ WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR ============================================================ Someone who thinks like an entrepreneur and treats every company advertising dollar as their own. Someone who understands marketing, sales, and unit economics. You develop the plan, you execute it, you shut down what does not work and scale what does. You do not wait for instructions. Technically, this is a strong generalist who uses AI to cover the workload that previously required several separate specialists: performance, SEO, content, video, and analytics. ============================================================ EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS ============================================================ Overall practical experience in digital / growth marketing: 5+ years, including at least 2 years independently developing and executing growth strategy. By area: - Performance marketing and customer acquisition with responsibility for budget and results: 3+ years - Google Ads — independently managing campaigns and budgets: 3+ years - SEO and Local SEO (preferably for local service businesses): 3+ years - Google Business Profile / Google Maps: 3+ years - Marketing analytics, tracking, attribution, ROAS / CAC / CPL: 3+ years - Meta / Instagram Ads and short-form content: 2+ years - Video marketing, YouTube, content production: 2+ years - Yelp and other local lead-gen platforms: preferably 2+ years - AI tools in marketing (research, copy, image/video generation, automation): 2+ years, or demonstrated advanced ability with fewer years Years alone are not what matters. The candidate must show concrete results from previous projects: budget, leads, CAC, ROAS, sales, and collected revenue. See the Proof of Experience section below. ============================================================ WHAT YOU WILL DO ============================================================ 1. STRATEGY AND GROWTH PLAN Independently analyze the market and competitors, develop a customer acquisition plan, present it to management, and execute it. The plan covers every channel (SEO, Google Maps, Google Ads, Meta, Yelp, YouTube, content, referrals, partnerships, existing customer base marketing), new territories, locations, and services, as well as targets for CPL, CAC, conversion rate, average ticket, ROAS, and profitability. 2. MAXIMUM RESULTS WITH MINIMUM BUDGET Increasing the advertising budget is not a strategy. Before asking for more ad spend, the manager must look for growth elsewhere: improve the offer, creatives, and landing pages; raise conversion rate and lead quality; reduce CPL and CAC; grow organic traffic, average ticket, repeat business, and referrals. The long-term objective is marketing assets (Google Maps, SEO, content, reviews, customer base) that bring in customers without advertising costs growing proportionally. 3. PAID CHANNELS Google Ads. Building and auditing campaigns; Search, Remarketing, Performance Max, and YouTube Ads when economically justified. Keyword management, negative keywords, search term analysis, ad copy, landing pages, conversion and call tracking, A/B testing of offers. Optimization for CPL, CAC, ROAS, and profit — not clicks. Meta / Instagram. Strategy, original creatives, Reels, Stories, testing audiences, offers, and messaging, campaign management, organic reach growth. Every piece of content has a purpose: Attention → Trust → Lead → Customer → Revenue. Yelp. Profiles for real locations, optimization, review responses, Yelp Ads only when the economics work. If the channel does not deliver customers at an acceptable cost, the manager recommends reducing or reallocating the budget. 4. ORGANIC CHANNELS SEO. Strategy, technical audit, keyword and competitor research, service pages and legitimate city / service-area pages, site structure, SEO content, internal linking, backlinks, indexing and ranking monitoring. Success is measured not by the number of pages, but by calls, customers, and revenue from organic search. Google Business Profile / Google Maps. Creating and verifying profiles only for real locations in compliance with Google requirements, full optimization, regular updates, photos and videos, a legitimate strategy for growing the quantity and quality of reviews, review responses, local ranking and competitor analysis. Each profile is a separate channel with its own tracking of calls, leads, and revenue. YouTube. An educational channel and a long-term asset: concepts, scripts, Shorts, AI video, voice-over, editing, project and educational videos. Not treated as a source of quick ROI. 5. CONTENT Content from every project. Every completed job is a marketing asset. We need a system that turns real projects into before / after content, Reels, Shorts, YouTube videos, case studies, and content for GBP, the website, SEO, and ad creatives. One project — multiple pieces of content for multiple platforms, using AI for speed and lower cost. Educational content. The company should become a source of useful information for homeowners: why an air conditioner is not cooling, repair vs. replace, how to choose a heat pump, how equipment is sized, when an electrical panel upgrade is needed, why permits and inspections matter, how to compare contractor estimates, what not to save money on. The chain: Educate → Build Trust → Create Demand → Generate Leads → Generate Revenue. A person may not be looking for anything today — but when they need us, they will remember us. Viral content. Systematically create and test material people want to share: unusual HVAC and electrical problems, breakdowns of bad installations, contractor and homeowner mistakes, myths, equipment comparisons, experiments, answers to common questions. Nobody can guarantee every video goes viral — the job is systematic work on ideas with high reach potential. Our content must be different. Thousands of contractors publish the same thing: "Call us for all your HVAC needs." We do not need that. The constant question: why would someone watch our content? It must be original, useful, easy for a homeowner to understand, visually recognizable, and interesting even to someone who is not buying anything right now. The goal is our own media style and brand voice. 6. AI AS A WORKING TOOL Professional use of modern AI tools for research and competitor analysis, copywriting, image and video generation, editing, AI avatars and voice-over, scripts, creatives, landing pages, SEO analysis, content repurposing, analytics, and automation. AI makes production faster and cheaper, but it does not replace strategic thinking, originality, fact-checking, or responsibility for results. 7. ANALYTICS AND FULL-FUNNEL RESPONSIBILITY The manager owns the entire customer journey: >> Strategy → Attention → Lead → Appointment → Customer → Sale → Payment → Collected Revenue To do this, they build and maintain attribution: CRM, call tracking, unique phone numbers, conversion and website tracking, Google Analytics, tracking across Google Ads, GBP, Yelp, Meta, YouTube, and landing pages. The company must know the source of every customer. A report like "Google Ads generated 100 leads" is not enough. We want to see: >> Marketing Spend → Leads → Qualified Leads → Appointments → Customers → Sales → Collected Revenue → Profit If there are leads but no customers, the manager finds exactly where the funnel breaks (traffic quality, offer, website, response time, call handling, qualification, scheduling, sales, pricing, follow-up) and proposes a measurable solution. ============================================================ KPI ============================================================ New and qualified leads, new customers, CPL, CAC, Lead → Customer conversion rate, jobs sold, average ticket, collected revenue, ROAS, Marketing ROI, profitability, organic acquisition growth. The number of posts, videos, views, impressions, and clicks is not the final result. On ROAS: $10,000 in advertising → $50,000 in collected revenue = ROAS 5x. But ROAS alone does not equal profit. The manager accounts for job costs, gross margin, CAC, refunds, chargebacks, and all marketing expenses. The goal is not an impressive number, but profitable growth. ============================================================ COMPENSATION ============================================================ The primary model is a percentage of revenue actually collected by the company from new customers that can be objectively attributed to marketing channels created or managed by the Growth Marketing Manager. There is no income cap: the company earns more → the manager earns more. Commission is paid only on money the company has actually received. Not included: unsigned and unpaid estimates, unpaid invoices, canceled jobs, refunds and chargebacks, existing customers without a confirmed new source, personal referrals outside the marketing system, repeat business (unless separately agreed). Customer source is confirmed through CRM, call tracking, unique phone numbers, website tracking, platforms (Google Ads, GBP, Yelp, Meta, YouTube), landing pages, and other pre-agreed attribution systems. ============================================================ PROOF OF EXPERIENCE ============================================================ During selection, the candidate must show real projects with numbers: what business, the starting situation, budget, number of leads and customers, CPL, CAC, ROAS, collected revenue, which organic channels were built, what did not work and why, and what the candidate did personally. "I increased brand awareness" and "I managed social media" are not proof of experience. The format: Problem → Action → Numbers → Result. ============================================================ WHO THIS POSITION IS NOT FOR ============================================================ Anyone who measures success by the number of posts, clicks, and impressions; solves every problem by increasing the budget; does not work with analytics; waits for instructions and avoids decisions; is not ready to own a measurable result; does not use AI professionally; produces the same generic content as every other contractor; cannot explain how their work turns into customers, revenue, and profit. ============================================================ CORE PRINCIPLE ============================================================ The Growth Marketing Manager can answer at any moment: how much we spent, how many qualified leads and new customers we got, what one customer cost, how much revenue they brought, which channels are profitable, what to scale, what to shut down — and how to get more customers without proportionally increasing the budget. The job is to build a marketing system that over time becomes stronger, more recognizable, more organic, cheaper, and more profitable. The ultimate result: the maximum number of profitable customers with the minimum necessary marketing budget.

We need a data engineer to own the pipeline that makes this possible: discovering venues from multiple sources, deduplicating them at scale, and — most importantly — extracting real insider information from unstructured review text. Vibe, best time to visit, recurring events, live music nights, specials, and other details no competitor (Google, Yelp, OpenTable) is systematically capturing. This extraction work is the core differentiator of the product, not a side task, and it needs to be built as a repeatable, ongoing process, not a one-time cleanup. This is a pipeline-building role, not a manual-labor role. You'll build an automated, resumable system that can run largely unattended, handle rate limits and messy source data, and scale from one city to a thousand without requiring manual babysitting at each step. A business-claim flow reduces ongoing maintenance over time — once a business claims its profile, it helps keep its own data current — and your pipeline should be designed with that in mind, prioritizing claim-conversion alongside raw ingestion rather than treating them separately. You'll work daily with Claude Code and AI-assisted extraction as the actual method of building this, not a shortcut layered on top. As the system scales, you may be running or supervising multiple parallel AI-driven extraction sessions across regions — we need someone who can verify output quality and catch when something's gone wrong, not someone who prompts once and trusts the result blindly. You don't need years of formal "data engineer" title experience to apply. What you need is a specific, demonstrable example: a project where you pulled messy, unstructured data (reviews, documents, scraped pages) into something structured and reliable, ideally including deduplication and some form of ongoing freshness/validation — not a one-time script that ran once and was never touched again. This role reports directly to the CTO. This is Monday–Friday, 40 hours/week, ground-floor ownership with real room to grow as the platform scales from one city to the entire country. description: Remote AR, Collections & Legal Compliance Specialist Job Overview: We are seeking an experienced AR, Collections & Legal Compliance Specialist to support residential property-management operations for communities in Texas, beginning with the Beaumont and Galveston areas, with potential expansion across the portfolio. The role reports to a designated Operations Leader. The specialist will take ownership of the administrative processes surrounding Accounts Receivable, delinquency and collections, resident communication, payment commitments, notices, community compliance, legal/eviction administration, and move-out coordination. The ideal candidate is highly disciplined, process-oriented, and exceptionally accurate with resident ledgers, dates, documentation, and legal/compliance workflows. The role requires strong communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to manage sensitive resident matters professionally while following standardized procedures. Key Responsibilities: Accounts Receivable & Delinquency Review portfolio accounts receivable and delinquency activity in Rent Manager daily. Maintain accurate collection queues by community and resident. Identify newly delinquent accounts, aging balances, recurring delinquency, and high-risk accounts. Contact residents according to approved collection procedures using telephone, text, email, resident portal, and other approved channels. Document material collection attempts and resident responses. Establish and document approved payment commitments and track their due dates. Follow up promptly on missed or broken payment commitments. Maintain accurate collection notes, tasks, account statuses, and supporting documentation. Escalate requests for exceptions, payment plans, hardship assistance, or management variances according to established procedures. Produce recurring delinquency and collections reports and participate in weekly collections/accountability reviews. Identify systemic causes of delinquency and recommend process improvements. Notice Administration Prepare approved late notices and collection communications using standardized, state-specific procedures and templates. Maintain notice dates and evidence of delivery or service where required. Track statutory and company deadlines. Verify resident ledgers, lease information, prior notices, and supporting documentation before escalation. Escalate inconsistencies or missing documentation before legal action proceeds. Administer approved late-notice and statutory-notice workflows in Rent Manager according to state-specific procedures and required U.S./legal approvals. Community Compliance & Enforcement Receive field-inspection results, photographs, videos, resident complaints, and other supporting information. Create and maintain compliance cases in Rent Manager. Verify supporting evidence before initiating approved resident communications. Prepare standardized Community Guideline notices and corrective-action correspondence. Establish cure deadlines according to approved procedures. Communicate professionally with residents regarding required corrective actions. Track open compliance cases and cure dates. Coordinate reinspections with local Community Operations Specialists. Maintain complete evidence and communication histories. Identify repeat or serious violations and escalate unresolved matters according to approved enforcement procedures. Maintain consistent application of Community Guidelines across communities. Identify recurring property-level compliance issues and report patterns to Operations leadership. Legal & Eviction Administration Identify accounts or compliance cases that have reached an approved escalation threshold. Assemble complete resident account and compliance documentation, including ledgers, leases, notices, payment histories, payment commitments, photographs, and communication records. Prepare legal referral packets. Coordinate directly with authorized U.S. management and legal counsel. Track filing dates, hearings, judgments, writs, possession dates, appeals, and other legal milestones. Maintain accurate legal status and next actions in Rent Manager. Track attorney requests for additional information. Coordinate with field personnel regarding possession or other physical-action requirements. Maintain a portfolio-wide eviction and legal pipeline. Immediately escalate missed deadlines, legal complications, or incomplete files. Handle legal and eviction matters administratively and do not independently determine legal strategy, file pleadings as legal counsel, serve process, or perform actions reserved for licensed or authorized U.S. professionals. Move-Out Coordination Receive and document Notices to Vacate and establish expected move-out dates. Coordinate required resident communications. Track possession status and key returns. Coordinate field inspections and physical documentation. Obtain forwarding information. Ensure resident and unit/site status is accurately updated in Rent Manager. Trigger the appropriate vacancy, turnover, or asset-management workflow upon possession. Coordinate the handoff to the Home Asset & Inventory Specialist when a home becomes vacant, abandoned, surrendered, or otherwise requires title or asset review. Coordinate with the Revenue Team when marketable inventory becomes available. Abandoned / Evicted Home Handoff Ensure a formal handoff occurs once legal possession, abandonment, surrender, or another approved transition is completed. Provide the receiving asset-management team with occupant status, possession date, legal status, known ownership/title information, resident ledger, supporting legal documents, field photographs, key/possession status, known liens or claims, and the next required action. Required Skills & Qualifications: 3+ years of U.S. residential property-management experience. Direct experience in Accounts Receivable, delinquency, and collections. Strong experience reading, reviewing, and reconciling resident ledgers. Experience administering late notices and collection workflows. Experience managing Community Guideline and/or lease-compliance cases. Familiarity with U.S. eviction workflow administration. Experience coordinating with attorneys or legal departments. Experience with move-out and possession administration. Strong experience with Rent Manager, the company’s CRM/property-management software, is highly preferred, particularly with Resident Ledgers, AR/Collections, charges and payments, resident notes and history, tasks and queues, documents and notices, attachments, workflows, automation, reporting, resident communications, move-outs, legal/compliance tracking, and dashboards. Experience building or improving Rent Manager workflows, automated task sequences, and collection/compliance queues is highly desirable. Excellent spoken and written English. Exceptional attention to legal dates, deadlines, resident records, and supporting documentation. Ability to conduct difficult resident conversations professionally. Strong emotional discipline, judgment, and professionalism. Ability to follow standardized procedures accurately without improvising or deviating from approved processes. title: Full-Time Video Editor – Direct Response / Meta Ads
job_title: Full-Time Video Editor – Direct Response / Meta Ads
description: We’re looking for a full-time Video Editor to join our creative team and produce high-performing direct-response video ads for Meta/Facebook and Instagram. This is not a traditional video editing position. We are not looking for someone who simply knows Premiere Pro, CapCut, or After Effects. We are looking for an editor who understands advertising psychology, viewer retention, pacing, visual storytelling, and performance creative. You need to understand how to take a script and turn it into an advertisement that keeps someone watching long enough to eventually purchase. What You’ll Be Responsible For You will receive scripts, hooks, creative direction, product assets, customer research, and reference advertisements. Your job is to turn those materials into finished direct-response advertisements. You should understand: What type of footage belongs in each section of a script How visuals should reinforce what the voiceover is saying When a visual should demonstrate the problem When a visual should demonstrate the desired outcome When product footage should appear When customer-style footage is more effective than polished brand footage How long each clip should remain on screen When visual changes are necessary to prevent attention from dropping How to create pattern interrupts without making the advertisement chaotic How to visually build curiosity How to maintain momentum through longer advertisements How to use subtitles, text overlays, screenshots, reviews, graphics, zooms, crops, transitions, and sound effects appropriately How to make a 2–3 minute advertisement continue feeling engaging throughout We do not want editors who simply place random stock footage over a voiceover. Every clip should have a reason for being there. This Is Performance Creative Our advertisements are not created randomly. Each script and creative batch is developed around specific variables such as: Customer avatar Market awareness level Market sophistication Specific customer problem Core desire Advertising angle Hook Unique mechanism Customer objections Proof Emotional journey Creative format Specific variable being tested As the editor, you need to understand the strategy behind the script so the visuals support it properly. For example, if a section of the script is designed to create skepticism, curiosity, authority, urgency, or emotional tension, the footage and editing should reinforce that purpose. You should be able to read a script and understand: What is the viewer supposed to feel here? What does the viewer need to see here? What visual would make this claim more believable? Where is attention likely to drop? Do we need a visual change here? Is this clip helping the story or simply filling space? That judgment is extremely important to us. Hooks Are Extremely Important The first few seconds of an advertisement can determine whether the rest of the video ever gets watched. You will regularly receive one main script with multiple hook variations. You should understand how to make each hook feel visually distinct and compelling while transitioning naturally into the same main body of the advertisement. We expect strong judgment around: Opening visuals First-frame selection Pattern interrupts Text placement Curiosity Pacing Visual juxtaposition Product reveals Problem demonstrations Emotional reactions Authority Results-focused openings A weak opening can ruin an otherwise strong advertisement. PERFORMANCE EXPERIENCE IS STRONGLY PREFERRED We are primarily interested in editors who have previous experience producing direct-response advertisements that actually generated sales. If you have worked on ads that scaled significantly, we want to see them. Preference will be given to applicants who can show advertisements they personally edited that achieved: $10,000+ in ad spend while maintaining a 2.0+ ROAS. If you have this experience, include proof showing: The advertisement Spend ROAS Revenue or purchase performance Relevant date range You should also clearly explain what part of the creative you were responsible for. If you have edited high-spend winning ads, that carries significantly more weight with us than a traditional editing reel. What You'll Be Editing The majority of the work will consist of direct-response social advertisements, including formats such as: UGC-style ads Founder/customer stories Testimonial ads Problem/solution ads Advertorial-style videos Authority-based ads Demonstration ads Comparison ads Story-driven advertisements Native-style social ads Longer 2–3 minute direct-response ads Shorter hook variations Iterations of existing winning advertisements Not every advertisement needs to look highly produced. Sometimes the strongest creative may intentionally look like an organic phone video, customer testimonial, news clip, podcast, interview, slideshow, or social post. You need to understand the difference between good editing and over-editing. Finding Footage You will not always be given every clip needed for an advertisement. You should be comfortable sourcing or creating appropriate supporting visuals using: Our branded footage Stock footage Customer-style footage AI-generated images AI-generated video Screenshots Reviews Social media-style content Product footage Graphics Other relevant assets You should be resourceful. If the script talks about something specific, we expect you to figure out what the viewer should see during that section rather than requiring us to select every individual clip for you. AI Tools Experience with AI creative tools is highly valuable. This may include: ChatGPT Sora Higgsfield Veo Kling Runway Midjourney Gemini / Nano Banana ElevenLabs Other AI image/video generation tools You do not need to use every tool listed. We care about your ability to use modern tools to make better advertisements and solve creative problems quickly. Editing Software You may use whichever professional editing software allows you to produce the best work, including: Adobe Premiere Pro After Effects DaVinci Resolve CapCut Final Cut Pro Other professional editing software The software itself does not matter. The quality of the final advertisement does. What We're Looking For You should have: Strong direct-response video editing experience Strong understanding of Meta/Facebook advertising Excellent sense of pacing Strong visual storytelling instincts Understanding of viewer retention Ability to identify strong supporting footage Strong judgment around clip duration Understanding of hooks and pattern interrupts Strong subtitle and text-overlay design Good sound design Strong attention to detail Ability to follow scripts accurately Ability to follow creative briefs Ability to replicate the general editing principles of reference advertisements without simply copying them Ability to work independently Fast turnaround times Reliable communication Ability to take feedback and implement it correctly Ability to produce a consistent volume of advertisements every week Experience editing for DTC/e-commerce brands spending significant amounts on Meta advertising is strongly preferred. What We Do NOT Want Please do not apply if your editing process is essentially: Add voiceover Add random stock clips Add captions Add music Export That is not what we consider direct-response editing. We need someone who thinks about the advertisement scene by scene and understands why each visual is being shown. Attention to Detail Matters Before delivering an advertisement, you should be checking: Spelling Subtitle accuracy Audio levels Music levels Voice clarity Clip resolution Aspect ratio Visual consistency Awkward cuts Repetitive footage Unnecessary dead time Branding Product accuracy Transitions Overall pacing The video should arrive ready to run as a paid advertisement. Position Full-Time / Long-Term We are looking for someone who can become a long-term member of our creative team. We continuously produce and test new advertisements, hooks, creative formats, stories, concepts, and iterations. Editors who demonstrate strong creative judgment and consistently contribute to winning advertisements will have significant room to grow with us. How To Apply Your application should include: Your video editing portfolio At least 3 direct-response advertisements you personally edited Your best-performing advertisements, if available Any proof of advertisements you edited reaching $10,000+ in spend at a 2.0+ ROAS A brief explanation of what YOU were responsible for on those advertisements The editing software you use The AI tools you currently use Your experience editing Meta/Facebook advertisements Please prioritize actual advertisements over cinematic reels, music videos, or traditional corporate editing examples. Shortlisted applicants will be invited to complete a paid trial advertisement. The trial will be used to evaluate your editing quality, visual judgment, pacing, ability to choose appropriate footage, ability to follow direction, attention to detail, and turnaround time.

description: 🏡 **WE’RE HIRING: SOCIAL MEDIA & MARKETING DIRECTOR – REAL ESTATE** **Real estate experience, strong knowledge of the real estate market, and a proactive mindset are highly important for this role.** We’re a fast-growing real estate team looking for a **proactive, creative, and results-driven Social Media & Marketing Director** who understands the real estate industry and knows how to turn marketing into measurable business results. We want someone who understands the **real estate market and the speed of the business**—new listings, open houses, price changes, closings, market updates, buyer and seller lead generation, agent recruiting, and everything in between. ### 💡 WE WANT SOMEONE WHO BRINGS IDEAS TO THE TABLE This is especially important to us. We are **not** looking for someone who simply waits for instructions or completes assigned marketing tasks. We want someone who actively brings **ideas, recommendations, strategies, and new opportunities** to the team. You should be comfortable looking at our current marketing and saying: **“Here’s what we should improve.”** **“Here’s an opportunity we’re missing.”** **“Here’s a campaign we should try next—and here’s why.”** We want someone who can identify opportunities, recommend strategies, develop campaigns, and take ownership of executing those ideas from start to finish. If you think marketing is just making flyers and posting on social media, this role isn’t for you. If you understand that: **Marketing → Attention → Traffic → Leads → Conversions** …keep reading. ### 📱 SOCIAL MEDIA STRATEGY & MANAGEMENT • Lead and manage our social media presence across Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and other relevant platforms • Develop and execute a consistent social media and content strategy • Create content that builds our brand, showcases listings and agents, educates consumers, and generates leads • Proactively identify real estate trends, local market topics, and content opportunities • Create and maintain an organized content calendar • Monitor engagement, reach, traffic, follower growth, and conversions • Recommend new content and campaign strategies based on performance • Assist with paid social campaigns, retargeting, and boosted content • Identify new platforms, formats, and strategies that could expand our reach ### 🌐 DIGITAL & WEBSITE MANAGEMENT • Update and maintain the team website, including properties, landing pages, team information, and market content • Optimize pages for lead capture and user experience • Monitor website traffic and proactively recommend improvements • Handle basic SEO optimization • Manage or coordinate CRM forms, IDX, lead capture tools, and other website integrations • Identify opportunities to improve website traffic and conversion rates ### 🏠 PROPERTY & AGENT MARKETING • Develop marketing campaigns for new listings, open houses, price improvements, Just Listed, Under Contract, and Just Sold properties • Create professional flyers, brochures, social media graphics, postcards, and other marketing materials • Develop creative ideas for promoting listings beyond standard property posts • Market our agents and team—not just our properties • Coordinate and order sign riders, signage, postcards, brochures, and other print materials • Maintain consistent branding across all marketing channels ### 📈 LEAD GENERATION & GROWTH • Develop campaigns designed to generate buyer, seller, renter, landlord, and agent recruiting leads • Drive qualified traffic from social media and digital campaigns to our website and landing pages • Assist with paid advertising, retargeting, and audience development • Track where traffic and leads are coming from • Analyze results and continuously improve campaigns based on performance • Regularly bring new lead-generation ideas and opportunities to the team • Identify areas where we can improve conversion from attention → traffic → leads → clients ### 📧 EMAIL MARKETING • Create and send consistent newsletters and marketing campaigns • Develop campaigns for past clients, prospects, active leads, our database, and real estate agent recruiting • Write engaging content featuring market updates, listings, real estate education, and team news • Build, segment, and maintain email lists • Track open rates, click-through rates, responses, and conversions • Test and improve subject lines, messaging, content, and calls to action • Propose new email campaigns based on opportunities within our database ### ⚙️ MARKETING OPERATIONS • Own marketing timelines for new listings and campaigns • Coordinate marketing vendors and maintain marketing inventory • Support agent recruiting campaigns through digital, social, and email marketing • Keep projects organized and ensure deadlines are consistently met • Identify opportunities and bring new marketing ideas to the team • Take ownership of marketing projects from concept through execution and performance review ### 🎯 WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR Strong candidates should have: • **Previous real estate marketing or social media experience** • **Strong knowledge and understanding of the real estate market** • Experience marketing real estate listings, agents, teams, or brokerages • A **proactive mindset—you see opportunities and take initiative instead of waiting for instructions** • Ability to regularly bring **new ideas, suggestions, strategies, and solutions** to the team • Strong understanding of social media strategy, content creation, and audience growth • Experience with Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or similar design tools • Experience managing or editing websites using WordPress, Squarespace, or similar platforms • Experience with email marketing platforms such as Mailchimp, Constant Contact, or similar tools • Working knowledge of SEO, lead generation, digital advertising, and analytics • Ability to understand marketing performance beyond likes and followers • Excellent organization and project-management skills • Ability to manage multiple listings, campaigns, deadlines, and priorities simultaneously • Strong written communication and attention to detail • Ability to work independently while collaborating with agents and leadership ### ⭐ WHAT WILL MAKE YOU STAND OUT • Hands-on experience marketing for a **real estate team, brokerage, or successful real estate agent** • Strong understanding of how buyers, sellers, renters, and homeowners engage with real estate content • A track record of bringing new marketing ideas and turning them into successful campaigns • Experience generating buyer and seller leads through social media and digital marketing • Experience with Meta Ads, retargeting, and audience development • Experience with real estate CRMs and IDX websites • Strong portfolio of real estate social media, property, and branding campaigns • Experience creating short-form video, Reels, and other video-first content • Experience with agent recruiting campaigns • Ability to analyze marketing data and turn it into actionable recommendations • Ability to spot opportunities and say, **“Here’s what I think we should do next—and here’s why.”** ### 📊 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE This position will be measured by results, including: • Increased qualified website traffic • Consistent social media growth and meaningful engagement • Increased inbound buyer, seller, and recruiting leads • Strong and consistent brand presence • High-quality listing marketing delivered quickly and on schedule • Consistent email campaigns with improving open and click-through rates • Increased traffic and conversions from digital campaigns • New marketing strategies and ideas being regularly introduced and tested • Continuous improvement based on marketing performance and analytics ### 🚀 THE PERSON WE WANT We want this person to become the **marketing expert on our team**—someone who understands real estate, understands our goals, and is constantly thinking about what we should be doing next. You won't just be asked: **“Can you make this?”** We also expect you to come to us and say: **“Here’s an idea.”** **“Here’s what I noticed.”** **“Here’s what we can improve.”** **“Here’s what our competitors are doing.”** **“Here’s what I recommend we do next.”** If you understand real estate, know how to build attention online, can turn that attention into leads, and are excited about **owning and improving the marketing direction of a growing real estate team**, we’d like to hear from you.

title: Real Estate Photo Editor
description: Full-Time In-House Real Estate Photo Editor — Individual Applicants Only Boardwalk Media Group is an established real estate media company based in Orange County, California. We photograph approximately 60 properties per month and are looking for one talented photo editor to join our team in a stable, long-term, full-time position. This is not a freelance overflow project. We want to build a lasting working relationship with one editor who will learn our style, maintain consistency across every property, and take pride in the final product. Important: No Agencies or Teams This position is exclusively for an individual editor. We are not accepting applications from: * Editing agencies * Editing teams * Account managers or brokers * Applicants who plan to subcontract or delegate the work * Applicants sharing an OnlineJobs.ph profile with another person The person we interview must be the person who personally completes every part of our editing work. Our files may not be downloaded, shared, or sent to anyone else for any reason. Responsibilities You will be responsible for: * Editing bracketed and flambient real estate photographs * Blending ambient and flash exposures naturally * Performing clean, realistic window pulls * Correcting white balance and mixed-light color casts * Maintaining consistent wall and room colors throughout an entire property * Straightening vertical and horizontal lines * Producing natural, accurate, high-end results without an artificial HDR appearance * Removing minor distracting objects when requested * Editing exterior, aerial, twilight, and detail photographs * Creating virtual twilight images when requested * Reviewing completed images for quality and consistency * Following Boardwalk Media Group’s editing standards * Completing revisions promptly when necessary * Organizing, exporting, and uploading completed files * Communicating clearly with our project coordinator and photographers * Meeting daily turnaround deadlines As you grow into the position, additional responsibilities may include final quality control and preparing completed jobs for client delivery. Required Skills You should have: * Strong Adobe Photoshop skills * Experience with layers, masks, actions, blending modes, and manual selections * Experience editing real estate, architectural, interior, or similarly complex photographs * A strong understanding of color correction and white balance * The ability to make multiple rooms within the same property look consistent * Careful attention to small details * Reliable internet and a computer capable of processing large RAW and Photoshop files * Good written English * The ability to accept feedback and reproduce a specific editing style consistently * The ability to work independently without passing assignments to anyone else Experience with Adobe Lightroom, Camera Raw, Dropbox, Google Drive, and real estate delivery platforms is helpful. What We Value We are not simply looking for the fastest editor. We care about: * Consistency from one image to the next * Accurate colors * Natural-looking windows * Clean flash blending * Reliability * Honest communication * Coachability * Attention to detail * A genuine interest in becoming part of one company long-term We will provide examples, feedback, and training on our preferred style. However, applicants should already have solid Photoshop fundamentals. Schedule and Availability This is intended to become a full-time, long-term position. You must be consistently available during the agreed-upon working schedule and able to meet next-business-day delivery deadlines. You may have personal projects or clients outside your scheduled working hours, but you may not perform other client work during the hours paid for by Boardwalk Media Group. You may never delegate Boardwalk work to another editor—even if you are sick, unavailable, or experiencing a heavy workload. If a problem occurs, you must communicate directly with us so we can make other arrangements. Hiring Process Shortlisted applicants will complete the following process: 1. A live video interview 2. A live Photoshop screen-sharing exercise 3. A small paid take-home editing test 4. A paid probationary period with gradually increasing volume During the interview, you will be asked to share your screen, open Photoshop, and explain your editing process. You may also be asked to show layered PSD files from previous work when permitted by your former clients. The quality of your live editing exercise must be consistent with the quality of your portfolio and take-home test. How to Apply Please begin your application with the exact words: I AM THE EDITOR Then answer every question below: 1. How many years have you personally edited photographs? 2. What types of photography have you edited? 3. How much real estate or architectural editing experience do you have? 4. How many real estate images can you personally edit in one working day? 5. How many clients are you currently editing for? 6. Does anyone ever assist you with downloading, blending, masking, retouching, quality control, exporting, or uploading your work? 7. If you become sick or overloaded, what do you normally do with your clients’ assignments? 8. Are you personally the owner and only user of your OnlineJobs.ph profile? 9. Are you comfortable completing a live Photoshop editing exercise while sharing your screen? 10. Are you looking for freelance projects or a stable full-time position with one company? 11. What computer, monitor, internet connection, and version of Photoshop do you use? 12. What is your expected monthly salary for a full-time position? 13. What working hours are you available in Philippine time? 14. When would you be available to begin? Please also include: * A link to your real estate or architectural photography portfolio * Three complete property examples, if available—not only your best individual images * Before-and-after examples * A screenshot of one of your layered Photoshop files * A short video introducing yourself and explaining your normal editing process Please do not send work belonging to another editor, employer, or team and represent it as your own. Do not complete an unpaid sample edit. Applicants selected for the take-home test will receive test files directly from us and will be paid for completing the assignment. Confidentiality and Personal-Work Requirement The selected applicant will sign an agreement requiring that: * All editing is personally performed by the hired editor * No work is subcontracted or delegated * Company and client files remain confidential * Files are never shared with another person * Company images are deleted from personal storage according to our file-retention policy * Client names, property information, workflows, presets, and pricing remain confidential Unauthorized sharing or subcontracting of our work will result in immediate termination. If you are a skilled individual editor who wants consistent work, clear expectations, constructive feedback, and the opportunity to grow with an established company, we would like to hear from you.

Develop working team leads so routine operations do not depend on one person. Address complaints promptly, escalate account risks and follow issues through to resolution. Coordinate operational onboarding, including contacts, access, workflow discovery, SOPs, team training and readiness checks. Maintain a clear record of client commitments and delivery deadlines. Process improvement and automation Identify repetitive work that can be standardized or automated. Provide the technology team with clear requirements, examples and acceptance criteria. Validate automation against real workflows and help agents adopt it. Maintain current records in DA’s operations platform. Follow company and client privacy, security and patient-data handling requirements. The technology team owns software development and technical fixes. Mandatory qualifications At least three years of hands-on US dental billing/RCM experience, covering multiple stages of the revenue cycle. Ability to work directly inside the PMS to review ledgers, post payments and adjustments, manage claims, investigate discrepancies and verify corrections. Clear spoken and written English, with confidence handling US customer calls and escalations. Consistent availability for the agreed US Eastern night shift, including seasonal daylight-saving changes. Reliable internet, backup connectivity and a private, secure workspace. Medical billing, general healthcare BPO or customer-service experience alone will not qualify. US dental RCM, hands-on dental PMS experience and payment-posting expertise are mandatory. Experience supporting multiple practices or a DSO and working across multiple PMS platforms is preferred. How success will be measured Payment-posting accuracy and reconciliation completeness. Verification and claims turnaround-time compliance. Timely follow-up on rejected, denied and unpaid claims. Reduction in aged AR, preventable errors and rework. description: MSP Telecom & IT Sales Operations Coordinator We are an established Managed Service Provider (MSP) seeking a highly organized, proactive, personable, and detail-oriented Telecom & IT Sales Operations Coordinator. We need someone who takes ownership, thinks critically, and gets things done — not someone who waits for instructions or simply reports that they are “still waiting.” Key Responsibilities Telecom & IT Orders / Deal Registration - Submit telecom and IT deal registrations and customer orders through carrier, vendor, distributor, and partner portals. - Process orders with 100% precision — accuracy is non-negotiable. - Verify pricing, products/services, customer information, service addresses, documentation, attribution, and all order details before submission. - Track orders through provisioning, activation, shipment, installation, or implementation. - Maintain accurate CRM, spreadsheets, portals, and sales records. - Coordinate quotes, contracts, approvals, documentation, and other requirements. Proactive Follow-Up & Problem Solving - Proactively communicate with Channel Managers, agents, customers, carriers, vendors, and distributors. - Regularly reach out to agents and Channel Managers for deal updates. - Identify gates and blockers preventing opportunities or orders from progressing. - Determine what information or action is needed and proactively get it. - Email, call, message, follow up again, or find another appropriate contact when necessary. - Maintain clear next actions, owners, and follow-up dates. - Make logical operational determinations independently when appropriate. - Escalate only when a genuine management decision is required. We don't want: “I'm still waiting for them.” We want: “Here is what's blocking us, here is what I've already done, and here is the next action.” Commissions & Agent Administration - Compile carrier/vendor commission and residual reports. - Reconcile commissions against customers, orders, activations, and agents. - Determine which agents should be paid according to established compensation plans. - Prepare organized commission payout reports. - Track paid, pending, missing, disputed, or incorrect commissions. - Investigate discrepancies and proactively obtain whatever information is needed to resolve them. Management Reporting You must be able to take a lot of information and make it easy for management to understand quickly. - Prepare concise daily/weekly sales and operations reports. - Highlight what changed, what matters, what's blocked, and what needs attention. - Clearly identify next actions, owners, deadlines, and recommended actions. - Create clean, easy-to-read spreadsheets, trackers, summaries, and reports. - Turn complicated information into simple, actionable information instead of dumping raw data on management. - Write clear professional emails and summaries independently. You must be able to think, analyze, write, and summarize independently without relying on AI to do your work. AI can be a tool, but it cannot replace your own judgment, understanding, writing ability, or critical thinking. Light Sales Development This is not a high-pressure sales position, but you must be comfortable communicating with prospects. - Follow up with new and existing MSP, IT, telecom, wireless, connectivity, cloud, and cybersecurity leads. - Conduct light outbound outreach and follow-up. - Build rapport and understand basic customer needs. - Schedule qualified appointments for salespeople or Channel Managers. - Maintain communication with prospects, referrals, and partner-generated opportunities. - Make sure good leads don't disappear because nobody followed up. Personality Matters We need someone who is naturally: - Friendly, warm, approachable, and professional - Socially aware and able to read the room - Comfortable communicating with customers, agents, vendors, technical people, and executives - Persistent without being abrasive or annoying - Able to adjust their communication style depending on the person and situation - Confident and personable on the phone - A strong written communicator - Good at building and maintaining relationships You should know when to send a friendly reminder, when to call, when to push harder, when to listen, and when to find another route. Be relentless about the outcome while remaining pleasant throughout the process. What We're Looking For The ideal candidate is: - Extremely organized and detail-oriented - Proactive, resourceful, and accountable - A strong critical thinker and problem solver - Comfortable taking initiative without constant direction - Able to make logical operational determinations independently - Excellent at persistent follow-up - Able to identify blockers, dependencies, missing information, and next actions - Capable of managing many deals, orders, agents, vendors, and communications simultaneously - Strong with spreadsheets, CRM systems, email, and online portals - Able to turn complex information into clear action items - Comfortable with light sales development and appointment setting - Personally accountable for the accuracy of their work Experience with MSPs, IT services, telecom, wireless, carrier services, technology distributors, VAR/channel sales, order provisioning, deal registration, commission reconciliation, CRM, or B2B sales operations is highly preferred. What Success Looks Like At any time, you should be able to tell management: What's moving? What's blocked and why? Who are we waiting on? What have you already done about it? What's the next action and who owns it? Which orders need attention? Which agents need to be paid? Which leads need follow-up? What actually requires management's attention? Our Standard If information is missing — get it. If something is blocked — work to unblock it. If someone isn't responding — follow up intelligently and find another path. If an order is submitted — make sure it's 100% correct. If numbers don't reconcile — investigate them. If a lead needs follow-up — follow up. If management needs to make a decision — bring the facts, options, and your recommended action. We are looking for someone who combines precision, initiative, critical thinking, organization, persistence, warmth, social intelligence, and common sense — and takes genuine ownership of getting the job done.

Our history shows the exact failure you're hired to prevent: reps sending 40-60 outreaches a week, reporting "interested projects," and producing no decision-maker conversations and no calls. You own the conversion at every stage: A. Positive reply ? meaningful advancement within 5 business days. That means a decision-maker conversation, a Telegram group or direct thread with the right person, or a concrete scheduled next step toward a call. If none occurs, the prospect is recycled or closed out of active pipeline. Claimed interest that never advances counts as nothing. B. Every live opportunity has one owner, one next action, one deadline. C. Any opportunity untouched for 5 business days gets a decision: advance, recycle, or close. Nothing sits in "waiting." D. "Calendly shared" is not a completed task. No booking within 2 business days means follow-up happens, and the prospect is told to confirm the booking with both you and the rep. E. If significant outreach produces no qualified calls, you identify the failure point (targets, contacts, messaging, channel, follow-up, or rep) and launch a new test within 24 hours. The same broken approach never runs for multiple weeks. 5. Pipeline control. One accurate source of truth: target, category, tier, contact and decision-maker status, owner, every touch, stage, next action, deadline, call status. Duplicate outreach prevented. All partner groups remain accessible to GMI even if a rep leaves. 6. Founder handoff. Before a call goes on the founder's calendar: a short brief covering who they are, why they're qualified, why LP Bonds fit, what interest they expressed, who d ---------- , and the desired outcome. No Calendly shared before the qualification gate is complete. 7. Reporting and escalation. Every Friday YOU post one consolidated report: outreach sent, positive replies, qualified conversations, groups created, calls booked, calls held, conversion at each stage, per-rep results, stalled deals, next week's tests. Exact numbers and names, no narratives. Chasing reps for their numbers is your job, done before Friday, never visible to the founder. If the week is heading to zero qualified calls, you tell the founder THAT DAY with the likely cause, the numbers, the fix being launched, and when results should show. Bad news early is rewarded. Bad news buried is a dealbreaker. Time allocation A. 50%+ on outreach, follow-up, and appointment conversion B. Up to 25% managing and recruiting reps C. Up to 25% research, reporting, and admin Building internal tools, assigning books, refining meeting formats, and polishing trackers do not count toward anything. If the team is below target, your personal outreach time goes up. First 30 days (paid trial) Day 3: Full audit of every rep and the current pipeline. Immediate correction plan presented. Day 7: Clean pipeline and reporting system live. 100+ prioritized qualified targets. Every rep assigned accounts and numbers. Two outreach tests launched. Your personal outreach started. Day 14: 2+ qualified appointments held. Measurable conversion at each funnel stage. Non-performers cut or on a final clock. Zero held appointments by Day 14 triggers an immediate role review. Day 30 minimum: 6 qualified appointments held, 2+ in the final week, clean pipeline, producing rep core. Target: 8-10 held, exiting at a 3-5/week pace. Base: $10/hr, up to 20 hrs/week B. $100 for every qualified appointment held that you personally booked C. $30 override for every qualified appointment held that your reps booked Partnership revenue, two lanes: D. Partnerships YOU originated: you earn the full rep-tier package: 25% of upgrade fees for the first 90 days after go-live, then 10% through month 12, plus the bond bonus ladder (+$500 at $10K minted, +$1,000 at $20K, +$5,000 at $100K and every $100K after, cumulative, no ceiling). E. Partnerships your REPS originated: you earn an override equal to 20% of your rep's commission payouts, paid by GMI on top of their commission, never deducted from them, plus $250 per partnership once $2,500 in cumulative LP Bond value has been minted in that partner's pools (USD value at time of mint, verified on-chain). Every partnership has exactly one originator of record in our tracker, so lanes never stack on the same deal. F, Additional bonuses possible for exceptional strategic partnerships G. No cap on any of the above. One appointment bonus per call ($100 personal OR $30 override, not both) H. Appointment bonuses paid after the call happens and the founder confirms it met the standard I.
